### Summary

Install stackgres operator 1.3.1 in clean K8s (EKS v1.21) and start a new postgres cluster. The first leader/replica pods start successfully, however, the second replica doesn't and crashes after all.

<!--(Summarize the bug encountered concisely)-->

### Current Behaviour

The second replica never gets `running` state when checking the following command.
```
bash-4.4$ patronictl list

| Member                          | Host               | Role    | State        | TL | Lag in MB |
+ Cluster: xxx-pgc-sgcluster (xxx)                    -----------+--------------+----+-----------+
| xxx-pgc-sgcluster-0             | xxx:7433           | Leader  | running      |  1 |           |
| xxx-pgc-sgcluster-1             | xxx:7433           | Replica | running      |  1 |         0 |
| xxx-pgc-sgcluster-2             | xxx:7433           | Replica | start failed |    |   unknown |
+---------------------------------+--------------------+---------+--------------+----+-----------+
```

[DISCUSSION]
[teoincontatto]: The patroni log states:

```
2022-09-23 09:36:36 UTC [26400]: db=,user=,app=,client= LOG:  database system was interrupted while in recovery at log time 2022-09-23 09:24:46 UTC
2022-09-23 09:36:36 UTC [26400]: db=,user=,app=,client= HINT:  If this has occurred more than once some data might be corrupted and you might need to choose an earlier recovery target.
2022-09-23 09:36:36,668 INFO: postmaster pid=26399
```

Despite the hint suggestion about data possibly being corrupted I think the cause may be another. In particular the patroni container has `1Gi` of memory and that may be too low. Thus the OOM killer may be the responsible of killing postgres process. Since the postgres process is a subprocess of patroni the latter restart postgres and no evidence of the OOM killer remains other than the logs in the node and tracking the exit code of the process (process exit code is 137 when OOM killer kills it). Since I do not know how to get those logs and seems there is no way to get exit code from an unrelated process I suggest to try to increase the memory and delete the failing Pod to see if the error goes away.

[teoincontatto]: Hello @zugao_vshn,

The STS restart may be slow due to the fact that it requires to download the new image (but image get cached so this may be an issue for the first cluster only), install all the extensions binaries for the new version (this is not cached unless you have the extensions cache enabled in the helm chart), perform the upgrade (this may take some time that depends on the size of the data) and finally reset the patroni status.

Do you use many or big (in disk size) extensions? If that is the case having a local extensions cache would help speed up that part. There is a way to build an image with the [build-offline-extensions.sh](https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/blob/main/stackgres-k8s/install/helm/build-offline-extensions.sh) script.
Do you have huge data that requires time to perform the upgrade? If that is the case, performing a backup, testing it and then perform the major version upgrade using `links` would make it much faster.

Issue:
Improve operator performance and responsiveness
### Problem to solve

Current responsiveness of the implementation of the reconciliation cycle was not an issue at the beginning of the project where the number of instances handled by StackGres was not enough big in order to cause a slow response of the operator to changes.

This causes operator performance issues, noticeable by big delays between change in resource and it being applied, manual SgBackups being stuck for a long time.

### Further details

When a user has more than, say, 1500 StackGres resources in the cluster the operator seems to be unable to keep up:

- Manually created SgBackups take a long time before being acknowledged and patched by the operator
- SgBackups stay in Pending for a long time
- The stackgres-operator pod frequently restarts because the liveness probe fails (when executed manually we get status `UP`)

### Proposal

Any of these options should help towards the goal:

- Make the operator deployment scalable so replicas can all work towards the same goal
- Employ pagination when requesting resources from the Kube API
- Increase request timeouts or make them configurable + documented
- Make certain calls asynchronous so the liveness probe goes through while the operator is executing a big query

### Implementation plan

We want to make the operator as responsive as possible by improving its implementation in the following areas:

- The reconciliation cycle of each custom resource should be multi-threaded.
- When a reconciliation cycle fails a new reconciliation cycle should be scheduled ASAP with an exponential back-off in case the failure persist.
- Reconciliation cycle triggered by a failure or an event should take precedence over a periodic reconciliation cycle so that the operator may respond

### Testing

There is a risk of increased complexity, but the value increase is in my opinion very much worth it as it becomes a lot more scalable.

## Acceptance Criteria

The operator still performs while managing a large amount of resources.

- [ ] Create an E2E test (not to be run in the CI/CD e2e test suite) in order to compare current implementation with the new implementation in a scenario with a large number of custom resources
- [ ] Test
- [ ] Document where needed

[teoincontatto]: Hello @zugao_vshn, we introduced an (experimental) thread pool in 1.15.1 (disabled by default on 1.15.2). You may configure it with the following env vars:

* `RECONCILIATION_ENABLE_THREAD_POOL`: When `true`enables the thread pool
* `RECONCILIATION_THREADS`: Number of threads (by default max(1, CPUs / 2))
* `RECONCILIATION_LOW_PRIORITY_THREADS`: When set creates a separate pool for low priority reconciliation (those that are executed each `RECONCILIATION_PERIOD` seconds) with the specified number of threads (less than `RECONCILIATION_THREADS`) 
* `RECONCILIATION_PRIORITY_TIMEOUT`: When set specify the milliseconds after which a pending reconciliation will gain more priority over newer pending reconciliations.

You may play with those env vars to improve performance (by setting `--set-string developer.extraEnv.<env name>=<env value>` in the helm chart or in the `Subscription.spec.config.env` section).

Also, in ~"target_version::1.16.0" we will include a change (introduced in ~"target_version::1.16.0-rc3"  that will be shipped this week) for clusters that uses Kubernetes as the patroni DCS (99% of the cases) so that Kubernetes API is used instead of the `patronictl` command (that is python and requires to spawn a separate process) is not used in the reconciliation cycle that should be an important improvement for performances.

### Summary

After upgrading the Stackgras operator to v1.13.0 we're not able to perform major Postgres upgrades anymore.

The actual `major-version-upgrade` init container runs successfully, all the logs look fine as well and it returns a 0 response code.
The issue happens somewhere in the patroni container after startup, right after all init containers have been finished.

The patroni container tries to create a Kubernetes `endpoint`, which isn't allowed by its `serviceaccount` and `role`.
See logs below. The major upgrade job notices an error and fails, leaving the Postgres cluster in some in-between state with only 1 replica instead of 2. If you increase the replica's afterwards, they fail to become a patroni cluster because they have a different cluster id.

So after `major-version-upgrade` init container successfully finishes, the patroni container logs the error and the major upgrade job stops, like this:
```
Major version upgrade completed successfully, removing old data from instance test-postgres-0

...

+ '[' test-postgres-0 '!=' '' ']'
+ echo 'FAILURE=major version upgrade failed. Please check pod test-postgres-0 logs for more info'
FAILURE=major version upgrade failed. Please check pod test-postgres-0 logs for more info
```

I noticed that this error also appears if you use, for example, version v1.10.0 of the Stackgres operator.
Only the major upgrade job ignores the same error (create endpoint) and continues with its tasks, finalising the major upgrade.

The error itself makes sense though, if you look at the `test-postgres-patroni` role. It doesn't have a `create` verb for the `endpoints` resource. It does however has this for the `endpoints/restricted`, which historically has been added to make Stackgres work with Openshift (looking at the issues here on Gitlab).

### Current Behaviour 

Create endpoint by patroni container fails as well but major upgrade job continues.

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy Stackgres v1.13.0 to Kubernetes.
2. Deploy a SGCluster with Postgres 15.x.
3. create PGConfig for Postgres 16
4. major upgrade your Postgres cluster from 15.x to 16.x

### Expected Behaviour

Major upgrade finishes successful.

### Possible Solution

1. patch the endpoint instead of (re?)create it
2. ignores the error during a major upgrade, just like. with stackgres operator v1.10.0
3. add `create` to the `endpoint` resource in the patroni role

### Environment

- StackGres version: 1.13.0
- Kubernetes version: 1.28
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: Rancher Kubernetes

Issue:
Allow to override SGInstanceProfile, SGPostgresConfig and SGPoolingConfig
SGInstanceProfile, SGPostgresConfig and SGPoolingConfig CRDs are meant to be reused across potentially multiple clusters.
What they are now are references. This means that if two clusters reference the same CR, they are "importing" the same configuration. This is good, but leaves the door open to the question: Which resources are referencing that configuration and will be affected by any modification to it? We are not sure if this is exactly what users wants.

Moreover, there's the problem of "I want this configuration but just slightly modify this given setting", which forces you to create a copy and modify.

Both issues can be solved if we allow these CRDs to be treated as templates that can be overridden. It's kind of the same thing but with a small difference:

SGInstanceProfile, SGPostgresConfig and SGPoolingConfig CRs will be templates, meaning that they're not the real configurations being imported in the SGCluster. For example, a template will not be the source of thrust until it get merged with the configuration parameters present in the SGCluster.

Once we have switched to this concept of templating, it's trivial to allow the user to "override" any value in any configuration. This could be done from the main SGCluster configuration, and would be a very convenient way of overriding values. With this principle in mind we would make it trivial to use defaults for everything and do all the small overrides from the main resource.

## Implementation plan

This is the initial proposal of the models changes:

```yaml
kind: SGCluster
spec:
  sgInstanceProfile: <string> # This field will become optional
  pods:
    resources: 
      containers: # Resources configuration to be merged with the specified container on top of SGInstanceProfile referenced by `sgInstanceProfile` field if specified.
        <string>: # The name of the container that can be prefixed with `backup.` or `dbops.` to indicate they belong to, respectively, an SGBackup or SGDbOps associated to the SGCluster
          <object> # This section will replace completely the container sections specified in SGInstanceProfile referenced by `sgInstanceProfile` field if specified. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.30/#resourcerequirements-v1-core
      initContainers: # Resources configuration to be merged with the specified init container on top of SGInstanceProfile referenced by `sgInstanceProfile` field if specified.
        <string>: # The name of the init container that can be prefixed with `backup.` or `dbops.` to indicate they belong to, respectively, an SGBackup or SGDbOps associated to the SGCluster
          <object> # This section will replace completely the init container sections specified in SGInstanceProfile referenced by `sgInstanceProfile` field. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.30/#resourcerequirements-v1-core
  configurations:
    sgPostgresConfig: <string> # This field will become optional
    postgres:
      postgresql.conf: # Postgres configuration. The final configuration is obtained by applying the Postgres defaults of the current operator version merged on top of this configuration and then, if specified, merged on top of SGPostgresConfig referenced by `sgPostgresConfig` field
        <string>: <string>
    sgPoolingConfig: <string> # This field will become optional
    pooling:
      pgBouncer:
        pgbouncer.ini # PgBouncer configuration. The final configuration is obtained by applying the PgBouncer defaults of the current operator version merged on top of this configuration and then, if specified, merged on top of SGPoolingConfig referenced by `sgPoolingConfig` field
          pgbouncer:
            <string>: <string>
          users:
            <string>:
              <string>: <string>

### Summary

After restoring an SGCluster from a snapshot backup if the primary Pod is evicted the Pod never reach back to the Ready status

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an SGCluster of 1 Pod with snapshot backups
2. Create a SGBackup
3. Create another SGCluster of 1 Pod from the SGBackup
4. Restart or just delete the Pod

### Expected Behaviour

After restoring an SGCluster from a snapshot backup if the primary Pod is evicted the Pod should get back to the Ready status

### Possible Solution

The mechanism to restore from a snapshot volume requires to move the `data` folder to `data.backup` to avoid Patroni from trying to perform a crash recovery. Then when patroni execute the restore the folder is renamed back to its previous name. When the Pod is restarted there is no check to avoid the renaming of the `data` folder and, since Patroni state indicate that the data should be there, Patroni fail to start.

[teoincontatto]: > Replace CLUSTER_NAMESPACE, CLUSTER_NAME and POD_NAME environment variables with the actual namespace and name of your SGCluster and the name of the Pod that is not able to become ready

# Fast workaround to make the Pod ready again

To make the Pod start a manual command have to be run in the `patroni` container in order to rename the folder `/var/lib/postgresql/data.backup` to `/var/lib/postgresql/data`.

To check if the folder has the wrong name run the following command:

```
kubectl exec -n "$CLUSTER_NAMESPACE" "$POD_NAME" -c patroni -- ls -l /var/lib/postgresql
```

It should give you an output similar to the following:

```
total 16
drwx--S--- 19 postgres postgres 4096 Dec 20 12:31 data.backup
drwxrwsr-x  3 postgres postgres 4096 Dec 20 12:30 extensions
-rw-------  1 postgres postgres   49 Dec 20 12:31 pgpass
drwxrwsr-x  3 postgres postgres 4096 Dec 20 12:30 relocated
```

Use the following command to rename the folder `data.backup`:

```
kubectl exec -n "$CLUSTER_NAMESPACE" "$POD_NAME" -c patroni -- mv /var/lib/postgresql/data.backup /var/lib/postgresql/data
```

# Workaround to fix the issue

A workaround to fix the issue for an SGCluster that has snapshot backups configured is to patch the templates ConfigMap for `start-patroni.sh` and `create-backup.sh` script. Use the following command:

wget "https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/raw/4455fb8ac19f2049b984135056521f3a6a865b94/stackgres-k8s/src/operator/src/main/resources/templates/start-patroni.sh"

kubectl patch configmap -n "$CLUSTER_NAMESPACE" "$CLUSTER_NAME"-templates --type merge -p '{"data":{"create-backup.sh":'"$(cat create-backup.sh | jq -Rs .)"'}}'
```

Then to avoid the current primary Pod from rename the folder create the file `/var/lib/postgresql/data/.restored_from_volume_snapshot` using the following command:

```
kubectl exec -n "$CLUSTER_NAMESPACE" "$POD_NAME" -c patroni -- touch /var/lib/postgresql/data/.restored_from_volume_snapshot
```

The fast workaround still apply but require user manual intervention so a new hotfix release will be shipped in order to fix this issue definitively.

### Summary

When replication mode is sync or strict-sync major version upgrade breaks.

### Current Behaviour 

The major version upgrade operation Job fail while trying to downscale the cluster to 1 instance with the following error:

```
Error from server (https://stackgres.io/doc/1.14/api/responses/error#constraint-violation): admission webhook "sgcluster.validating-webhook.stackgres.io" denied the request: SGCluster has invalid properties. The total number of instances must be greather than the number of synchronous replicas
```

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an SGCluster with version 15 and replication mode set to sync
2. Create a copy of the SGPostgresConfig for version 16
3. Create a SGDbOps major version upgrade operation targeting the SGCluster and SGPostgresConfig for version 16 created above.

### Expected Behaviour

The SGDbOps perform the major version upgrade operation and restore the replication mode to its previous value.

### Possible Solution

Store the replication mode in the `SGCluster.status.dbOps.majorVersionUpgrade` section and change the replication mode to async before downscaling the cluster instances.

### Environment

- StackGres version: 1.14.3
- Kubernetes version: *
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: *

[DISCUSSION]
[teoincontatto]: # Manual Fix

To revert the operation you will have to perform the following steps (please, replace CLUSTER_NAMESPACE, CLUSTER_NAME with the actual values of your environment):

1. Retrieve the previous postgres version from the SGCluster.status.dbOps.majorVersionUpgrade section:

```
PREVIOUS_POSTGRES_VERSION="$(kubectl get sgcluster -n "$CLUSTER_NAMESPACE" "$CLUSTER_NAME" --template='{{ .status.dbOps.majorVersionUpgrade.sourcePostgresVersion }}')"
```

2. Backup the validating webhook:

```
kubectl get validatingwebhookconfigurations.admissionregistration.k8s.io stackgres-operator -o yaml > stackgres-operator.validatingwebhookconfiguration.yaml
```

3. Remove the validating webhook:

```
kubectl delete validatingwebhookconfigurations.admissionregistration.k8s.io stackgres-operator
```

4. Patch the SGCluster and set the previous postgres version and remove the SGCluster.status.dbOps.majorVersionUpgrade section:

```
kubectl patch sgcluster -n "$CLUSTER_NAMESPACE" "$CLUSTER_NAME" --type merge -p "--- { spec: { postgres: { version: '$PREVIOUS_POSTGRES_VERSION' } }, status: { dbOps: null } }"
```

4. Restore the validating webhook:

```
kubectl create -f stackgres-operator.validatingwebhookconfiguration.yaml
```

5. Delete the cluster Pods (this will disrupt your service):

```
kubectl delete pod -n "$CLUSTER_NAMESPACE" -l "app=StackGresCluster,stackgres.io/cluster-name=$CLUSTER_NAME,stackgres.io/cluster=true"
```

# Workaround

> This only apply if you have `SGCluster.replication.mode` field set to a value different from `async`.

To perform the major version upgrade avoiding the bug you will have to remove the synchronous replication configuration from the SGCluster first and add it back later.

### Problem to solve

Our organization is running an EKS cluster with Calico to avoid using AWS's VPC CNI plugin, so that we can run more pods in the same EC2 instance.

However, running Calico and other operators break the Stackgres operator webhook, as it is listening in already used ports.

This makes it impossible to use Stackgres in this cluster - all requests fail when calling the webhook, such as:

```bash
$ kc delete sgobjectstorage dev-stackgres-backups
Error from server (InternalError): Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook "sgobjectstorage.validating-webhook.stackgres.io": failed to call webhook: Post "https://stackgres.stackgres.svc:443/stackgres/validation/sgobjectstorage?timeout=10s": Address is not allowed
```


### Further details

Calico states this is not their specific limitation, but EKS's.

However, we are running other operators in the same cluster that provide a way to get around this limitation - using `hostNetwork` for operator pods.


### Proposal

Implement `hostNetwork` for operator pods in the Helm chart and the ability to change the port where the operator listens.
Just enabling `hostNetwork` on the operator pod doesn't solve the problem, as the operator itself might be listening on a port that is already in use:

```bash
2025-01-22 22:43:17,618 ERROR [io.qu.ru.Application] (main) One or more of the following ports: 8080,8443 seem to be in use by another process. Quarkus may already be running or one of the ports is used by another application.
```

### Testing

<!-- What risks does this change pose? How might it affect the quality of the product?  -->
If this change is accepted and implemented, the Kubernetes operator will have one more value to add in values.yaml.

However, this will improve the compatibility of Stackgres in certain Kubernetes configurations.

## Acceptance Criteria
<!-- Acceptance Criteria, Definition of Done, describe the expected output -->
Ideally, an optional "`hostNetwork`" entry in `values.yaml` would suffice, as well as way to change the port the operator listens on.


### Links / references

[official calico docs](https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/getting-started/kubernetes/managed-public-cloud/eks#install-eks-with-calico-networking)

[DISCUSSION]
[teoincontatto]: The operator exposes a Service. Would be enough to change the port there or should we also allow to change the actual port used by the operator to listen?

[pedro.farinha]: I'd say both - if the pod exposes the port in `hostNetwork`, it can be already in use.
Having the port changed in the `Service` would also help. It would also to give some flexibility in certain situations.

Issue:
Provide support for encrypted backups

Backups are currently stored in clear. When using a block storage provider, it would be useful to encrypt the backups before transfer. The encryption key could be stored in a secret. If a symmetric key is used, then backups can also be easily restored.

**Acceptance criteria:**

Part1:

- [ ] Create a POC.

Part2:

- [ ] Implement the encription options

[jose_oss_pg]: @jose_oss_pg create UI issue related to dev after the third step.

cc: @ldgarcia

[jose_oss_pg]: @sebawebber thank you! I will create them.

[pmcnamee_symb]: We have a strong interest in this. Currently, we tried GitProtect but our instance is far too large and a complete backup via that product is not feasbile.

I have setup a native (gpg) attempt but this produces another copy of the backup file, and ours happens to be quite large. I also don't know if running the gpg (for about 40 minutes) will impact performance on the server.

[zadjadr]: Please prioritize this issue, if possible. This is a deal-breaker for us.

[teoincontatto]: Since we use [wal-g](https://wal-g.readthedocs.io/) for backups we will be able to easily support encryption via:

* [libsodium](https://doc.libsodium.org/)
* [OpenPGP](https://www.openpgp.org/)

The first just need a secret key while the latter requires an RSA key pair (private and public).

[daurskikh]: Are there plans for supporting cloud providers' server-side encryption?

[teoincontatto]: That's a good point.

We may include also:

* [S3 server-side encryption with AWS KMS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingKMSEncryption.html)
* [GCS Customer Supplied Encryption Key (CSEK) for client-side encryption and decryption](https://cloud.google.com/docs/security/encryption/customer-supplied-encryption-keys)
* OpenPGP with envelope key stored in key management system
* [Yandex Cloud KMS](https://cloud.yandex.com/en/services/kms)

[oivindoh]: @gcannata did you abandon this work? Sodium or PGP support would be such a great feature to be able to throw backups onto cloud vendor object stores!

[ssoloch]: Also interested in this feature.

Considering that WAL-G already supports encryption, I've tried to hack a solution around current operator limitations. With environment variables injected (using gatekeeper as operator doesn't seem to support custom env vars) WAL-G tries to create an encrypted backup but fails... because it's currently built without libsodium support. Likely doing just those two things (compilation with libsodium and a way to inject env variables to proper containers) would be enough to add client-side encryption support. Doing it on backup CR level might require passing necessary env variables from a backup job to WAL-G (it's possible to specify password this way). Not sure about restores, I'm yet to evaluate how those are performed.

Small note about cloud provider's encryption methods: those are all server-side, even S3 SSE-C and mentioned GCS CSEK. While those two protect data at rest from cloud provider's eyes, data in transit is unencrypted **and key is transferred alongside it**. Client-side solution is much better.

[adamcharnock]: I'm also interested in this feature. The lack of it makes using wal-g-based backups very tricky for us (EU GDPR, etc), to the point where we will likely just use daily PVC snapshots instead (thereby sacrificing up-to a whole days worth of data in case of failure).

I can see this issue has been around for a while, but it is now also one of top three StackGres issues on GitLab. If it it would help get this moving, I propose a two-phase development process:

1. First add symmetric encryption using wal-g's libsodium support as it seems most straightforward. Ensure the CRD changes are extensible.
3. Once stable, look at adding additional forms of encryption.

# Example CRD Update

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGCluster
# [...]
spec:
  # [...]
  configurations:
    backups:
    - sgObjectStorage: # name of the referenced SGObjectStorage
      # [...]
      encryption:
        symmetric: # Symmetric encryption, but other kinds supported in future
          secretRef:
            name: secret-name
            key: secret-key
```

The tasks would then be to:

- [ ] Update the CRD definitions
- [ ] Validate the found encryption key
- [ ] Build wal-g with libsodium support
- [ ] Pass `WALG_LIBSODIUM_KEY` to wal-g
- [ ] Update e2e tests to test encrypted backup & restore
- [ ] Update the documentation

I've already done some of this in !1657, although I would need to update it a bit in light of this conversation.

# Can I help?

I could likely find time to work on the above over the next month or two, if there would be interest in that from Stackgres? If so, I would kindly ask for permission to run execute pipelines in your CI system if possible.

Issue:
stackgres-operator helm chart and ArgoCD
Hi there,

I've been using ArgoCD to deploy stackgres operator and have a few false diffs showing against the deployment. Because Argo re-acts to differences in the templated helm resources vs the live manifest running against the kubernetes cluster, these difference cause Argo to show the application as OutOfSync. This is likely also the case for tools like helm diff etc.

I attempted to fix some of the issues in !1566 but realised the problems were slightly deeper than I initially thought. I'm using version 1.9.0 of the helm chart

**SGCluster config includes invalid fields**

As the SGConfig config created by the helm chart simply templates all the non-null helm values into the resource spec, you end up with 2 fields which aren't part of the SGConfig schema, rbac and global. This could be fixed simply like I have in !1566 by omitting those keys, or possibly the template could be more explicit and include only keys which are part of the SGConfig spec.

**SGDbOps CRD nullable = false fields**

Kubernetes seems to omit any keys where nullable == false. This causes the SGDbOps CRD to show a diff in Argo.

![image](/uploads/5212f310e14b83212e46c1727253c2c5/image.png)

The following paths should be removed:

```
spec.versions[0].schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.status.properties.benchmark.properties.pgbench.properties.latency.properties.average.properties.unit.nullable = false
spec.versions[0].schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.status.properties.benchmark.properties.pgbench.properties.latency.properties.standardDeviation.properties.unit.nullable = false
spec.versions[0].schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.status.properties.benchmark.properties.pgbench.properties.transactionsPerSecond.properties.includingConnectionsEstablishing.properties.unit.nullable = false
spec.versions[0].schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.status.properties.benchmark.properties.pgbench.properties.transactionsPerSecond.properties.excludingConnectionsEstablishing.properties.unit.nullable = false
```

**Validating and Mutating webhooks are re-written by the operator**

The validating and mutating webhooks are re-written by the operator as part of it's startup process. There are a couple of thing causing a diff between the templated helm manifest and the operator managed config:

* The operator is removing some of the webhook items
* The operator re-writes the webhook keys in a different order than the helm chart
* The helm-chart specifies an empty caBundle option (`Cg==`), which the operator pod updates with the cluster caBundle.

To fix, the following needs to be done:

* Align operator and helm chart for both validating and mutating webhook resources
  * Ensure correct ordering of items and the webhook array, as well as key ordering.
  * Remove any unused options from the helm manifest
  * Ensure plural settings match between helm and operator (e.g. `sgscript.mutating-webhook.stackgres.io` vs `sgscripts.mutating-webhook.stackgres.io`)
* If no caBundle is specified, omit the `webhooks[].clientConfig.caBundle` key entirely, this will cause Argo not to track changes against it and attempt to revert the operator updates back to the empty bundle (`Cg==`). See !1566 and the [ECK operator helm chart](https://github.com/elastic/cloud-on-k8s/blob/main/deploy/eck-operator/templates/webhook.yaml#L46) for how they acheive that.

[DISCUSSION]
[anguswilliams]: For anyone running into similar issues with Argo, I've worked around it by using the following [Argo diff](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/diffing/#application-level-configuration) customisation settings on the stackgres-operator Application resource

```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: stackgres-operator
spec:
...
  ignoreDifferences:
    - group: admissionregistration.k8s.io
      kind: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
      jsonPointers:
        - /webhooks
    - group: admissionregistration.k8s.io
      kind: MutatingWebhookConfiguration
      jsonPointers:
        - /webhooks
    - group: stackgres.io
      kind: SGConfig
      jsonPointers:
        - /spec/global
        - /spec/rbac
    - group: apiextensions.k8s.io
      kind: CustomResourceDefinition
      jqPathExpressions:
        - '.spec.versions[].schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.status.properties.benchmark.properties.pgbench.properties | .. | select(.nullable? == false)'
```

Issue:
Remove resource existence check from validating webhook
We would like to discuss pros and cons of two approaches related to checking or not if some associated resources of a CR exists in the validating webhook to decide if a change in the approach is needed.

# Current approach

Currently when a CR is created the validating webhook checks if the associated resources exists. For example, for a sgcluster it checks if the configuration CRs exists.

## Pros

* It show immediately what are the missing parts when trying to create a CR.

## Cons

* It difficults installation / restauration procedures since the creation of resources requires a certain order to be followed.

# Alternative approach

Another approach would be to allow creation of any CR even if those associated resources does not exists and rely on operator in order to detect those resources are missing, skipping the reconciliation cycle for that CR and notify with an error event specifying which resources was missing. When the missing resources are created the operator will continue with reconciliation of the CR.

This will also allow to prevent failures due to an associated resource removed accidentally (here we are referring to Secret, ConfigMap, etc. since associated StackGres's CRs deletion is prevented in such cases) and making the reconciliation of a CR inconsistent.

## Pros

* It allow any installation procedure since the creation of CRs does not requires to follow any order.

## Cons

* It does not show immediately what is the problem when trying to create a CR but it will show the problem (similar to what happen when creating a pod resource) in the event associated with that CR.

[DISCUSSION]
[ahachete]: My opinion is to enforce strict checking, at least short-term. I envision not doing it will add noticeable complexity in code, documentation and behaviour.

While it sounds a bit quite inter-intuitive, that's why we provide default configurations. And documentation helps anyway.

This is not necessarily a bad idea, it could work well, but it is not a short-term priority.

[white-hat1]: I'd like support this request as an administrator of several k8s clusters which serve >200 developers and run thousands of deployments (many of these deployments include a local database).
None of standard k8s resources or any 3rd party CDRs we are using are doing such pre-deploy checks because it breaks CI/CD and dramatically complicates deployment process.
Instead, k8s should accept a valid manifest file and will try to create corresponding resources. If dependency is not satisfied - k8s scheduler should try to schedule a resource later. For example, if you describe a secret and a pod (which is mounting this secret) in a single YAML file, you will never see an error from k8s telling you “deploy a secret first, a pod later”
The same way, SGcluster should still be accepted by k8s even if it's configuration is still not available, and it should remain in "Pending" state until the configuration or any other dependency becomes available.

[ahachete]: Hard to disagree :) Let's follow K8s convention here :thumbsup: 

Thanks for the feedback. Adding to `1.0` milestone.

[jose_oss_pg]: @teoincontatto @ahachete @jorsol @gcannata Should we prioritize this issue or keep in the backlog with the current urgency?

[teoincontatto]: I think this is a killer feature for some use cases (Git DevOps) since configurations and instances can not be currently created in parallel or in a different order.

I do not see it as very hard to implement given that we have many E2E tests. Basically the user will not be bothered on creation of an SGCluster about a missing resource (SG* or Secret or ConfigMap) and will receive events about the missing referenced resource later. This is a typical pattern for Kubernetes resources. So I vote to include it sooner than later. But I think I need some quorum from others in order to know if this is wanted or not.

@ahachete Do you think this is a good thing to implement?

[ahachete]: Yes, I agree.

Issue:
Add default resource limits to StackGres (ex: stackgres-collector) components to prevent memory spikes
### Problem to solve

When the "stackgres-collector" is started, it exhibits significant memory spikes. In my cluster, memory usage climbs up to 27GB, which matches the total memory available on my worker node. Upon investigation, I discovered that the default installation of StackGres does not set resource limits (memory and CPU), a critical best practice in Kubernetes to prevent such issues.

**This uncontrolled memory growth leads to two main problems:**

1. Memory usage surges dramatically, potentially leading to instability.
2. Grafana dashboards stop displaying data once the memory spike occurs. Deleting the stackgres-collector pod restores normal memory levels and dashboard functionality.

Thankfully, I was able to identify and mitigate the issue using Grafana. However, it highlights a need for StackGres to implement default resource limits for its components.

### Further details

**Use cases:** Users deploying StackGres may unknowingly encounter memory or CPU resource overuse if resource limits are not explicitly defined.

**Benefits:** Setting default resource limits in StackGres installations would improve out-of-the-box stability and avoid resource contention issues. It also aligns with Kubernetes best practices.

**Goals:**

1. Prevent memory spikes from impacting cluster stability.
2. Ensure continuous functionality of monitoring tools like Grafana.

### Proposal

Update the default StackGres Helm charts or configuration to include reasonable default resource limits for all components, especially the stackgres-collector. The installation guides document these defaults clearly and provide recommendations for users to adjust based on their cluster capacity.

### Testing

- Validate the behavior of the stackgres-collector with default resource limits in different cluster setups.
- Verify that Grafana and other monitoring tools remain functional during heavy usage scenarios.
- Ensure no significant degradation in collector performance due to resource capping.

### Summary

Major version upgrade to Postgres 17 fail with unrecognized configuration parameter "lc_collate"

### Current Behaviour 

The Job fails in the pre-checks phase reporting the following error:

```
++ kubectl exec -n keycloak keycloak-0 -c patroni -- psql -q -t -A -c 'SHOW lc_collate'
ERROR:  unrecognized configuration parameter "lc_collate"
```

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an SGCluster with version 16
2. Create an SGDbOps to perform a majorVersionUpgrade op to version 17

### Expected Behaviour

The Jobs completes successfully

### Possible Solution

Since `lc_collate` setting has been removed in Postgres 16 change the query in `run-major-version-upgrade.sh` so that default locale is retrieved from `pg_database` table instead of from the settings, like the following:

```
SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'lc_collate' UNION ALL SELECT datcollate FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'template1' LIMIT 1;
```

#### Workaround

To workaround this issue execute the following steps (set env vars to actual values):

1. Patch the script that run the major version upgrade:

```
kubectl annotate configmap -n "$CLUSTER_NAMESPACE" "$CLUSTER_NAME"-templates stackgres.io/reconciliation-pause=true

kubectl get configmap -n "$CLUSTER_NAMESPACE" "$CLUSTER_NAME"-templates -o json \
  | sed "s/SHOW lc_collate/SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'lc_collate' UNION ALL SELECT datcollate FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'template1' LIMIT 1/" > /tmp/."$CLUSTER_NAMESPACE"."$CLUSTER_NAME"-templates.configmap.json

kubectl patch configmap -n "$CLUSTER_NAMESPACE" "$CLUSTER_NAME"-templates --type merge --patch-file=/tmp/."$CLUSTER_NAMESPACE"."$CLUSTER_NAME"-templates.configmap.json

rm /tmp/."$CLUSTER_NAMESPACE"."$CLUSTER_NAME"-templates.configmap.json
```

2. Run the major version upgrade SGDbOps and wait for its completion.

3. Allow the scripts to be reocncilied by the operator:

```
kubectl annotate configmap -n "$CLUSTER_NAMESPACE" "$CLUSTER_NAME"-templates stackgres.io/reconciliation-pause-
```

Issue:
Make SGDistributedLogs generate and own an SGCluster
### Problem to solve

Currently an `SGDistributedLogs` custom resource create resources directly to deploy a slightly modified and reduced version of a `SGCluster`. This is not an ideal case for the following reasons:

* An `SGDistributedLogs` can not be monitored using the Web UI and to do so would require to implement the same parts that are already implemented for an `SGCluster`.
* `SGDbOps` can not be applied to an `SGDistirbutedLogs` so that it loses many of the advantages offered by this kind of operations.
* `SGInstanceProfile` or `SGPostgresConfig` can not be changed for an `SGDistributedLogs`. And this could bring problems later if the database for logs requires any exceptional tuning.
* Connection pooling and an `SGPoolingConfig` can not be enabled and configured for an `SGDistributedLogs`.
* `SGBackupConfig` or `SGBackup` can not be applied to an `SGDistirbutedLogs` so that it loses the ability to backup logs if the user want to. So this option is not considered in this case.
* `SGBackup` can not be applied to an `SGDistirbutedLogs` so that it loses many of the advantages offered by this kind of operations.
* Many fields of `SGDistributedLogs` CRD are taken from the `SGCluster` CRD so that this makes the `SGDistributedLogs` implementation mostly a duplication of the code of the implementation for the `SGCluster`, thus not following a [good code practice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coding_best_practices#Reusability).

### Proposal

An `SGDistributedLogs` should generate an `SGCluster` that is owned by the `SGDistributedLogs` together with the a default `SGInstanceProfile` and a `SGPostgresConfig` and a separate Kubernetes Deployment of 1 replicas to host the Fluentd and DistributedLogs Controler containers that will connect to the Postgres instance to store the logs.

In the future we may include the Fluentd instance as a sidecar of the cluster created by the `SGCluster` when #538 will be implemented.

### Testing

This change should not bring any modification to the functionality offered by the `SGDistributedLogs`, instead it will bring additional functionality since already existing functionality for the `SGCluster` will apply to the `SGDistributedLogs`. Existing E2E tests should still be working as a validation for the `SGDistributedLogs`.

Some validation will be added in order to check that some restriction are applied to an `SGCluster` owned by a `SGDistributedLogs`:

* The `.spec.postgresVersions` field must be `12.x`
* The `.spec.postgresExtensions` field must include `timescaledb` extensions with version `1.7.4` and can not be overwritten.

## Acceptance Criteria

Create an `SGDistributedLogs` should not change in functionality.

[teoincontatto]: ## Workaround

The workaround consist in creating a CronJob that will patch the ConfigMap in order to add the missing Pods to the OTEL collector configuration and fix the start script in order to allow a correct reload of the configuration on changes (you may need to adapt the above script if you installed the operator in a different namespace than `stackgres` or with a name different than `stackgres-operator`):

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  namespace: stackgres
  name: stackgres-collector-2926-workaround
spec:
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  schedule: '*/5 * * * *'
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          serviceAccountName: stackgres-operator
          containers:
          - name: concile-collector-configmap
            image: quay.io/ongres/kubectl:v1.28.14-build-6.37
            command:
            - /bin/sh
            - -exc
            - |
              cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/stackgres-collector-config-add-pod-if-missing.jq
              .receivers.prometheus.config.scrape_configs = 
              (
              .receivers.prometheus.config.scrape_configs
              |map(
                if 
                  ((.static_configs|any((.labels.namespace == $namespace) and (.labels.pod|test("^" + $namesuffix + "-[^-]+$")))) 
                  and ((.static_configs|any(.labels.pod == $name))|not))
                then .static_configs = 
                  .static_configs 
                  + [ (
                    .static_configs[0]
                      |.labels.instance =
                        ($podip + ":" + (
                          .labels.instance
                            |sub("^[^:]+:";"")))
                      | .labels.pod = $name
                      | .targets[0] = 
                        ($podip + ":" + (
                          .targets[0]
                          |sub("^[^:]+:";"")))) ] 
                else . end))
              EOF

              cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/start-otel-collector-fix.sh
              #!/bin/sh

              OTEL_COLLECTOR_LAST_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/otel-collector
              CONFIG_PATH="${COLLECTOR_CONFIG_PATH%/*}"

              update_config() {
                rm -Rf "$OTEL_COLLECTOR_LAST_CONFIG_PATH"
                cp -Lr "$CONFIG_PATH" "$OTEL_COLLECTOR_LAST_CONFIG_PATH"
              }

              has_config_changed() {
                for file in $(ls -1 "$CONFIG_PATH")
                do
                  [ "$(cat "$CONFIG_PATH/$file" | md5sum)" \
                    != "$(cat "$OTEL_COLLECTOR_LAST_CONFIG_PATH/$file" | md5sum)" ] \
                    && return || true
                done
                return 1
              }

              run_otel_collector() {
                set -x
                exec otelcol-contrib --config "$COLLECTOR_CONFIG_PATH"
              }

              is_child() {
                local PID="$1"
                grep -q "^PPid:[[:space:]]$$$$" "/proc/$PID/status" 2>/dev/null
              }

              set +x
              PID=
              while true
              do
                if ! is_child "$PID" || has_config_changed
                then
                  if [ -n "$PID" ] && is_child "$PID"
                  then
                    >&2 echo "Reloading otelcol-contrib config"
                    kill -s HUP "$PID" || true
                  else
                    >&2 echo "otelcol-contrib process not found, starting it"
                    run_otel_collector &
                    PID="$!"
                  fi
                  update_config
                fi
                sleep 5
              done
              EOF

              kubectl annotate configmap -n stackgres stackgres-collector --overwrite stackgres.io/reconciliation-pause-
              RESOURCE_VERSION="$(kubectl patch configmap -n stackgres stackgres-collector --type merge -p "{ \"data\": { \"stackgres-collector-2926-workaround\": \"$(date +%s)\" }}" --template '{{ .metadata.resourceVersion }}')"
              kubectl annotate sgconfig -n stackgres stackgres-operator --overwrite stackgres.io/stackgres-collector-2926-workaround="$(date +%s)"
              until [ "$RESOURCE_VERSION" != "$(kubectl get configmap -n stackgres stackgres-collector --template '{{ .metadata.resourceVersion }}')" ]
              do
                sleep 1
              done
              kubectl annotate configmap -n stackgres stackgres-collector --overwrite stackgres.io/reconciliation-pause=true
              kubectl get configmap -n stackgres stackgres-collector -o json | jq -r '.data["config.yaml"]' > /tmp/stackgres-collector-config.yaml
              kubectl get sgcluster -A --template '{{ range .items }}{{ printf "%s %s\n" .metadata.namespace .metadata.name }}{{ end }}' \
                | while read NAMESPACE NAME
                  do
                    kubectl get pod -n "$NAMESPACE" \
                      -l app=StackGresCluster,stackgres.io/cluster=true,stackgres.io/cluster-name="$NAME" \
                      --template '{{ range .items }}{{ printf "%s %s %s\n" .metadata.namespace .metadata.name .status.podIP }}{{ end }}'
                  done \
                | while read NAMESPACE NAME PODIP
                  do
                    yq -y --arg namespace "$NAMESPACE" --arg name "$NAME" --arg namesuffix "${NAME%-*}" --arg podip "$PODIP" \
                      -f /tmp/stackgres-collector-config-add-pod-if-missing.jq /tmp/stackgres-collector-config.yaml > /tmp/stackgres-collector-config.yaml.tmp
                    mv /tmp/stackgres-collector-config.yaml.tmp /tmp/stackgres-collector-config.yaml
                  done
              jq -sR '{ data: { "config.yaml": . } }' /tmp/stackgres-collector-config.yaml > /tmp/stackgres-collector-configmap.json
              kubectl patch configmap -n stackgres stackgres-collector \
                --type merge --patch-file /tmp/stackgres-collector-configmap.json
              jq -sR '{ data: { "start-otel-collector.sh": . } }' /tmp/start-otel-collector-fix.sh > /tmp/stackgres-collector-configmap.json
              kubectl patch configmap -n stackgres stackgres-collector \
                --type merge --patch-file /tmp/stackgres-collector-configmap.json
```

### Summary
When add stackgres-operator chart as a dependency in our chart's `Chart.yaml` file, e.g.,

```yaml
- alias: stackgres
  condition: stackgres.enabled
  name: stackgres-operator
  repository: https://stackgres.io/downloads/stackgres-k8s/stackgres/helm/
  version: 1.14.0
```

Installing our chart will fail when `stackgres.enabled=true` with the following error from `install-sgconfig` job

```
+ kubectl replace -f /SGConfig.yaml
customresourcedefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io/sgconfigs.stackgres.io replaced
+ kubectl apply -f /sgconfig.yaml
Error from server (BadRequest): error when creating "/sgconfig.yaml": SGConfig in version "v1" cannot be handled as a SGConfig: strict decoding error: unknown field "spec.enabled"
```

The problem is 1.14.0 changed to create the sgconfig object using `kubectl apply -f`, and by default it does `strict` validation. It's not a problem in 1.13.0 as the sgconfig object is rendered from helm template and installed by helm with `warn` level validation.

Issue:
After major version upgrade pg_hba.conf have trust permission for remote connections
### Summary

After major version upgrade `pg_hba.conf` have trust permission for remote connections allowing any user to connect without password.

### Current Behaviour 

The pg_hba.conf is the one created by `pg_upgrade` utility that has the trust permission for remote connections.

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an SGCluster with version "15"
2. Create an SGPostgresConfig with version "16"
3. Create a SGDbOps for major version upgrade to upgrade the cluster to version 16.3 and use the SGPostgresConfig for version "16"

### Expected Behaviour

The `pg_hba.conf` file is not changed from the one generated by the bootstrap process.

### Possible Workaround

There are 2 workaround. You may apply both of them (the second one is permanent):

1. After a major version upgrade connect to the `patroni` container (`kubectl exec -n "$CLUSTER_NAMESPACE" "$CLUSTER_NAME"` -c patroni -- bash`) and overwrite the `pg_hba.conf` file with the following script that replaces it with the correct one (just change `replicator` username if you have something different in the last line) and reload the Postgres configuration:

```

#
# This file controls: which hosts are allowed to connect, how clients
# are authenticated, which PostgreSQL user names they can use, which
# databases they can access.  Records take one of these forms:
#
# local         DATABASE  USER  METHOD  [OPTIONS]
# host          DATABASE  USER  ADDRESS  METHOD  [OPTIONS]
# hostssl       DATABASE  USER  ADDRESS  METHOD  [OPTIONS]
# hostnossl     DATABASE  USER  ADDRESS  METHOD  [OPTIONS]
# hostgssenc    DATABASE  USER  ADDRESS  METHOD  [OPTIONS]
# hostnogssenc  DATABASE  USER  ADDRESS  METHOD  [OPTIONS]
#
# (The uppercase items must be replaced by actual values.)
#
# The first field is the connection type:
# - "local" is a Unix-domain socket
# - "host" is a TCP/IP socket (encrypted or not)
# - "hostssl" is a TCP/IP socket that is SSL-encrypted
# - "hostnossl" is a TCP/IP socket that is not SSL-encrypted
# - "hostgssenc" is a TCP/IP socket that is GSSAPI-encrypted
# - "hostnogssenc" is a TCP/IP socket that is not GSSAPI-encrypted
#
# DATABASE can be "all", "sameuser", "samerole", "replication", a
# database name, or a comma-separated list thereof. The "all"
# keyword does not match "replication". Access to replication
# must be enabled in a separate record (see example below).
#
# USER can be "all", a user name, a group name prefixed with "+", or a

# you can also write a file name prefixed with "@" to include names
# from a separate file.
#
# ADDRESS specifies the set of hosts the record matches.  It can be a
# host name, or it is made up of an IP address and a CIDR mask that is
# an integer (between 0 and 32 (IPv4) or 128 (IPv6) inclusive) that
# specifies the number of significant bits in the mask.  A host name
# that starts with a dot (.) matches a suffix of the actual host name.
# Alternatively, you can write an IP address and netmask in separate

### Summary

After upgrading from Stackgres Operator to v1.13 we're the metric `pg_replication_is_replica` doesn't include labels like `cluster_name` anymore.

We found out because the alert `PostgresSplitBrain` taken from https://stackgres.io/doc/latest/runbooks/postgres-alerts/ started giving false positives.

I verified all the other metrics om the page mentioned above, and it seems really only `pg_replication_is_replica` is affected.

### Current Behaviour 

`pg_replication_is_replica` doesn't have unique labels

#### Steps to reproduce

Upgrade to Stackgres Operator v1.13 and perform a `SecurityUpgrade` on your Postgres clusters.

### Expected Behaviour

`pg_replication_is_replica` metric should still have the unique labels like `cluster_name`.

### Possible Solution

It seems something related with pg_exporter, when querying the metrics endpoint it shows:
```
# HELP pg_replication_is_replica Indicates if the server is a replica
# TYPE pg_replication_is_replica gauge
pg_replication_is_replica 1
```

instead of this, in previous versions of the Stackgres Operator:
```
# HELP pg_replication_is_replica Indicates if this host is a replica
# TYPE pg_replication_is_replica gauge
pg_replication_is_replica{cluster_name="lightdash-postgres",namespace="lightdash",server="/var/run/postgresql:5432"} 0
```

### Environment

- StackGres version: v1.13.0
- Kubernetes version: 1.28
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: Rancher


### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

`prometheus-postgres-exporter` container
```
ts=2024-09-12T13:53:30.956Z caller=util.go:92 level=info msg="Could not parse string" err="strconv.ParseFloat: parsing \"none\": invalid syntax"
ts=2024-09-12T13:53:30.956Z caller=namespace.go:241 level=info err="Unparseable column type - discarding:  pgbouncer_show_clients replication <nil>\n"
```

[DISCUSSION]
[teoincontatto]: Thanks for the feedback! The latest version of postgres exporter do not allow to overwrite the internal `pg_replication_is_replica` metric with a custom query so it get removed in 1.13.

The solution will be to bring back the removed metric but with a different name. I would suggest `pg_replication_is_replicating`.

A workaround to fix the actual problem before the fix is implemented would be to annotate the `${CLUSTER_NAME}-prometheus-postgres-exporter-config` ConfigMap with `stackgres.io/reconciliation-pause=true` and change the `query.yaml` key in order to bring back the removed metric but with the name changed:

```
  queries.yaml: |-
    pg_replication:
      master: true
      query: |
        SELECT
        CASE
          WHEN pg_last_wal_receive_lsn() = pg_last_wal_replay_lsn() THEN 0
          ELSE extract (EPOCH FROM now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp())::integer
        END AS lag,
        CASE
          WHEN pg_is_in_recovery() THEN 1
          ELSE 0
        END AS is_replicating;
      metrics:
        - lag:
            usage: "GAUGE"
            description: "Replication lag behind master in seconds"
        - is_replicating:
            usage: "GAUGE"
            description: "Indicates if this host is a replica"
    ...
```

Issue:
[Feature] Implement OpenTelemetry in StackGres
The objective of this issue is to implement OpenTelemetry and define the best use case.

OpenTelemetry will help us to develop Logging v 2.0.

**Proposal**

After researching here is a proposal to implement OpenTelemetry collector into the StackGres architecture.

The OpenTelemetry collector will be implemented as a Deployment that will spawn a single Pod that will scrape for the metrics directly.

```plantuml
@startuml

package "OTEL Deployment" {
  [OTEL Collector]
}

[Prometheus]

node "Node 1" {
  [SGCluster Pod 1]
}

node "Node 2" {
  [SGCluster Pod 2]
}

[SGCluster Pod 1] --> [OTEL Collector]
[SGCluster Pod 2] --> [OTEL Collector]
[OTEL Collector] --> [Prometheus]

@enduml
```


An additional DeamonSet, disable by default, may be configured in order to scrape the metric from each configured Node and send them to the Deployment's collector in order to reduce the load on a single process.

```plantuml
@startuml

package "OTEL Deployment" {
  [OTEL Collector]
}

[Prometheus]

node "Node 1" {
  [SGCluster Pod 1]
  [OTEL Collector Node 1]
}

node "Node 2" {
  [SGCluster Pod 2]
  [OTEL Collector Node 2]
}

[SGCluster Pod 1] --> [OTEL Collector Node 1]
[SGCluster Pod 2] --> [OTEL Collector Node 2]
[OTEL Collector Node 1] --> [OTEL Collector]
[OTEL Collector Node 2] --> [OTEL Collector]
[OTEL Collector] --> [Prometheus]

@enduml
```

The configuration will be global and placed in the SGConfig CRD (and so the values of the helm chart will reflect such spec) as follow:

                         # Each OpenTelemetry Collector receive

[ahachete]: The main goal of this issue is to start a transition to a more standards-based OpenTelemetry architecture for our Observability. We will pursue three main goals with this transition:

* Easier configuration. Right now the Prometheus stack is a "dependency" that you should preinstall, and then configured with a wealth of Helm parameters. We should make observability configuration a post-installation decision, and should be easy to be configured. It should be configurable from the Web Console too!

* Simplification of the required stack / enablemente of new components and technologies. By switching to OTEL, we may eventually replace some components with others based on newer technologies or components that require less moving parts. This will not be immediate, but will hapen over time.

* Allow to export the metrics to external services and SaaS applications. By using OTEL and the vast array of exporters supported, we enable users to consume the metrics (and logs) wherever they choose, not only local to their Kubernetes cluster (or accessible to their Kubernetes cluster).

This is probably an epic to keep open for a while. For a first iteration, what I propose to do is:

1. Deploy a cluster-wide OTEL Collector Contrib. It can be its own `Deployment` or a sidecar to the Operator. It could be (but not by default) disabled via Helm chart parameters.
1. Allow for configuration of the collector (another CRD?), also from the Web Console. Among the configuration options we should support:
    * Send them to a local Prometheus stack, including Grafana dashboard injection (as it works now)
    * Send them to an external SaaS service.
1. Phase out the `prometheusAutoBinding` in favor of a default behavior where metrics are unconditionally sent to the collector (if not disabled by Helm chart installation parameter). By default metrics are logged to stdout only, unless the collector is configured.
1. Always deploy the Promeheus exporter (as it will be exporting metrics, as long as there's an OTEL Collector present).

This should be a change that should have minor impact for users, but should allow a better configurability. Documentation will need to be accordingly adjusted (potentially on many areas).

Potentially related issues/ideas to consider here (separate from this issue):
* If we consider a separate CRD to configure the collector, maybe we should consider a more general approach and have a CRD to configure in general many aspects of StackGres, all dynamically? It could be expanded in the future, and potentially phase out Helm chart parameters (or allow them to be used too, but only to configure this CRD initially, with the ability to change it later anytime).
* Move the Prometheus exporter to a Daemonset.

[teoincontatto]: > Deploy a cluster-wide OTEL Collector Contrib. It can be its own `Deployment` or a sidecar to the Operator. It could be (but not by default) disabled via Helm chart parameters.

I would choose a separate deployment since a sidecar to the operator will mean that we will not be able to scale the OTEL collector (currently operator can not be scaled and the effort to do so may be not trivial and add too much on the plate of the release that we can afford).

> Allow for configuration of the collector (another CRD?), also from the Web Console. Among the configuration options we should support:
> 
> * Send them to a local Prometheus stack, including Grafana dashboard injection (as it works now)
> * Send them to an external SaaS service.

and
                                                                                                                                                                
> If we consider a separate CRD to configure the collector, maybe we should consider a more general approach and have a CRD to configure in general many aspects of StackGres, all dynamically? It could be expanded in the future, and potentially phase out Helm chart parameters (or allow them to be used too, but only to configure this CRD initially, with the ability to change it later anytime).

I think the ability to configure the collector from the Web Console requires to have a CRD, otherwise we will end up creating a REST API that modify the StackGres Operator installation or bloating the SGCluster CRD with the configuration of the collector.

Currently we are using helm for configuring the StackGres Operator to integrate with Prometheus Operator and we use such configuration together with SGCluster configuration in order to enable it at the cluster level. I think that with the new approach we should still allow to configure both at global and cluster level. So I see we need two configuration for the OTEL Collector:

* A global level configuration that could fit in helm chart values or in a new CRD that manage global aspects of the collector like how exposing or who is the target of the metrics, the k8s specific configuration (annotations, tolerations, affinity etc.), the default configuration for clusters and other configs of the operator itself. 
* A cluster level configuration that can overwrite the default configuration for cluster and that could allow to define also how to expose the metrics for such cluster (overwriting also) the global configuration or to fine tune the metrics that are exposed.

I feel like we have to analyze the possibilities to craft a good CRD to reference from the StackGres cluster in order to enable the collector. We may have it created by default (as for other configs) and add a flag to disable it and that will disable the Prometheus exporter also. To do so we will probably have to create a PoC to explore the ground and see what we can achieve since it is not known or not clear to me. WDYT?

We should study how do the transition for those that are using already the Prometheus Operator integration. My idea is that when upgrading to the new version we should create a documentation on how to integrate StackGres OTEL collector with Prometheus Operator or Prometheus configuration. WDYT?

[teoincontatto]: I've create a PoC that runs an OpenTelemetry Contrib Collector deployment that is configured to scrape stats from existing prometheus exporters of StackGres clusters (prometheus postgres exporter and envoy). I've disabled the Prometheus integration so that it does not interfere.

For the only purpose of this PoC the otel collector configuration is crafted using a sidecar of otel collector. When correctly implemented it will be created automatically by the operator itself. In any case the idea is to provide the user with some template options including the "empty" configuration for the output that logs everything in the Pod stdout or send metrics to prometheus (and any other SaaS service we may want to include) but also to configure the output of the collector as they want to so that any custom scenario could be achieved as long as the otel collector supports it. This will also include options for the input like global scraping configuration or fine grained scraping configuration and options like enabling the grafana integration.

There is also a simple hack that allow to update the operator without helm (spoiler helm is still there but hidden) by just changing the key `values.yaml` in a specific ConfigMap called `stackgres-configuration` in the same namespace than the operator. The idea to use a ConfigMap instead of a real CRD is that ConfigMap whould allow to install the operator with a single YAML. ConfigMap can be also validated using a custom validationwebhook on the specific resource. Any change to the configuration will be detected by a special operator called `stackgres-configurator` that is a special Deployment with wide permissions to allow to trigger the update of the Operator helm char release. The configurator is a "stupid" operator that is only in charge of updating the helm chart release using helm. It is already possible for part of the operator helm chart values configuration to be updated without disruption of the webhooks (excluding first install of course). OTOH we should improve this by making also the operator webhook disruption free for any change in the configuration if possible.

Having a CRD as a mechanism of configuring the operator and make it live together with the helm char values configuration should be possible. We may just replace the ConfigMap with this CRD that probably should be unnamespaced and only be able to have a single name (`stackgres-configuration`). We may even use it as a way to remove other unnamepsace resources (ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding, ValidatingWebhookConfigurations, MutatingWebhookConfigurations, CRDs, etc.) and solve issues like #815.

Regarding the Prometheus Operator stack OpenTelemetry Collector requires a [configuration on the Prometheus side in order to export data](https://uptrace.dev/opentelemetry/prometheus-metrics.html#exporting-opentelemetry-metrics-to-prometheus). This is similar to what the current integration does but, instead of configuring a ServiceMonitor or PodMonitor for each cluster, it will be the user (since we want to remove Prometheus integration) that will have to configure a single ServiceMonitor or PodMonitor to point to the OpenTelemetry Collector.

[teoincontatto]: The PoC revealed a problem with reloading the configuration for prometheus receiver in the otel collector contrib that requires the collector to be restarted completely (by shutting down the process and start it again). To circumvent this problem it will be created a wrapper script (not possible in the PoC since the container used do not include any other executable than the otel collector itself) that will allow to shutdown the process and start it again on a configuration change.

[teoincontatto]: As commented in the last meeting we will introduce a new (configurable) layer for open telemetry that will be put in between the centralized open telemetry Deployment and the Prometheus exporters to allow to scale better the distribution of load by using the Open Telemetry Protocol (OLTP) and only rely on Prometheus protocol on the same node. For this purpose a DaemonSet of Open Telemetry Collector will provide an Open Telemetry Collector instance per node that will receive telemetries using local connections. The cluster pods will connect to DaemonSet instance on the same node using the `.status.hostIp` and a knwon port (set by global configuration). The DeamonSet instances will then connect to the Deployment (with 1 instance by default but scalable by the user). The user may remove the DeamonSet by global configuration flag, in which case the exporters will be scraped from the Deployment instances. But in this case the instances of the Deployment can not be scaled.

[ahachete]: Technically speaking, we may have additional Prometheus-protocol interaction if the user wants to consume the metrics from the Deployment of the OTEL Collector. We may consider whether that will be the Prometheus scraping the collector or remote-push.

[teoincontatto]: This issue will no more include the functionality of configuring the operator using the Web Console and that functionality is moved to issue #2111

[teoincontatto]: I am reviewing the configuration part looking also at the upgrade from previous versions for this feature. Currently the operator creates PodMonitors that allows to connect the StackGres exporters (postgres and envoy) to any Prometheus instances created by the Prometheus operator.

Now on we will just need one PodMonitor that will connect to the pod of the collector for each Prometheus instance created by the Prometheus operator.

I think that the idea of connecting to any Prometheus instance created by the Prometheus operator is wrong (or, at least, not optimal). We should instead create a PodMonitor for each Prometheus instance the user requires. So that the configuration is not everything or nothing but, instead, an array of references to Prometheus instances created by the Prometheus operator that the user choose to configure to scrape the cluster metrics.

To make the configuration even more fine grained, it should allow to connect a Prometheus instance to a specific exporter in the collector configuration. For this reason, in order to also provide an easy automatic integration with Prometheus Operator, we should provide both path.

Finally the configuration should be global (i.e. should go into the helm chart values.yaml) so that the user can use the same exporter to connect to the Prometheus instance (or any other consumer) or define his particular set of exporter to connect to his particular consumers. The SGCluster will include a field that indicates the receiver (prometheus by default) from which the scrapers to that cluster will be configured by the operator.

## Proposal

The following section will be added to the helm chart values in order to configure the Prometheus integration (this does not include the full configuration changes in that file that this issue requires but will add that info later on):

```yaml
collector:
  prometheusOperatorMonitors: # Optional section to configure PodMonitors for specific Prometheus instances
                              # Warning: resources created by this integration that does set
                              #  the metadata namespace to the same as the operator will not
                              #  be removed when removing the helm chart. Changing the namespace
                              #  may require configure the Prometheus CR properly in order to
                              #  discover PodMonitor in such namespace.
  - name: <Prometheus CR reference> # Required. Will allow to create a PodMonitor in the Prometheus CR namespace that will scrape from the collector Pod pointing by default to the prometheus exporter
    exporter: # Indicates the name of the exporter to scrape from that will be configured in the PodMonitor
    metadata: # overwrite some PodMonitor metadata
      name:
      namespace: # changing the namespace may require configure the Prometheus CR properly in order in order to discover PodMonitor in such namespace.
      labels:
      annotations:
      ownerReferences:
    spec: {} # PodMonitor spec that will be overwritten by the operator
```

If .collector.prometheusOperatorMonitors is not specified field .prometheus.allowAutobind will create prometheus integrations for all the Prometheus instances that exists in the K8S cluster. This will provide the easy path for user that do not want to configure much stuffs and will be backward compatible with previous versions.

The SGCluster will include the following new fields:

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGCluster
spec:
  configurations:
    metrics:
      disable: <boolean> # will replace .spec.pods.disableMetricsExporter that will become deprecated and ignored.
      receiver: <string> # will indicate the receiver in the configuration for the collector scraper (if not specified, will default to prometheus)
```

The field `.spec.prometheusAutobind` will still be used to control if the cluster will be finally scraped by any PodMonitor.

The operator will no longer create PodMonitor for the cluster Pods (only for the collector) and those existing will be removed.

## Implementation plan

The benchmark will use stats from pg_stat_statement to generate a load based on:

* top-n queries that consume more than 95% of the execution time.
* top-n queries that consume more than 95% of the number of queries.
* user provided custom queries

Since values are not present in the query from pg_stat_statements there are some options to retrieve such values:

* Sampling queries from pg_stat_activity
* Use values from logs (if they are enabled)
* Use values from Postgres histogram stats
* Extract values from pgotel

~Read-only queries are filtered by checking them one by one using a read-only transaction.~

Read-only queries are filtered using a configurable regular expression.

Use pgbench to perform the benchmark using the custom queries.

## Acceptance Criteria

* [] Implement feature
* [] Test feature
* [] Document feature

[DISCUSSION]
[teoincontatto]: I was able to produce a PoC in the following script:

[pgbench.sh](/uploads/7901dee6bb96a4ae825891f5934d507c/pgbench.sh)

The script creates an SGCluster and 3 pgbench SGDbOps. The first pgbench initialize the database with 10Gi of data without primary keys, the second run an initialization scripts that creates in a new database (to minimize noise on the main database) a table called topqueries to store the top N queries from pg_stat_statements (configurable), a table called queries (with an index on the query) to store the queries sampled from pg_stat_activity, reset the pg_stat_statements and uses pg_cron to schedule (configurable) the insertions into the topqueries table (in order to have time for pg_stat_statements to collect data) and the insertions into the queries from pg_stat_activity (done frequently and based on the query id stored in topqueries). The second pgbench run also a normal pgbench in order to simulate the real traffic. Finally the third pgbench uses a set of scripts based on a sample of the queries collected in the queries table to replay the real traffic generated by the second pgbench.

Also, to avoid having to lose queries upfront during the first sampling phase (when gathering the list of most slow or most called queries), instead of filtering using a read-only connection, we will use a regular expression filter.

[teoincontatto]: Here is the proposed changed based on changed from #1027 that includes an additional benchmark type `sampling` that will create a status in the SGDbOps to be used with the new `replay` mode of the `pgbench` benchmark to replay sampled queries in the target database:

```yaml

kind: SGDbOps
spec:
  op: benchmark
  benchmark:
    type: sampling # * `sampling`: Will sample real queries and store them in the SGDbOps status in order to be used by a `pgbench` benchmark using `replay` mode. The benchmark database will be used to store the sampled queries but user must specify a target database to be sampled in the `sampling` section.
    sampling:
      targetDatabase: <string> # The target database to be sampled
      topQueriesCollectDuration: <string> # An ISO 8601 duration in the format `PnDTnHnMn.nS`, that specifies how long the to wait before selecting top queries in order to collect enough stats.
      samplingDuration: <string> # An ISO 8601 duration in the format `PnDTnHnMn.nS`, that specifies how long will last the sampling of real queries that will be replayed later.
      topQueriesFilter: <string> # Regular expression for filtering representative statements when selecting top queries. Will be ignored if `mode` is set to `custom`. By default is `^ *(with|select) `. See https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-matching.html#FUNCTIONS-POSIX-REGEXP
      mode: <string> # The mode used to select the top queries used for sampling:
                     # * `time`: The top queries will be selected among the most slow queries.
                     # * `calls`: The top queries will be selected among the most called queries.
                     # * `custom`: The `customTopQuery` will be used to select top queries.
      topQueriesPercentile: <integer> # Percentile of queries to consider as part of the top queries. Will be ignored if `mode` is set to `custom`. By default `95`.
      topQueriesMin: <integer> # Minimum number of queries to consider as part of the top queries. By default `5`.
      customTopQuery: <string> # The query used to select top queries. Will be ignored if `mode` is not set to `custom`.
      queries: <integer> # Number of sampled queries to include in the result. By default `10`.
      omitTopQueriesInStatus: <boolean> # When `true` omit to include the top queries stats in the SGDbOps status. By default `false`.
    pgbench:
      mode: replay # * `replay`: Will replay the sampled queries of a sampling benchmark. If the `custom` section is specified it will be used instead. Queries can be referenced setting `custom.scripts.replay` to the index of the query in the sampling benchmark SGDbOps's status (index start from 0).
      replay:
        samplingSGDbOps: <string> # SGDbOps of type benchmark that will be used to replay sampled queries.
      custom:

        - replay: <integer> # The index of the query in the sampling benchmark SGDbOps's status (index start from 0).
status:
  benchmark:
    sampling:
      topQueries:
      - id: <string> # The query id of the representative statement calculated by Postgres
        stats: # The top query stats returned by the top queries query
          <string>: <string>
      queries:
      - query: <string> # The sampled SQL query
        id: <string> # The query id of the representative statement calculated by Postgres
        timestamp: <string> # The sampled query timestamp

### Summary

CREATE USER authenticator with password 'auth_pass' superuser;
```
* Create the secret in your Kubernetes setup

kubectl -n your_namespace create secret generic postgresql-origin \
--from-literal=superuser-username=postgres \
--from-literal=superuser-password=postgresql \
--from-literal=replicator-username=postgres \
--from-literal=replicator-password=postgresql \
--from-literal=authenticator-username=authenticator \

touch /var/lib/postgresql/15/main/postgresql.conf

echo '
# "local" is for Unix domain socket connections only
local   all             all                                     trust
# IPv4 local connections:
host    all             all             127.0.0.1/32            scram-sha-256
# IPv6 local connections:
host    all             all             ::1/128                 scram-sha-256

local   replication     all                                     trust
host    replication     all             127.0.0.1/32            scram-sha-256
host    replication     all             ::1/128                 scram-sha-256
