Issue:
S3 WAL segment upload and download extremely slow with WAL-G 3.0.1
### Summary

WAL-G version 3.0.1 included in the latest StackGres 1.11 has unacceptable performance when targeting an S3 bucket that contains a considerable number of objects. This is due to a bug in WAL-G.

### Current Behaviour

Calls to `wal-g wal-fetch`, `wal-g wal-push`, and potentially others, take \~15 minutes (for example) to complete when they usually would take only a few seconds, if the target S3 bucket contains a few thousand objects. This results in huge lags in WAL log shipping and crash recovery.

Whenever wal-g is launched for wal-fetch or wal-push, it performs a credential validation step when targeting S3 before it performs the actual work. This validation consists of calling `ListObjects` on the target bucket.

A bug on WAL-G 3.0.1 results in this validation step calling ListObjects as a multi-page request (1 HTTP request per page), each page with a single object, in sequence, until all objects in the bucket are listed.

In my case, this issue resulted in WAL chunks taking over \~15 minutes EACH to be sent to S3, as each call to `wal-g wal-push` caused the whole bucket to be listed first, one key at a time. My cluster was 3 days behind in WAL logs being uploaded. Forcefully restarting the instance was equally disastrous as `wal-g wal-fetch` also took \~15 minutes to download EACH object it needed from S3.

The bug in WAL-G seems resolved in the master branch of WAL-G after this [PR in their repo](https://github.com/wal-g/wal-g/pull/1718).

#### Steps to reproduce

In a cluster with backups to AWS S3 configured, running StackGres 1.11 and Postgres 16.2 for example, and some write activity, where the target backup S3 bucket already contains a few thousand objects, you'll notice a build up of ".ready" files under /var/lib/postgresql/data/pg_wal/archive_status in the cluster's patroni container. With appropriate tools installed in the container, you'll identify e.g. with `ps` that a wal-g process is taking several minutes to send a segment.

Using AWS CloudTrail logging for AWS S3 data requests, you'll notice there will be thousands and thousands of ListObjects requests with max-keys=1 coming from the account used to upload WAL chunks.

### Expected Behaviour

WAL-G to perform its work in a short few seconds per file, as per previous versions.

### Workaround

Currently, I have to use a Kyverno policy to force the injection of a WAL-G [environment variable that skips S3 verification](https://github.com/wal-g/wal-g/blob/ae8fc4e8374243433fcbc90786fdc0928784879d/docs/STORAGES.md?plain=1#L94) by wal-g. In the patroni container of each cluster, I set `S3_SKIP_VALIDATION=true`.

```
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: add-walg-s3-fix
  namespace: cluster1-timescaledb
spec:
  rules:
    - name: add-walg-s3-fix
      match:
        any:
        - resources:
            kinds:
              - StatefulSet
            names:
              - timescaledb
      mutate:
        patchStrategicMerge:
          spec:
            template:
              spec:
                containers:
                  - name: patroni
                    env:
                      - name: S3_SKIP_VALIDATION
                        value: "true"
```

### Possible Solution

Roll back the version of wal-g used in StackGres, or wait until a new version is released containing the fix.

### Environment

- StackGres version: 1.11.0
- Kubernetes version: 1.30
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: AWS

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

None.

Issue:
Implement SGStream to integrate with Postgres CDC and CloudEvents
Postgres allow to perform CDC using [logical replication](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/logical-replication.html) in order to obtain a stream of changes from a source table (or tables) in a database.
Integrating this functionality with [CloudEvents](https://cloudevents.io/) will allow users to gain the ability of new way of integrate their applications with Postgres. For example lambda functions based on Postgres change events using [Knative Service](https://knative.dev/docs/serving/).

Other than integrating with CloudEvents we want to allow other target of CDC, including the same Postgres. This is why this proposal want to create new CRD that we will call SGStream that is independent of an SGCluster but can obviously reference one as its source.

## Implementation plan

[Debezium Engine](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/development/engine.html) provide a well tested and maintained foundation that allows to perform CDC not only on Postgres but on a wide range of other CDC sources through pluggable [Debezium Connectors](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/2.6/connectors/index.html).

[CloudEvents](https://cloudevents.io/) provide a spec that allows for various formats (JSON, protobuf, etc.) and various bindings (HTTP, kafka, ...). Since [Knative support the CloudEvents HTTP binding for sources](https://github.com/knative/eventing/blob/main/docs/spec/sources.md) we will chose that as the first supported binding type and JSON for the first supported format. Such binding and format should be enough common to allow integration with a wide range of targets in this first implementation.

The SGStream CRD will then connect a CDC source with a target. At first we will just implement the SGCluster as source type (but we will allow to extend this in the future. OTOH we will just implement CloudEvents as target type (also open to extension for the future). There will be some extra configuration for Debezium and the StatefuletSet (PV will be used to store CDC status) that will be created to run it.

The proposed SGStream CRD is as follow:

[DISCUSSION]
[teoincontatto]: After an analysis of the Debezium JDBC connector I can not find a known usage of it with the `DebeziumEngine` class. In particular the connector mentioned in the [docs](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/jdbc.html#jdbc-overview) is a [Kafka Connect sink connector](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/connect/index.html#connectors) that requires the [Kafka Connect runtime](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/connect/index.html#workers). Including such a runtime would not suite our needs due to the fact that it will require a Kafka deployment that we want to avoid.

Instead the class `io.debezium.connector.jdbc.JdbcChangeEventSink` of the `debezium-connector-jdbc` java module seems a good candidate to be used together with `DebeziumEngine` class. Such java class requires to be initialized receiving the documented properties. I still have to check if all of them are supported or only a subset. This means that the model proposed in the description may change depending on that. The `DebeziumEngine` use a single thread to read CDC events from the source database. Those events have to be passed to the JdbcChangeEventSink in order to be sinked in the target database. Below a discussion about the issues that have to be carefully solved in order to use this approach.

1.

To initialize the class `JdbcChangeEventSink` we use the code from the `start(Map<String, String>)` method of the class `io.debezium.connector.jdbc.JdbcSinkConnectorTask`. It is quite short and straightforward but we will have to monitor its evolution in order to maintain the initialization code properly.

2.

The type of record class that `JdbcChangeEventSink` class receives the CDC event in for of `org.apache.kafka.connect.sink.SinkRecord`. `DebeziumEngine` builder allow to specify a bunch of types for the received CDC events. In particular the type `io.debezium.embedded.Connect` defines the `org.apache.kafka.connect.source.SourceRecord` type from Kafka Connect API that extends the same type `org.apache.kafka.connect.connector.ConnectRecord` as for the `SinkRecord` type. The difference is  that the `SinkRecord` requires some fields that are not present in the `SourceRecord`:

* The [Kafka offset](https://kafka.apache.org/30/javadoc/org/apache/kafka/clients/consumer/KafkaConsumer.html):

    > Kafka maintains a numerical offset for each record in a partition. This offset acts as a unique identifier of a record within that partition, and also denotes the position of the consumer in the partition. For example, a consumer which is at position 5 has consumed records with offsets 0 through 4 and will next receive the record with offset 5.

After analyzing the code seems that the `JdbcChangeEventSink` class is not using it in any path except when the `primary.key.mode` property is set to `kafka`. We could simply vet this configuration option by removing it from the documentation and throwing an error if the user try to set it to such value.  In any case we set this value to the value of the LSN shifted by 32 bit (so losing 32 most significant bits) and anded with a monotonic counter of 32 bit. This should provide a offset that behaves as expected.

* The `org.apache.kafka.common.record.TimestampType`

An enum which value can be one of `NO_TIMESTAMP_TYPE`, `CREATE_TIME` or `LOG_APPEND_TIME`.

The type is not used by the `JdbcChangeEventSink` or any dependent class. In any case we set this value to `CREATE_TIME`.

* The [Kafka partition](https://kafka.apache.org/30/javadoc/org/apache/kafka/clients/consumer/KafkaConsumer.html):

Another difference is that in the `SinkRecord` the Kafka partition field that is passed down to the `ConnectRecord` type can not be `null` but `DebeziumEngine` only delivers `SourceRecord` with a `null` value for the Kafka partition field.

The Kafka partition does not seem to be used by the `JdbcChangeEventSink` or any dependent class. In any case we will set its value to `0` simulating that there is only a single partition with value `0`.

3.

Since the `JdbcChangeEventSink` use some resources we have to make sure that when the `DebeziumEngine` is closed the `JdbcChangeEventSink` class is also closed.

[teoincontatto]: Some notes on DDL migration:

* Migration of DDL is basic, we will need to use some tools like `pg_dumpall` and `psql` or `pg_restore` in order to migrate the DDL completely. We can perform the copy of the DDL using such tools before Debezium starts. User can disable such feature using `SGStream.spec.target.sgCluster.skipDdlImport`. Special care will have to be taken with sequences where a final step will set them as in the source database.

* Adding a column or a table is supported.

* When a column is dropped the target database will still have the dropped column. Migration will not be stopped by such an event.

* Altering a column type is not supported and will break the migration.

* Creating a table is supported.

* When a table is dropped the target database will still have the dropped table. Migration will not be stopped by such an event.

The condition will be set when Debezium receive the custom signal `tombstone`. When such a signal is received the Debezium Engine will be shutdown and, in case the source is a Postgres database, the replication slot and the publication (if exists) are dropped.

Issue:
Allow limiting the scope of operator to a set of namespaces
### Problem to solve

Currently, the helm-chart creates `ClusterRole` that allows very broad permissions on the cluster. This role is bound to both the operator & init service accounts through a `ClusterRoleBinding` which gives the operator extensive permissions across all namespaces in the cluster.

<!-- Provide a clear and concise description of what problem this will solve-->

### Further details

This raises a security concern when installing the operator on clusters with mixed-workloads which are relying on namespace isolation. In such a use-case Stackgres might only be used in certain namespaces but the operator would still have access to resources across the entire cluster.

This also creates the potential for privilege escalation through the operator/rest api.

<!-- Include use cases, benefits, and/or goals -->

### Proposal

The following changes will address this problem:

* In helm chart the field `allowedNamespaces` will allow to create a set of pairs of `Role` and `RoleBinding` for each namespace listed in the value of field `allowedNamespaces`. The rules that affect namespaced resources present in the `ClusterRoles` will be moved to the `Roles` created. The `RoleBindings` created will target the same subjects as the `ClusterRoles`. This change will now affect how the operator works. The operator and other component will still have cluster level permissions. The operator will receive the list of namespaces set in `allowedNamespaces` with the environment variable `ALLOWED_NAMESPACES` that will be user in order to enable operator scoping when installed with OLM. The operator will not be able to list namespaces but, when a functionality requires such list, will be able to use the list of allowed namespaces instead.

* In helm chart the field `disableClusterRole` will allow to disable completely the creation of any `ClusterRole` (except for the installation process) when set to `true`. This flag will allow to install the operator with privileges within the scope of a single namespace or a set of namespaces but will break some functionalities. In particular:
    * Creation and upgrade of CustomResourceDefinitions. This will become responsibility of the installation, implemented with a post-install/post-upgrade Job.
    * Set CA bundle for Webhooks. This will become responsibility of the installation, implemented with a post-install/post-upgrade Job.
    * Check existence of CustomResourceDefinition when listing custom resources. This can be solved with a refactor.
    * Validation of StorageClass. This will become a limitation.
    * REST API endpoint `can-i/{verb}/{resource}` and `can-i` will always return the full list of permissions for any resource and verb since they rely on creation of subjectaccessreviews unnamespaced resource that requires a cluster role.
    * Other REST API endpoints will not work since they rely on impersonation that requires a cluster role. This will make unusable the Web Console.
* In helm chart the field `allowImpersonationForRestApi` will allow to workaround the limitation of the impersonation that breaks the REST API. When set to `true` it will allow the creation of the ClusterRole to provide permissions to impersonate users at the cluster level even when `disableClusterRole` is set to `true`.

### Testing

* [ ] All E2E test should be adapted in order to make sure this functionality do not prevent the operator and the resources generated from working as expected

## Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] Implement the changed
* [ ] Adapt E2E framework in order to allow test the changed
* [ ] Document the feature

### Links / references

* [Kubernetes User Impersonation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/authentication/#user-impersonation)
* [OLM scoping](https://olm.operatorframework.io/docs/advanced-tasks/operator-scoping-with-operatorgroups/)

[DISCUSSION]

We have to prioritize this issue. thanks

[teoincontatto]: There is a "kind of" blocker related to operator bundle packaging that allows to use CRD conversion webhooks only for AllNamespace Operators (i.e. operators that can access all namespaces). More details on why this is so are in the second point of [this OLM enhancement](https://github.com/operator-framework/enhancements/blob/master/enhancements/olm-crd-conversion-webhooks.md#csv-support-for-crd-conversion-webhook):

> CRD conversion webhooks intercept requests for all namespaces, so only AllNamespace operators will ship with conversion webhooks and only those can be installed to leverage these webhooks. Once an AllNamespace operator is installed, it would claim ownership of the API in every namespace, and OLM will not allow installation of any other Operator that claims the same API.

[teoincontatto]: Probably, the only option in order for this functionality to be implemented is to remove completely the conversion webhook and rely completely on the CR upgrade logic already present in the operator bootstrap and supported by the mutating webhooks.

<!--

### Problem to solve

Restoring a replica using pg_basebackup put heavy load on the primary and is slow. Instead, if a replica was able to get the latest backup and use it to restore the data will avoid to impose such load on the primary and may be faster.

### Proposal

The feature will be enabled by default as long as the backups are configured in the SGCluster. We will add a new section `SGCluster.spec.replication.initialization` that will containes the following values:

* `mode`:
    * `BackupFromPrimary`: When this mode is used replicas will be always created from the primary using `pg_basebackup`.
    * `BackupFromReplica`: When this mode is used replicas will be created from another existing replica using
     `pg_basebackup`. Fallsback to `BackupFromPrimary` if there's no replica or it fails.
    * `FromExistingBackup`: When this mode is used replicas will be created from an existing SGBackup. If `backupNewerThan` is set
     the SGBackup must be newer than its value. When this mode fails to restore an SGBackup it will try with a previous one (if exists). Fallsback to `BackupFromReplica` if there's no backup left or it fails.
    * `FromNewlyCreatedBackup`: When this mode is used replicas will be created from a newly created SGBackup.
     Fallsback to `FromExistingBackup` if `backupNewerThan` is set and exists a recent backup newer than its value or it fails.
* `backupNewerThan`: An ISO 8601 duration in the format `PnDTnHnMn.nS`, that specifies how old an SGBackup have to be in order to be seleceted to initialize a replica.
 When `FromExistingBackup` mode is set this field restrict the selection of SGBackup to be used for recovery newer than the specified value.
 When `FromNewlyCreatedBackup` mode is set this field skip the creation SGBackup to be used for recovery if one newer than the specified value exists. 
* `backupRestorePerformance`: Section to configure backup restore configuration similar to the one in `SGCluster.spec.initialData.restore.fromBackup.performance`
  
### Testing

* [ ] Test the 4 modes in an E2E test

## Acceptance Criteria

* [] Implement the feature
* [] Test the feature
* [] Document the feature

[DISCUSSION]
[ahachete]: I fully agree with the issue and its goals. I have some further thoughts on the proposal for the field:
* I'd call it `replicaInitializationMode` instead.
* I'd not allow `OnlyBackups`. Because they may lead to a state where the replica initialization may fail.
* I propose instead the following ones:
    * `BackupFromPrimary`.
    * `BackupFromReplica`. Similar to the above, but creating the base backup from another replica, if exists. Fallsback to `BackupFromPrimary` if there's no replica or it fails.
    * `FromExistingBackup`. This one would need to clarify that also includes snapshots, if backups are being created from snapshots. Also that it will (obviously) start from the latest backup available. Fallsback to `BackupFromPrimary` if there's no backups configured.
    * `FromNewlyCreatedBackup`. This one is similar to the previous one, but creates a backup just before initializing the replica. This won't make much sense for regular backups, but it makes a lot of sense if using snapshots, since replica creation time may significantly decrease (time for creating a new snapshot may be much shorter than replicating a lot of WALs if the most recent snapshot is old).

Since the restore from a backup may always fail I would add a field called `SGCluster.spec.replication.initialization.failbackForBackupUpTo` that will try to restore from the latest backup failing over the previous backup and repeating this up to that number less one (default to 1 so will just try latest) and if not working (or backups are not configured) will fall back to first a replica and then (if fails or not present) falls back to the primary.

When creating the new one (with the same name) and upon performing the mandatory restart operation after an upgrade, as part of the startup process Postgres checked for WAL files in the backup... and found invalid ones! Since the cluster name was the same, it tried to access the backup files from the previous cluster. Postgres uses an internal SYSTEM IDENTIFIER for every cluster, and those IDs didn't match. This prevented Postgres from starting up and caused the upgrade operation to fail.
```

The objective of this issue is add code to introduce an extra path element where backups are stored that is unique per cluster, regardless of the name (fully preventing this situation in the future).

In particular we propose to change the default backup path in order to include the creation timestamp:

```
SGCluster.spec.configurations.backups[].path <- "sgbackpus.stackgres.io/<SGCluster.metadata.namespace>/<SGCluster.metadata.name>/<postgres major version>/<SGCluster.metadata.creationTimestamp>"
```

Integrate with KEDA (Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling) and Vertical Pod Autoscaler for horizontal and vertical autoscaling
[KEDA](https://keda.sh/) allows to automatically scale horizontally (up and down) resources based on events fired from configured triggers. KEDA provides a great deal of flexibility in defining the triggers and the scaling configuration.

[Vertical Pod Autoscaler](https://github.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/tree/master/vertical-pod-autoscaler) allows to automatically scale vertically (up and down) cpu and memory resources for Pods based on stats.

From a general perspective, scaling up and down a Postgres database is a decision that shouldn't be taken lightly, as it may have availability and performance implications. Replica horizontal scaling can be performed, if configured properly, in a non-disruptive manner (or at least in a way where the performance hit is understood). Again, if properly configured, it can be automated, and here's where KEDA may play an important role.

Replicas are by default initialized from the primary node, which may suffer some I/O impact during replica creation. For zero impact replicas can also be initialized from backups + continuous archiving. The user may already specify this through the [replicate from storage](https://stackgres.io/doc/latest/reference/crd/sgcluster/#replicate-from-storage) property.

[KEDA supports scaling of custom resources](https://keda.sh/docs/2.10/concepts/scaling-deployments/#scaling-of-custom-resources) (like we'd need for our `SGCluster`), requiring:

2. That a KEDA `ScaledObject` is implemented, in the same namespace as the `SGCluster`.

For primary (and replicas) vertical scaling it may happen in a disruptive or non-disruptive manner. Disrupting means that the Pod will be evicted and re-created with increased or decreased cpu and/or memory resources based on actual usage. The disadvantage is that in case of the primary being evicted the database will be unavailable until respawned or a failover happens. Non-disruptive means that the node will allow to increase the CPU and memory without stopping the database using a feature called "In Place Resources Update". [teoincontatto]: Actually I do not see how the `replicationGroups` section could be implemented. KEDA `ScaledObject` (just like `HorizontalPodAutoscaler`) is only able to change the `/scale` subresource and has no knowledge of sub-groups. Indeed, we may introduce an alternative definition for replication group size in the `SGCluster.spec.replication.groups` section that will be based on field `percentageOfInstances` and optional fields `startInstances` and `maxInstances` (both default to null). While field `percentageOfInstances` will be mutually exclusive with `instances`, the other two can be specified only when `percentageOfInstances` is also specified. This way each group will have a number of instances based on a formula rather than a fixed number.

For example, if a group has `percentageOfInstances` set to 20% and SGCluster has a total of 10 instances the group size will be of 2 instances.

The `startInstances` field will be used to make sure the group start with at least such number of instances. Back to the example, if the group has `startInstances` set to 2 and SGCluster has a total of 10 instances the group will still be of 2 instances. But if the total number of instances drop from 10 then the group size will be of 0.

The `maxInstances` field will be used instead to make sure the group do not grow more than the specified number of instances. In the example, having `maxInstances` set to 3 means that if SGCluster has a total of 20 instances the group size will be of 3 instances and will grow no further, instead of having 4 instances when the `maxInstances` field is not set.

OTOH StackGres will still be able to implement partially a group that can scale by creating a separate SGCluster with `SGCluster.spec.replicateFrom.instance.sgCluster` pointing to another one.

Issue:
Allow Patroni to use an "external" DCS (not Kubernetes API -> etcd)
When running Patroni on Kubernetes, it's usual to use as a DCS the etcd behinds Kubernetes. Patroni explicitly supports Kubernetes API for etcd as a DCS, and this is the current mechanism for StackGres.

This is convenient --no additional configuration required, no extra resources to be provisioned-- but may not be completely adequate for larger environments.

The problem is that Kubernetes etcd is meant to support all the metadata for Kubernetes itself, and may have to support a decent load. Surely, large Kubernetes clusters dimension and operate large enough etcd clusters.

But Patroni itself needs X amount of request/unit of time to etcd, which is proportional to the number of instances of the cluster, and obviously the number of clusters. At some point, large number of clusters and instances per cluster may lead to a huge load in the Kubernetes etcd which may be undesirable.

Instead, we should also allow Patroni to be configured to use an "external" etcd (it may be running within the Kubernetes cluster but as independently deployed etcd cluster) or even outside Kubernetes. Similarly for other supported DCSs (Consul, Zookeeper).

This is currently not permitted in StackGres, and to support this one of the following approaches may be considered:
1. `SGCluster.spec.configurations.patroni.initialConfig` should allow `consul`, `etcdv3` and `zookeeper` sections.
1. Specify an additional property for this, like in `SGCluster.spec.configurations.patroni.dcs` and allow there the above objects.
1. Alternatively, reconsider the idea of the `SGPatroniConfig` CRD (https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/issues/863).

[DISCUSSION]
[jose_oss_pg]: @teoincontatto @jorsol @gcannata could you please evaluate this issue?

can we consider for the release 1.8?

[teoincontatto]: The 1.8.0-rc1 release is closed to feature requests development.

[teoincontatto]: Currently, some of the functionality of StackGres, is based on the low level implementation of Patroni to detect the primary instance. This logic requires a refactor in order to be based on the Patroni REST API so that the underlying implementation do not affect other components.

[ahachete]: Can you elaborate a bit more? How would affect using a different DCS the Patroni behavior? How this is related to the REST API?

Sorry, I'm missing some details here :sweat_smile:

[teoincontatto]: For example we run SGScript only on the primary instance. To make sure the controller that executes the query is on the primary instance the Endpoints marked by Patroni with the primary instance name is used against the running Pod name. If the DCS changes to something else we can not use the Endpoints anymore to detect who is the current primary. The same happens to know if a Pod that was the primary has been deleted where we need the primary history that we get from the config Endpoints. So the idea is to refactor all that code to instead use the Patroni API to gather all that information.

But another issue, much more critical, is that when other DCS are configured Patroni will no longer update the Endpoints. In that case the operator (or, probably better, the Pod local controller) should be able to detect such configuration and update the Endpoints itself. But having the Endpoints update separated from the leader election may be less safer (see also [Patroni docs](https://patroni.readthedocs.io/en/latest/kubernetes.html#use-endpoints)). It is OK for me to allow configuration of other DCS but we should specify that doing so will end in a less safer HA architecture.

[ahachete]: > If the DCS changes to something else we can not use the Endpoints anymore to detect who is the current primary

Why not? Unless I'm missing some Patroni details, these concepts should be orthogonal. Endpoint management is derived from information stored in the DCS but *abstracted away* from which DCS is used and how Patroni communicates with the DCS.

OK, I think I may be understanding now: you mean if we switch to an external DCS that is not K8s, then the additional K8s configuration (like Endpoint management) would be unavailable to use?

* Refactor Patroni configuration ConfigMap generator: will have to be replaced local Pod controller that updates the configuration using Patroni API
* Read-write Endpoints will have to be managed by StackGres using Patroni API
* HA info will have to be retrieved from Patroni API

Issue:
Allow to mount custom volumes into StackGres containers
Sometimes we need to be able to mount files in the existing StackGres containers. Here is a brief list of usages:

* Advanced configuration for Patroni (like external DCS, see #2626)
* Provide a way to copy data out of the database to a file to be accessed by a custom container.
* Configure extensions

## Implementation plan

The idea is to provide two new sections where a user can list the custom volume mounts for any container or init container (even the custom one):

```yaml
kind: SGCluster
spec:
  pods:
    customVolumeMounts:
      <container name>:
      - name: <custom volume mount name> # See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.29/#volumemount-v1-core
    customInitVolumeMounts:
      <init container name>:
      - name: <custom volume mount name> # See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.29/#volumemount-v1-core
```

Some paths will be excluded as they may break the SGCluster like /var/lib/postgresql, /var/lib/postgresql/data, /var/lib/postgresql/extensions, /var/lib/postgresql/relocated, /var/lib/postgresql/update, /lib64, /usr/lib, /usr/lib64, /usr/lib/postgresql, /usr/lib/postgresql/**, /var/run, /var/run/postgresql, /etc/env, /etc/env/.secret, /etc/patroni

Issue:
SGCluster failing to start when node running on FIPS mode
### Summary, current behaviour

FIPS mode is a enhanced security mode that ensures only certain cryptographic algorithms and best practices are used on a system. Postgres depends on SSL library which is FIPS-aware. There's a [relevant post about Postgres and FIPS mode](http://peter.eisentraut.org/blog/2023/12/05/postgresql-and-fips-mode) worth reviewing.

FIPS mode is a OS setting, but it's exposed via the kernel's `/proc` interface, and therefore becomes a "node setting". So "running on FIPS mode" means essentially running a container on a worker node that has been configured for FIPS mode.

And when running StackGres on a FIPS-enabled worker node, SGCluster fails to create with the following message:

```
FATAL: password encryption failed: disabled for FIPS
STATEMENT: ALTER USER "postgres" WITH PASSWORD  **********
```

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Setup a FIPS-enabled worker node. OS distros like RHEL and Ubuntu Pro support it. Here it was reproduced with RHEL 8. [More information about FIPS on RHEL](https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/8/html/security_hardening/assembly_installing-a-rhel-8-system-with-fips-mode-enabled_security-hardening).
2. Log in / create account with RedHat, download evaluation version of RHEL (60 days, login is sufficient). Tried with 8.5 ISO (since 8.5 version seems to be one fully FIPS validated).
3. For simplicity, create a VM (e.g. KVM, Virtualbox) to install.
4. At installation boot, press [Tab] to edit command line options and append “fips=1” to the install command line.
5. Install.
6. Upon boot, check:

    ```
    root@localhost ~]# fips-mode-setup --check
    FIPS mode is enabled.
    
    [root@localhost ~]# cat /proc/sys/crypto/fips_enabled
    1
    ```
1. Install and configure k3s:
    ```
    curl -sfL https://get.k3s.io | sh -
    …
    alias kubectl="sudo /usr/local/bin/k3s kubectl"
    ```
1. Install Helm. Install StackGres with Helm and create a basic cluster. Create simple cluster. It fails:

    ```
    simple-0   5/6 	CrashLoopBackOff   5 (2s ago)	4m48s
    simple-0   5/6 	Running        	6 (2m49s ago)   7m35s
    ```

1. Events:
    ```
    aht@localhost ~]$ kubectl logs simple-0 -c patroni

    6m21s                       Normal  ClusterPgBouncerConfigUpdated   SGCluster/simple                                Patroni config updated
    2m51s (x21 over 6m18s)   Warning   BackOff                          Pod/simple-0                                    Back-off restarting failed container patroni in pod simple-0_default(139aed26-9d1a-4acc-b87d-0d2fd74f168f)
    21s (x8 over 6m21s)         Warning   ClusterControllerFailed       SGCluster/simple                                An error occurred while reconciling patroni configuration: Process with pattern ^[^ ]+ /usr/bin/patroni .*$ not found
    19s (x39 over 8m6s)         Normal  ClusterUpdated                  SGCluster/simple                                Cluster default.simple updated: StatefulSet:simple (+/metadata/creationTimestamp -> 2023-12-31T18:53:04Z), StatefulSet:simple (+/metadata/generation -> 1) and other 46 resources where patched
    ```
1. Logs:
    ```
    aht@localhost ~]$ kubectl logs simple-0 -c patroni

    …

    creating configuration files ... ok
    running bootstrap script ... ok
    2023-12-31 19:00:40.397 UTC [2142] FATAL:  password encryption failed: disabled for FIPS
    2023-12-31 19:00:40.397 UTC [2142] STATEMENT:  ALTER USER "postgres" WITH PASSWORD E'****-****-****-***';

    child process exited with exit code 1
    initdb: removing data directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data"
    2023-12-31 19:00:40,406 INFO: removing initialize key after failed attempt to bootstrap the cluster
    Traceback (most recent call last):
      File "/usr/bin/patroni", line 8, in <module>
        sys.exit(main())
      File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/patroni/__main__.py", line 345, in main
        return patroni_main(args.configfile)
      File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/patroni/__main__.py", line 239, in patroni_main
        abstract_main(Patroni, configfile)
      File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/patroni/daemon.py", line 174, in abstract_main
        controller.run()
      File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/patroni/__main__.py", line 194, in run
        super(Patroni, self).run()
      File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/patroni/daemon.py", line 143, in run
        self._run_cycle()
      File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/patroni/__main__.py", line 203, in _run_cycle
        logger.info(self.ha.run_cycle())
      File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/patroni/ha.py", line 1972, in run_cycle
        info = self._run_cycle()
      File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/patroni/ha.py", line 1785, in _run_cycle
        return self.post_bootstrap()
      File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/patroni/ha.py", line 1669, in post_bootstrap
        self.cancel_initialization()
      File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/patroni/ha.py", line 1662, in cancel_initialization
        raise PatroniFatalException('Failed to bootstrap cluster')
    patroni.exceptions.PatroniFatalException: Failed to bootstrap cluster
    performing post-bootstrap initialization …
    ```

### Expected Behaviour

Cluster should be created without issues.


### Possible Solution

The [`password_encryption`](https://postgresqlco.nf/doc/en/param/password_encryption) parameter is not explicitly being set to `scram-sha-256`, but it is the default value since Postgres 14 (and Postgres 16 has been tested here). Still, an explicit test can be performed by creating the following `SGPostgresConfig`:

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGPostgresConfig
metadata:
  name: pgconfig1
spec:
  postgresVersion: "16"
  postgresql.conf:
	password_encryption: 'scram-sha-256'
```
and referencing it from the `SGCluster`. However, results where the same, the cluster creation fails at the same step.

The problem seems to be that despite this default value, at some point an MD5 password is attempted to be created. Note that MD5 is forbidden in FIPS mode. That's why this same cluster creation (with or without the above Postgres configuration) works on a non-FIPS enabled cluster without a problem.

Examining this on a non-FIPS cluster, we note that `/etc/patroni/config.yml` contains:

```yaml
bootstrap:
  post_init: '/usr/local/bin/post-init.sh'

  initdb:
  - auth-host: md5
  - auth-local: trust
  - encoding: UTF8
  - locale: C.UTF-8
  - data-checksums
  pg_hba:
  - 'host all all 0.0.0.0/0 md5'
  - 'host replication replicator 0.0.0.0/0 md5'
```

So it appears that MD5 is being set at cluster bootstrap (initdb) as well as for `pg_hba.conf`. The latter should not be a problem, as according to [Postgres documentation on password authentication](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/auth-password.html) "_if md5 is specified as a method in pg_hba.conf but the user's password on the server is encrypted for SCRAM (see below), then SCRAM-based authentication will automatically be chosen instead_".

But the former probably is. At `initdb` time Postgres parameters are not configured yet, and probably if MD5 is explicitly requested it may be honored as such.

It is surprising that creating the cluster on a non-FIPS environment shows that SCRAM-SHA-256 is used despite this setting!

```
postgres=# table pg_authid ;
  oid  |           rolname           | rolsuper | rolinherit | rolcreaterole | rolcreatedb | rolcanlogin | rolreplication | rolbypassrls | rolconnlimit |           rolpassword                                   | rolvaliduntil                                                                               
-------+-----------------------------+----------+------------+---------------+-------------+-------------+----------------+--------------+--------------+---------------------------------------------------------+---------------
    10 | postgres                    | t        | t          | t             | t           | t           | t              | t            |           -1 | SCRAM-SHA-256$4096:************************************
 16384 | replicator                  | f        | t          | f             | f           | t           | t              | f            |           -1 | SCRAM-SHA-256$4096:************************************
 16385 | authenticator               | t        | t          | f             | f           | t           | f              | f            |           -1 | SCRAM-SHA-256$4096:************************************

```

I'm not an expert on Patroni's source code nor Python, but [here](https://github.com/zalando/patroni/blob/8acefefc4238b9d32cda2e8670ba53e212837c7c/patroni/postgresql/bootstrap.py) it is (probably) the relevant code being executed, and it may be creating the user twice (first with MD5, honoring the configuration request, and later with SCRAM-SHA-256 when the `password_encryption` value is honored).

Whatever the case is, it looks like these settings are hardcoding MD5 when they shouldn't. If I'm not mistaken, these settings are being generated from [`start-patroni.sh`](https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/blob/main/stackgres-k8s/src/operator/src/main/resources/templates/start-patroni.sh?ref_type=heads). To fix it, I propose to:

* Remove this hardcoding of MD5. Instead, we should use `scram-sha-256` as a default iif the user has not explicitly requested `md5` as a value for `password_encryption`. Alternatively, we may remove this parameter altogether if we can verify that this behaviour is Patroni's default (I'm not sure if this is the case, but can be tested).
* Also change the relevant lines in `.initdb.pg_hba` that reference to `md5` and replace them following the same logic as above.
* Remove/reconsider the use of `trust` also in `pg_hba` and use `peer` instead. This requires testing to ensure container is executed with the same `postgres` user so that `kubectl exec -it ... -c postgres-util -- psql` still works and doesn't break.


### Environment

- StackGres version: `1.7.0`, but also reported to happen on previous versions.
- Kubernetes version: `1.28` from K3s (see above).
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: VM with RHEL 8.5 with FIPS enabled (see above).

[DISCUSSION]
[jose_oss_pg]: cc: @teoincontatto

[ahachete]: Shouldn't this be considered a bug @teoincontatto ? In my understanding, we're enforcing MD5 passwords on default settings where SCRAM-SHA-256 is already the default, and this happens to "work" on non-FIPS but doesn't on FIPS.

Is it possible to fix this and issue a point release?

[teoincontatto]: Since patroni is in charge of running initdb I was looking into it. What comes out is an [issue with a similar problem](https://github.com/zalando/patroni/issues/1583).

I am OK with changing the default of `auth-host` to `scram-sha-256`. This is something that fix the configuration for this case but I wonder if we should allow some more configuration there. Maybe we could also add a way to configure more the initialization (like encoding and locale). Maybe a good fit for the password encryption is the SGPostgresConfig CRD where we could extract the value of `password_encryption`. As a second option for the value of password encryption and the value of encoding and locale we may create a new section under `SGCluster.spec.postgres.initdb`.

For a point release I would suggest to check if there is any workaround and, if not, perform the extra effort.

I think it is possible to create a workaround by adding the annotation `stackgres.io/reconciliation-pause: "true"` to the ConfigMap `<cluster name>-templates` and changing the `start-patroni.sh` manually by replacing `auth-host: md5` with `auth-host: scram-sha-256`, then deleting the cluster Pod should fix the issue. What do you think? Can you try it?

For other options, I agree we should have some additional configurability for `initdb` options, and I agree this should have a place in `SGCluster.spec.postgres.initdb`.

Let's treat this as two separate issues, the former as a bug fix addressed at the next point release, and the additional initdb configuration in the next major release?

[gcannata]: These are the detailed steps to apply the workaround:

1. Create an SGCluster with Helm:

`helm install -n NAMESPACE --creatre-namespace CLUSTER https://stackgres.io/downloads/stackgres-k8s/stackgres/1.7.0/helm/stackgres-cluster-demo.tgz`

2. Edit the ConfigMap of the SGCluster:

`kubectl edit -n NAMESPACE configMap CLUSTER-templates`

3. In the configMap just opened for editing add under metadata.annotations:

`stackgres.io/reconciliation-pause: "true"`

PS: is important to give a string and not a boolean otherwise it will fail

4. Always in the configMap just opened for editing change `auth-host` from

`auth-host: md5`

to

`auth-host: scram-sha-256`

5. Delete the SGCluster pod and now should be working right away.

Issue:
Support K8s snapshots in the web console
With the implementation of #2499, SG now provides SGClusters and SGShardedClusters with an `useVolumeSnapshot` flag that indicates if SGBackup should create backups using Volume Snapshots.

Optionally, user can specify the name of the `VolumeSnapshotClass` used to create the VolumeSnapshot (or simply choose to use the default one). Also, a `fastVolumeSnapshot` field is used to set the `fast` flag when calling the `pg_backup_start` function.

In order to support such features, we must include the following specs on SGClusters and SGShardedClusters forms and details, accordingly.

**For SGCluster:**

```yaml
kind: SGCluster
spec:
  configurations:
    backups:
    - sgStorageClass: <string>
      path: <string>
      useVolumeSnapshot: <boolean> # If specified SGBackup will use VolumeSnapshot to create backups. See also https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volume-snapshots/
      volumeSnapshotClass: <string> # It indicates the name of the VolumeSnapshotClass to use to create the VolumeSnapshot. If not set the default one will be used. See also https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volume-snapshots/
      fastVolumeSnapshot: <boolean> # If specified SGBackup will create a backup forcing a fast start (by setting parameter `fast` to `true` when calling `pg_backup_start`) that will reduce the time the backups may take at the expense of more IO usage. See also https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/continuous-archiving.html#BACKUP-LOWLEVEL-BASE-BACKUP
```

**For SGShardedCluster:**

```yaml
kind: SGShardedCluster
spec:
  configurations:
    backups:
    - sgStorageClass: <string>
      paths: [<string>]
      useVolumeSnapshot: <boolean> # If specified SGBackup will use VolumeSnapshot to create backups. See also https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volume-snapshots/
      volumeSnapshotClass: <string> # It indicates the name of the VolumeSnapshotClass to use to create the VolumeSnapshot. If not set the default one will be used. See also https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volume-snapshots/
      fastVolumeSnapshot: <boolean> # If specified SGBackup will create a backup forcing a fast start (by setting parameter `fast` to `true` when calling `pg_backup_start`) that will reduce the time the backups may take at the expense of more IO usage. See also https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/continuous-archiving.html#BACKUP-LOWLEVEL-BASE-BACKUP
```

Also, when an SGBackup is created using a VolumeSnapshot, the status of the SGBackup will have to include the `backup_label` and `tablespace_map` returned by `pg_backup_stop` function and the name of the VolumeSnapshot created. In such cases, the status will not include the `internalName`, `backupPath` and `sgBackupConfig` fields.

```yaml
kind: SGBackup
status:
  volumeSnapshot:
    name: <string> # The name of the VolumeSnapshot
    backupLabel: <string> # The content of `backup_label` column returned by `pg_backup_stop` encoded in Base64
    tablespaceMap: <string> # The content of `tablespace_map` column returned by `pg_backup_stop` encoded in Base64
```

- [ ] Include the corresponding fields on SGCluster form tests
- [ ] Implement the feature for SGShardedClusters
- [ ] Include the corresponding fields on SGShardedCluster form tests
- [ ] Implement the adjustments on SGBackups status

Ideally the Wal-G code would have a proper connection timeout.

Backup jobs don't hang forever. Failure is reported sooner.

apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1

```

```
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGBackup
spec:

Issue:
Configure Operator dynamically from the Web Console
### Problem to solve

Currently the operator can be installed and upgraded only using helm chart. There is a mechanism to install the operator using a YAML file but in such case the installation can no longer be upgraded properly.

We need a mechanism that allow to install StackGres properly from the StackGres Web Console

### Proposal

Create a functionality that allow to view and edit a global configuration of the operator and uses the StackGres REST API to get and update it.

### Testing

* Check Web Console is able to display the operator configuration
* Check Web Console is able to edit the operator configuration

## Acceptance Criteria

* [x] Implement the view of operator configuration
* [x] Implement the edition of operator configuration
* [ ] Test the view of operator configuration
* [ ] Test the edition of operator configuration

[DISCUSSION]
[teoincontatto]: The endpoints that will return and update the operator configuration object will use the structure of the SGConfig CRD.

Exists a YAML file with a possible structure that can be reused and with all the fields under section `SGConfig.spec` (for example `containerRegistry` will be `SGConfig.spec.containerRegistry`) that can be viewed and updated as the reference for the From and View: https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/blob/main/stackgres-k8s/install/helm/stackgres-operator/values.yaml

Another table of the parameters that will be configurable is: https://stackgres.io/doc/latest/install/helm/parameters/

[teoincontatto]: Some update here about the new CGConfig CRD that will be available in the StackGres REST API and will allow to modify StackGres installation configuration. Here is the latest SGConfig OpenAPI v3 Spec from the development branch [`2111-configure-operator-dynamically`](https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/tree/2111-configure-operator-dynamically?ref_type=heads): https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/blob/2111-configure-operator-dynamically/stackgres-k8s/src/common/src/main/resources/crds/SGConfig.yaml

Differently from an SGCluster resource the SGConfig should not be created or removed from the Web Console. It will be created during the installation of the StackGres Operator (or by the operator itself if it is configured to do so depending on the installation method). cc: @jorsol @jose_oss_pg @ldgarcia @ahachete

[teoincontatto]: My idea is to make this something generic and that allows for long queries results. In particular see [this comment](https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/issues/1782#note_962250934) for a proposal of the result (just the result).

[teoincontatto]: After rethinking this a bit I think we could change the returned type using JSON stream with the `application/x-ndjson` format. This way, if we will be able to extend this endpoint with any query in the future.

In particular the idea is to use the same concept used in the referenced comment:

```yaml
---
# this element is returned before the first tuple of each result set
resultSetIndex: <integer> # the current result set number (starting from 0)
fields:
- <string> # each for column
---
- <any> # each for column
```

But in `application/x-ndjson` format so that the root array elements are sent one by one instead of being wrapped in an real JSON array:

```json
{"resultSetIndex":<integer>,"fields":[<string>]}
[<any>]
[<any>]
[<any>]
{"resultSetIndex":<integer>,"fields":[<string>]}
[<any>]
[<any>]
[<any>]
[<any>]
[<any>]
```

When the returned element is an object then it is to be interpreted as carrying metadata (resultSet index and list of fields) and when it is an array it is simply a tuple.

@ldgarcia Do you think this would be feasible?

In any case we can still return the result also in `application/json` so that there is no need to change the code that parse the response into JSON.

[DISCUSSION]
[dan.pretselman]: This runbook will show you how to setup [Citus](https://www.citusdata.com/) extension on Stackgres clusters.

Let's assume that the final layout will have one Coordinator cluster and 2 Worker clusters.

Follow the steps below:

1. Install the Citus extension **on each cluster**,  
   this can be done in the Stackgres Web Console under "extensions" tab  
   or by adding the Citus extension to the `spec:` section in the `SGCluster` CRD of your clusters:  

  ```
  apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
  kind: SGCluster
  metadata:
    name: your-cluster-name
    # ...
  spec:
    # ..
    postgres:
      extensions:
      - name: citus
        publisher: com.ongres
        repository: https://extensions.stackgres.io/postgres/repository
        version: your-citus-version   #for example: 11.0-2
  # ..
  ```  
   **Note:** Adjust the Cluster name and Citus version to desired and available version

2. Add the Citus extension to `shared_preload_libraries` configuration variable in `postgresql.conf` **in each cluster.**  
   It can be done through the Stackgres Web Console by adjusting the Postgres Configuration that used in the cluster  
   or by adding the Citus extension to the `shared_preload_libraries` under `specs:`, `postgresql.conf:` section  
   in clusters `SGPostgresConfig` CRD.
```
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGPostgresConfig
#..
spec:
  #..
  postgresql.conf:
    #..
    shared_preload_libraries: citus, pg_stat_statements, auto_explain
    #..
```
**Note:** that citus must be at the beginning of `shared_preload_libraries`.

 3. Restart the clusters after adjusting the `shared_preload_libraries`.

 4. Create the extension **on every database and every cluster** where you want to use Citus,  
    by executing the command below in the desired database:  

    ```create extension citus;``` 

 5. By default, the worker nodes/clusters will try to use encrypted communication(SSL),  
    If you choose not to configure SSL, you need to permit the worker nodes not to use SSL.  

    It can be done through the Stackgres Web Console by adjusting the Postgres Configuration that used in the cluster   
    or by adding `citus.node_conninfo='sslmode=prefer'` under `specs:`, `postgresql.conf:` section  
    in clusters `SGPostgresConfig` CRD.  
```
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGPostgresConfig
#..
spec:
  #..
  postgresql.conf:
    #..
    citus.node_conninfo: sslmode=prefer
    #..
```

 6. Configure the [authentication ](https://docs.citusdata.com/en/stable/develop/api_metadata.html?highlight=pg_dist_authinfo&_gl=1*po0f0*_ga*MTk3MDAyMzk2LjE2NTY3MDk0ODQ.*_ga_DS5S1RKEB7*MTY1Nzc1NzE2MC42LjAuMTY1Nzc1NzE2MC4w#connection-credentials-table)used by Citus worker nodes to connect to one another.  
    Add a record to citus `pg_dist_authinfo` table that will hold the authentication parameters,  
    for the simplicity, let's say we want to use `postgres` sql user,  
    in such case, populate the pg_dist_authinfo` table as below   

    nodeid = 0, means we will use the `postgres` user to connect to each worker node/cluster 

    Execute on the **coordinator** cluster/node **only**  
    `insert into pg_dist_authinfo(nodeid,rolename,authinfo)`
     `values(0, 'postgres', 'password=xyz');`  


    **Note:** Replace "xyz" with the actual password for postgres user,  
              assuming same password is used in the related worker clusters.  
              If you want to use different passwords on each cluster, you can change the passwords  
              and update this table with specific nodeIds and passwords afterward you add the nodes.  

 7. **Only** on the coordinator cluster execute the Citus UDFs below on the desired database:  

     a. Set the coordinator:  

       ``` select citus_set_coordinator_host('$your-coordinator-cluster-node', 5432); ```  

       **Note:** Replace $your-coordinator-cluster-node with the actual hostname.  

     b. Set the worker nodes, execute the UDF below for each worker cluster,  
        in our case we have 2 worker clusters/nodes, so we will run:  

        select * from citus_add_node('workercluster#1', 5432);  
        select * from citus_add_node('workercluster#2', 5432);  
  
      **Note:** Replace workercluster#1/workercluster#2 with the actual hostnames of the worker clusters.  

 8. Verify the installation by running the command below on the database on the coordinator cluster:

Add support to K8s snapshots in StackGres

The objective of this issue is to gather information to implement support to K8s snapshots for StackGres.
 
The current URL that support from Kubernetes on snapshots is : https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volume-snapshots/
 
``` 
In Kubernetes, a VolumeSnapshot represents a snapshot of a volume on a storage system.
 
This document assumes that you are already familiar with Kubernetes persistent volumes.
```

**Proposal**

The proposal is to have new field `useVolumeSnapshot` and `volumeSnapshotClass` under `SGCluster.spec.configurations.backups` section that indicate if SGBackup should create backups using VolumeSnapshot and, optionally, specify the name of the VolumeSnapshotClass to use to create the VolumeSnapshot (or use the default one). This configuration will live together with the `sgStorageClass` and `path` configuration since WAL archiving will continue to use it to archive WAls and is required in order to restore the SGBackup properly. Field `fastVolumeSnapshot` is used to set the `fast` flag when calling the `pg_backup_start` function.

For SGCluster:

```yaml
kind: SGCluster
spec:
  configurations:
    backups:
    - sgStorageClass: <string>
      path: <string>
      useVolumeSnapshot: <boolean> # If specified SGBackup will use VolumeSnapshot to create backups. See also https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volume-snapshots/
      volumeSnapshotClass: <string> # It indicates the name of the VolumeSnapshotClass to use to create the VolumeSnapshot. If not set the default one will be used. See also https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volume-snapshots/
      fastVolumeSnapshot: <boolean> # If specified SGBackup will create a backup forcing a fast start (by setting parameter `fast` to `true` when calling `pg_backup_start`) that will reduce the time the backups may take at the expense of more IO usage. See also https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/continuous-archiving.html#BACKUP-LOWLEVEL-BASE-BACKUP
```

For SGShardedCluster:


```yaml
kind: SGShardedCluster
spec:
  configurations:
    backups:
    - sgStorageClass: <string>
      paths: [<string>]
      useVolumeSnapshot: <boolean> # If specified SGBackup will use VolumeSnapshot to create backups. See also https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volume-snapshots/
      volumeSnapshotClass: <string> # It indicates the name of the VolumeSnapshotClass to use to create the VolumeSnapshot. If not set the default one will be used. See also https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volume-snapshots/
      fastVolumeSnapshot: <boolean> # If specified SGBackup will create a backup forcing a fast start (by setting parameter `fast` to `true` when calling `pg_backup_start`) that will reduce the time the backups may take at the expense of more IO usage. See also https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/continuous-archiving.html#BACKUP-LOWLEVEL-BASE-BACKUP
```

When an SGBackup is created using a VolumeSnapshot the status of the SGBackup will have to include the `backup_label` and `tablespace_map` returned by `pg_backup_stop` function and the name of the VolumeSnapshot created. Also, in this case, the status will not include the `internalName`, `backupPath` and `sgBackupConfig` fields.

```yaml
kind: SGBackup
status:
  volumeSnapshot:
    name: <string> # The name of the VolumeSnapshot
    backupLabel: <string> # The content of `backup_label` column returned by `pg_backup_stop` encoded in Base64
    tablespaceMap: <string> # The content of `tablespace_map` column returned by `pg_backup_stop` encoded in Base64
```

- [ ] Describe the tests that will be implementes

[DISCUSSION]
[teoincontatto]: After including [csi-driver-host-path](https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/csi-driver-host-path) into kind I was able to test snapshotting against a running SGCluster and recover it successfully.

## Backup with VolumeSnapshot

Despite the PoC was completely manual it should then be possible to include the snapshotting as an option for SGBackup so that the user will see it as an alternative method. The proposal is to have new field `useVolumeSnapshot` and `volumeSnapshotClass` under `SGCluster.spec.configurations.backups` section that indicate if SGBackup should create backups using VolumeSnapshot and, optionally, specify the name of the VolumeSnapshotClass to use to create the VolumeSnapshot (or use the default one). This configuration will live together with the `sgStorageClass` and `path` configuration since WAL archiving will continue to use it to archive WAls and is required in order to restore the SGBackup properly. This should show better the proposed change:

```yaml
kind: SGCluster
spec:
  configurations:
    backups:
    - sgStorageClass: <string>
      path: <string>
      useVolumeSnapshot: <booleab> # If specified SGBackup will use VolumeSnapshot to create backups. See also https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volume-snapshots/
      volumeSnapshotClass: <string> # It indicates the name of the VolumeSnapshotClass to use to create the VolumeSnapshot. If not set the default one will be used. See also https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volume-snapshots/
```

The backup procedure will require to use the [Postgres low level API to make base backups](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/continuous-archiving.html#BACKUP-LOWLEVEL-BASE-BACKUP) calling the function `SELECT pg_backup_start(label => '<SGBackup name>', fast => false)` before the snapshot is taken and calling the function `SELECT * FROM pg_backup_stop(wait_for_archive => true)` after the backup is completed and the `backup_label` and `tablespace_map` columns returned by this function (that will be included as files with the same names in the folder where backup get restored) should be included in the SGBackup along with the name of the VolumeSnapshot created. Seems that `archive_mode` have to be set to `always` in order for this method to work properly.

When an SGBackup is created using a VolumeSnapshot the status of the SGBackup will have to include the `backup_label` and `tablespace_map` returned by `pg_backup_stop` function and the name of the VolumeSnapshot created. Also, in this case, the status will not include the `internalName`, `backupPath` and `sgBackupConfig` fields. Here is a proposal:

```yaml
kind: SGBackup
status:
  volumeSnapshot:
    name: <string> # The name of the VolumeSnapshot
    backupLabel: <string> # The content of `backup_label` column returned by `pg_backup_stop` encoded in Base64
    tablespaceMap: <string> # The content of `tablespace_map` column returned by `pg_backup_stop` encoded in Base64
```

The VolumeSnapshot created will be owned by the SGBackup so that when the latter is removed the backups is also removed automatically.

The current reconciliation of SGBackup uses wal-g that remove old WALs and old backups. When using VolumeSnapshot the logic to clean old WAL and backups will have to change in order to free up the space correctly for both. Also, if the user switch back to use the SGObjectStorage for SGBackup there are chances that WAL required by an older backup done with a VolumeSnapshot are removed so we need some mechanism to prevent that. 

## Restore a VolumeSnaphot

The restore procedure will require to create the PersistentVolumeClaim that reference the VolumeSnapshot for the Pod 0 before the StatefulSet is created and the StatefulSet must not set `StatefulSet.spec.podManagementPolicy` to be `OrderedReady` before Patroni bootstrap is completed. Also the `start-patroni.sh` script will include the logic to create the `backup_label` and `tablespace_map` files in the data folder.

### Summary

I've upgraded the Stackgres Operator to v1.6.0 (via Helm). Everything went fine. I restarted all Postgres clusters maintained by the operator afterwards. 

Now I'm trying to perform a major upgrade from Postgres 14 to 15. I've tried 14.6 to 15.5, this didn't work. I tried a Minor upgrade from 14.6 to 14.9, which was successful, and then a Major upgrade from 14.9 to 15.5. Same errors.

I tried it both with `Hard link files` enabled and disabled. After failure the rollback finished successfully. 

### Current Behaviour 

Major upgrade won't work with Postgres extensions installed.

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a SGCluster
2. Intall extensions, e.g. `timescale_tsl` or `pg_stat_kcache`
3. Perform a major upgrade from Postgres 14.x to 15.x

Install extensions via the SGCluster manifest:
```
  postgres:
    extensions:
    - name: timescaledb_tsl
      publisher: com.ongres
      version: 2.11.0
    - name: pg_stat_kcache
      publisher: com.ongres
      version: 2.2.1
```

### Expected Behaviour

Upgrade successful. 

### Possible Solution

It seems something goes wrong when installing the extensions in the new Postgres version. It successfully downloads the extension, but fails when installing them. 

### Environment

- StackGres version: v1.6.0
- Kubernetes version: v1.26.7

[timvandruenen]: Whole day of testing.. :slight_smile: haha.

Seems the issue, at least for us, is only present when SSL is enabled in the SGCluster definition. So:
```
spec:
  postgres:
    ssl:
      enabled: false
```
Does work, but:
```
spec:
  postgres:
    ssl:
      enabled: true
      certificateSecretKeySelector:
        name: postgres-cert
        key: tls.crt
      privateKeySecretKeySelector:
        name: postgres-cert
        key: tls.key
```
Fails.

We use cert-manager certs for our Postgres instances. We use a ClusterIssuer (self-signed) in combination with a Certificate per SGCluster. We don't have anything like trust-manager (https://cert-manager.io/docs/trust/trust-manager/) or KPI so the certs remain seen as "self-signed" by services. So they enable a flag like `insecure tls`.

The above is tested with Stackgres v1.5.0. I'll perform the test with v1.6.0 now as wel.

Issue:
Enable specifying of pod priority class for resources
### Problem to solve

In a cluster operating at capacity limits it can happen that database or other pods like backups can not be scheduled.

Currently there is no way in the SGCluster to pass the [`priorityClassName`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/pod-priority-preemption/) field to the pod specification.
Also patching the StatefulSet does not work because the Operator will revert any changes when reconciling the CR.

### Further details

The ability to specify pod priorities ensures that:

* DB Pods will be schedulable (by preempting lower priority pods if necessary)
* DB Pods will not be evicted from a node before all lower priority pods have been evicted.

### Proposal

The value to pass is a simple string value and could be added as field to the pods `scheduling` object, e.g.:

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGCluster
metadata: {}
spec:
  # ...
  pods: 
    scheduling:
      nodeAffinity: {}
      #...
      priorityClassName: databases
```

### Testing

Primary risk is that creation of StatefulSets Deployments and Jobs could (or will) be rejected by the API-Server if the given priority class does not exist.

## Acceptance Criteria

StatefulSets/Deployments/Jobs specify a `priorityClassName` in their pod template spec.

### Links / references

https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/pod-priority-preemption/

Issue:
Configure Operator dynamically from the REST API
### Problem to solve

Currently the operator can be installed and upgraded only using helm chart. There is a mechanism to install the operator using a YAML file but in such case the installation can no longer be upgraded properly.

We need a mechanism that allow to install StackGres properly from any medium (YAML, helm, kustomizer, etc.) and also to allow a dynamic configuration to be performed from the Kubernetes API, StackGres REST API.

### Proposal

Create an installer / upgrader that is capable of detecting change in the configuration and upgrade the operator on the fly without disrupting functionality (except in some cases like version upgrade or certificate upgrade).

Create a REST API endpoint that allow to read and change a global configuration of the operator.

The installer's corner cases should be documented properly:

* During upgrade of the operator version the clusters functionality may be interrupted
* During upgrade of the certificated the clusters functionality may be interrupted

### Testing

* Check that the installer is able to install everything from scratch
* Check that the installer is able to upgrade any configuration parameter
* Check that the installer provide a default configuration (like current helm)
* Check that the installer interfere the minimum possible with the running clusters while updating things (expect some corner cases like upgrading the operator version)
* Check REST API endpoint is able to read the configuration
* Check REST API endpoint is able to write and validate the configuration

## Acceptance Criteria

* Implement the installer
* Test installer
* Implement the REST API
* Test REST API

In order to validate stackgres resource creation an update, we have used a [custom validation webhook](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/extensible-admission-controllers/). 
Validating webhooks require to use SSL even if the validating endpoint is inside the cluster. 
The SSL certificates are installed in the cluster as secrets and then, are provided to the operator as a volume. 
In the case that a certificate is self-signed, it needs to be provided as a caBundle to the validating webhook, which is no other thing than the operator's SSL certificate encoded in base64. 

Whatever certificate are we using, it is going to expire at some point. Which could become a painful task unless we provide an easy way to do it. 

### Further details

A self-signed certificate may require to be manually distributed across the cluster. 
Check this page for details: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/certificates/#distributing-self-signed-ca-certificate

Automating the certificate rotation could encourge our users to follow good practices in terms of certificates administration. If the SSL rotation becomes a painful task, our users may feel tempted to follow bad practices in order to avoid the task. 

It could help to fix a potential problem that a certificate may have, by allow to the cluster admin to concentrate only on the SSL certificate content, and not in the certificate distribution.  

### Proposal

This could be a series of alternatives of implementation: 

- Ideally we could use a helm helper to automate the process, by using an upgrade task.
- A Single run job that executes a program that update those tasks.  
- We could create a script that take the certificate from some folder and install it across the cluster. 

### Testing
A failure on this process migth cause that the validation webhook cannot perform validations, in which case stackgres may not be able to create new clusters.

[DISCUSSION]
[ahachete]: Consider using [cert-manager](https://github.com/jetstack/cert-manager). In this case, it would need to be declared as an operator dependency, similarly to what Prometheus is now for StackGres.

[simon.beck]: We just ran into the problem that the webhook cert expired.

Classify as SMELL or NO_SMELL based on whether it describes architectural problems.

CPU and MEMORY parameters both are updated with the new values but the values of the `initContainers` are not updated and this leads to problems when you try to bootstrap a cluster with that instance profile if you do not have enough resources, your pods will stay in a `Pending` state. 


#### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an Instance profile with high values of `cpu` and `memory` 
2. Edit your Instance profile to lower CPU and memory values. 
3. Check the yaml generated and you'll see that after editing it the iniContainer values will remain with the initial values.

### Expected Behaviour

The instance profile is updated according to the new values supplied.

[DISCUSSION]
[teoincontatto]: @kadaffy This is the expected behavior, if you want to reset those sections with default values you will have to remove them also. The idea is that the default is based on the initial value but then you may change it to whatever you want, if you want to change CPU and MEMORY without affecting containers and init containers resource requirements you should allowed to do so.

[kadaffy]: @teoincontatto The problem is that if you update the CPU and RAM to a lower values, the init containers remain with the initial size specified and this can lead to the cluster not being initialized due to the lack of resources and is very confusing to troubleshoot because those initContainers values are set by the operator and not the user.

[teoincontatto]: Again, this is expected since the value are set only if they are not already specified. In case you want the operator to set them to the default you have to remove the value that are specified. But the user may also provide such values. I'd like to propose some changes to the SGShardedCluster implemented in ~"target_version::1.5.0-beta1".

We need to add much more configuration from the SGCluster to the SGShardedCluster for both coordinator and shards. In particular:

* scheduling
* metadata
* extensions
* ssl
* replication
* customVolumes and customContainers
* postgresServices for any coordinator, primary coordinator and any primary shard
* disableConnectionPooling, disableMetricsExporter and disablePostgresUtil
* resources
* credentials
* managementPolicy
* managedSql
* distributedLogs
* backups

More or less all those are straightforward changes and could be implemented easily with just checking the spec is applied as is to the generated SGCluster.

It is a non goal of this issue to add support for replicas service, backups, initialData and replicateFrom. Those developments have to go in separate standalone issues since they require to provide a PoC, some testing and, maybe, some support on other CRD (like SGBackup).

Another proposal we need to address is to provide specific configuration overrides for individual sharded clusters. The proposal to achieve that is to create a new section called `.spec.shards.overrides`. It will be an array of object where each object will allow any field already available in the `.spec.shards` section with the only exception of the `clusters` field. A new field `index` of each object in the array of the new field `.spec.shards.overrides` will indicate the shard to which the specified configuration overrides will apply. This section, if not specified, will indicate that all shards have the same configurations as specified in the `.spec.shards` section.

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1alpha1
kind: SGShardedCluster
spec:
  postgres: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.postgres
  replication: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.replication but without role and groups
  postgresServices:
    coordinator:
      any: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.postgresServices.* but without customPorts
      primary: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.postgresServices.* but without customPorts
      customPorts: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.postgresServices.*.customPorts
    shards:
      anyPrimary: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.postgresServices.* but without customPorts
      customPorts: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.postgresServices.*.customPorts
  configurations:
    credentials: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.configurations.credentials
    backups: # Same as SGCluster.spec.configurations.backups but without the .path and with .paths 
      - paths: [ <string> ] # set and updated automatically by the operator
  metadata: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.metadata
  coordinator:
    instances: 2
    managedSql: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.managedSql
    replication: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.replication override SGShardedCluster.spec.replication
    configurations: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.configurations excluding backups and credentials
    pods: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.pods
    metadata: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.metadata override SGShardedCluster.spec.metadata
  shards:
    cluster: 2
    instancesPerCluster: 2
    sgInstanceProfile: size-s
    managedSql: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.managedSql
    replication: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.replication override SGShardedCluster.spec.replication
    configurations: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.configurations excluding backups and credentials
    pods: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.pods
    metadata: {} # same as SGCluster.spec.metadata override SGShardedCluster.spec.metadata
    overrides: # every thing under here override SGShardedCluster.spec.shards (do not include .clusters and .overrides)
      index: 0
      instancesPerCluster: 3
      sgInstanceProfile: size-l
```

Second, this is for client connections. Intra-cluster connections (coordinators to workers) are a separate thing. And potentially should be configurable too. For intra-cluster we should allow the options:
* No SSL.
* SSL with client certificates automatically generated.

I don't think we need to go beyond this. But I'd like to have the second option (SSL with client certificates automatically generated) be **the default**, as this is a Citus best practice.

From the worker's Postgres perspective it's just a "client" connection, not a replication one (in any case). So it's like an user connecting, albeit a special one. Only needs to be enabled on the workers (and the coordinators to have the client certificate, obviously).

Currently we provide an SSL configuration under `SGCluster.spec.ssl` with `certificateSecretKeySelector` and `privateKeySecretKeySelector` sections.

You say that intra-cluster connections are a separate thing but it is not really clear to me if we should set a different certificate and private key for those connections respect to user connections.

We may add an optional `caSecretKeySelector` to enable `validate-ca` mode. `validate-full` mode is quite a bit more complicated to setup so that I would not support it for now. Also we could add there an `autoGenerate` flag that indicate that the certificates and the private key (and the CA) will be generated automatically.

So, we may simply use that same ssl configuration for citus too. The setup should be quite simple by setting the following configuration:

ALTER SYSTEM SET citus.node_conninfo =

```
