If you created the instance with the Google Cloud Console do the following:

* Get the instance configuration:

```
gcloud compute instances export "$INSTANCE_NAME"   --destination=/tmp/openshift-crc.yaml   --zone="$INSTANCE_ZONE"
```

* Add the advanced configuration to enable nested vistualization to the /tmp/openshift-crc.yaml file:

```yaml
advancedMachineFeatures:
  enableNestedVirtualization: true
```

* Update the instance configuration and restart the instance

```
gcloud compute instances update-from-file "$INSTANCE_NAME"   --source=/tmp/openshift-crc.yaml   --most-disruptive-allowed-action=RESTART   --zone="$INSTANCE_ZONE"
```

* Check virtualization is enabled by running the following command in the instance (output should not be 0):

```
grep -cw vmx /proc/cpuinfo
```

Following steps have been performed in order to set up the instance to run CRC and the StackGres E2E tests:

* Set up user:
    * SSH using the google cloud console
    * `sudo usermod -G google-sudoers -a "$USER"`
    * `sudo usermod -G dbus -a "$USER"`
    * `echo "<your public SSH key>" > ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
    * chmod 400 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
* For next steps use SSH with the private SSH key associated to the user that have been configured in previous step
* Create a disk partition formatted with ext4 to mount ~/.crc folder since the Fedora image set the partition with a 10GB disk template:
    * `sudo fdisk /dev/sda` then `n` select all defaults and `w`
    * `sudo mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda6`
    * `mkdir ~/.crc`
    * `sudo mount /dev/sda6 ~/.crc`
* Install following packages:
    * `sudo yum install -y NetworkManager git wget curl jq docker pip`
    * `sudo usermod -G docker -a matteom`
    * `sudo pip install yq`
    * `sudo wget -q -O /usr/local/bin/kubectl "https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.21.3/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl" && sudo chmod a+x /usr/local/bin/kubectl`
    * `wget https://get.helm.sh/helm-v3.9.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz -O - | sudo tar xz --strip-components=1 -C /usr/local/bin -f - "linux-amd64/helm"`
    * `wget https://github.com/derailed/k9s/releases/download/v0.25.18/k9s_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz -O - | sudo tar xzf - -C /usr/local/bin/ k9s`

[teoincontatto]: The reason why it is so hard to test StackGres on top of CRC (and maybe any OpenShift cluster) is that the default PV recycling mechanism is broken. The Pod that should recycle the PV by remove the data after it is Released throws some weird permission denied errors on some files that, if running the same command on the node, are deleted as expected. I am trying to write some workaround in order to delete such data by connecting directly to the node so that when a PV is in Failed status (due to the error mentioned) it clean up the data correctly and wait for the Pod to re-try the operation that will complete since the permission denied error goes away. Something like:

```
while true
do
  kubectl get pv -o json --watch \
    | jq --unbuffered -r '.metadata.name + " " + .status.phase' \
    | while read -r PV PHASE
      do
        echo "$PV $PHASE"
        if [ "$PHASE" = Failed ]
        then
          echo "Cleaning up $PV"
          E2E_ENV=crc sh ~/stackgres/stackgres-k8s/e2e/e2e crc_run_on_node \
            sh -xc "ls -1 /mnt/pv-data/$PV | while read -r DIR; do rm -rf /mnt/pv-data/$PV/\$DIR; done"
        fi
      done
done
```

[teoincontatto]: Finally, using [Rancher local path storage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rancher/local-path-provisioner/v0.0.22/deploy/local-path-storage.yaml) and executing `~/.crc/bin/oc/oc debug -q "$(kubectl get node -o name | head -n 1)" -- setenforce 0` allow to get rid of the buggy OpenShift pre-created PVs (and the above script) also allowing volume expansion required to pass some E2E tests

### Problem to solve

We would like to use [cert-manager](https://cert-manager.io/) issued TLS certificates instead of passing our own in via values.yaml or using a self-signed certificate.

### Further details

This would considerably ease Operations on our side as we already have a working cert-manager installation in all of our clusters.

### Proposal

I think the first step would be to generate the self-signed certificates as a `kubernetes.io/tls` Secret that matches the format that cert-manager creates:

```
apiVersion: v1
data:
  ca.crt: <ca-cert>
  tls.crt: <tls-cert>
  tls.key: <tls-key>
kind: Secret
metadata:
  annotations:
  name: test-tls-cert
  namespace: test
type: kubernetes.io/tls
```

After that I believe we would want a flag in values.yaml that would allow us to easily turn off cert generation:

```
cert:
  auto_generate: true
```

I think we would also probably want to be able to name the Secret that would get volume mounted?

If you know of a workaround here I am all ears. I searched through the docs and Issues and couldn't find anything relevant.

### Testing

<!-- What risks does this change pose? How might it affect the quality of the product?  -->


## Acceptance Criteria

* [x] Allow to use an already existent secrets for both operator and REST API
* [x] Add a flag in order to create cert manager custom resources that allow to create the operator secret automatically
* [x] Tests
### Links / references

[DISCUSSION]
[teoincontatto]: Hi @pobrien!

This is a nice ~"Feature Request". From what I see this is partially supported by the new flag `cert.reset` (starting from ~"target_version::1.3.0") that skip overwriting the cert if already created but it does not work when installing, only for upgrades. So we need to create another flag like `cert.create` that allows to skip certificate creation always.

Another thing that should be implemented is the usage of a TLS Secret and not a generic one since the keys we currently use are not `tls.crt` and `tls.key` but `server.crt` and `root.key`.

There is another certificate for the Web Console and REST API and an RSA key pair to sign and read JWT stored in another Secret. We may extend this feature request to have TLS Secret for that too.

Issue:
Allow specify request and limit in sginstanceprofile for non-production
Currently sginstanceprofile only allow to specify a single value for cpu and memory that will be used for both request and limit each of those resources.

Some non-production environment requires to specify both to make it possible to create a cluster that can be deployed in node with less resources and are not critical environment.

Proposed change for the `SGInstanceProfile` CRD to allow to specify a request for resources different from the limit:

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGInstanceProfile
spec:
  cpu: <string> # CPU(s) (cores) limit for every Pod of an `SGCluster`. Please note that
     # every Pod contains not only the `patroni` (Patroni and Postgres) container, but
     # several other sidecar containers. While the majority of the resources are
     # devoted to the main Postgres container, some CPU is needed for the
     # sidecars.
     # 
     # The number of cores set is applied only to the `patroni` container of each Pod while the
     # other sidecars will not be subjected to any resource restriction.
     # 
     # A minimum of 2 cores is recommended.
  memory: <string> # RAM limit for every Pod of an `SGCluster`. The suffix `Mi` or `Gi`
     # specifies Mebibytes or Gibibytes, respectively. Please note that every
     # Pod contains not only the `patroni` (Patroni and Postgres) container, but several
     # other sidecar containers. While the majority of the resources are devoted
     # to the main Postgres container, some RAM is needed for the sidecars.
     # 
     # The amount of RAM set is applied only to the `patroni` container of each Pod while the
     # other sidecars will not be subjected to any resource restriction.
     # 
     # A minimum of 2-4Gi is recommended.
  requests:
    cpu: <string> # CPU(s) (cores) requested for every Pod of an `SGCluster`. Please note that
       # every Pod contains not only the `patroni` (Patroni and Postgres) container, but
       # several other sidecar containers. While the majority of the resources are
       # devoted to the main Postgres container, some CPU is needed for the
       # sidecars.
       # 
       # The number of cores set is applied only to the `patroni` container of each Pod while the
       # other sidecars will not be subjected to any resource restriction.
       # 
       # A minimum of 2 cores is recommended.
       #
       # If not specified or if field `.spec.nonProductionOptions.enableInstanceProfileRequests`
       # is not set to `true` in the associated `SGCluster` will be equals to `.spec.cpu`.
    memory: <string> # RAM requested for every Pod of an `SGCluster`. The suffix `Mi` or `Gi`
       # specifies Mebibytes or Gibibytes, respectively. Please note that every
       # Pod contains not only the `patroni` (Patroni and Postgres) container, but several
       # other sidecar containers. While the majority of the resources are devoted
       # to the main Postgres container, some RAM is needed for the sidecars.
       # 
       # The amount of RAM set is applied only to the `patroni` container of each Pod while the
       # other sidecars will not be subjected to any resource restriction.
       # 
       # A minimum of 2-4Gi is recommended.
       #
       # If not specified or if field `.spec.nonProductionOptions.enableInstanceProfileRequests`
       # is not set to `true` in the associated `SGCluster` will be equals to `.spec.memory`.
```

The fields `.spec.requests.cpu` and `.spec.requests.memory` will be optional and their values will be the same as respectively `.spec.cpu` and `.spec.memory` if the former are not specified.

A flag `enableInstanceProfileRequests` will be added under section `.spec.nonProductionOptions` in `SGCluster` in order to be able to use the new proposed fields of `SGInstanceProfile`.

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGCluster
spec:
  nonProductionOptions:
    enableInstanceProfileRequests: <boolean> # If true, will allow to use fields `.spec.requests.cpu` and `.spec.requests.memory` from `SGInstanceProfile`. By default is `false`.
```

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Implement the feature
- [ ] Test the feature
- [ ] Create issue for UI @jose_oss_pg TODO

[xaviersierra]: @teoincontatto Can you provide an example of what you have in mind? Like a CRD a sample. 

Also, can you explain how this could help in test environments?

[teoincontatto]: > @teoincontatto Can you provide an example of what you have in mind? Like a CRD a sample.

The idea is to provide the value for cpu and memory as commonly expressed in a Pod:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: frontend
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: images.my-company.example/app:v4
    resources:
      requests:
        memory: "64Mi"
        cpu: "250m"
      limits:
        memory: "128Mi"
        cpu: "500m"
  - name: log-aggregator
    image: images.my-company.example/log-aggregator:v6
    resources:
      requests:
        memory: "64Mi"
        cpu: "250m"
      limits:
        memory: "128Mi"
        cpu: "500m"
```

Not sure how to express that in our current sginstanceprofile CRD without generating to much incompatibilities but we could do something like:

```yaml
---
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGInstanceProfile
metadata:
  name: size-s-staging
  namespace: default
spec:
  # cpu: '1'
  # memory: 2Gi
  requests:
    memory: "1Gi"
    cpu: "500m"
  limits:
    memory: "2Gi"
    cpu: "1"
```

Where `.spec.cpu` and `.spec.memory` are mutually exclusive with `.spec.requests` and `.spec.limits`. 

> Also, can you explain how this could help in test environments?

This was something that comes from an user request but I am not sure the exact use case they where having.

IMO testing and/or staging environments could have less resources than production environment and therefore they have less capacity. This feature would allow for instance, to put more PostgreSQL instances in the same node maintaining the resources limits. In order to test some functionality this would permit to afford short resources spikes that the resources requested (simulating a production environment) but enforcing that the PostgreSQL instances are never using more resources than the specified limit.

[xaviersierra]: I undertand, in order to not introduce any breaking change, we could use a CR like this:

``` yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGInstanceProfile
metadata:
  name: size-s-staging
  namespace: default
spec:
  cpu: '1'
  memory: 2Gi
  requests:
    memory: "1Gi"
    cpu: "500m"

```

In which the requests object is optional, and if not specified will use the same values as there is in `.spec.cpu` and `.spec.memory.` 

This would allow old CRs to still working the same way, and at the same we can introduce new functionality.

### Summary

CABundle attached to the mutatingwebhookconfiguration's for stackgres is replaced every time ArgoCD is sync'd.

### Current Behaviour 

Every time that a Sync happens in ArgoCD all of the Jobs as part of the Stackgres Helm Chart are run. I believe this causes a new CABundle to get created and the MutatingWebhookConfigurations to get updated with that new CABundle.

This results in the dreaded `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` error through the UI and when manipulating SGClusters on the CLI.

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Install ArgoCD. We are currently testing on 2.1.x
2. Install Stackgres Helm Chart via ArgoCD. See our values.yaml file below.
3. Once ArgoCD creates all of the Stackgres objects, hit the Sync button
4. The mutatingwebhookconfiguration's cabundle will be updated and UI/CLI operations will error out

### Expected Behaviour

We expect that certs to stay the same and not cause TLS issues.

### Possible Solution

<!-- What do you think is the possible solution for the bug -->

I may be wrong on some details here, but I think Implementing https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/issues/1841 would help address this issue.

Since we're not passing in a cert or key via Helm Values (since this is GitOps and we don't want the cert and key in a git repository) the chart tries to do the friendly thing and generate the CA, cert, and key so everything can be TLS'd. If we could pass in a secretKeyRef that points to a `kubernetes.io/tls` Secret this could all be avoided, I would think.

I suspect at the heart of this issue is that ArgoCD isn't running `helm install` or `helm upgrade` like the chart expects, instead it's doing a `helm template` so I believe all of the install/upgrade jobs are running every time there is an ArgoCD Sync, and this ends up updating the mutatingwebhookconfiguration. This also causes the auto-generated admin password to be updated each time, which more than anything can be confusing.

[sebawebber]: Regarding the password being rewritten every upgrade/install, there is a solution: manually creating the secret and referencing it in the helm configuration, like this:

```yaml
## export SGUSER=admin SGPASSWORD='my-super-password-goes-here' ; 
## kubectl create secret generic -n stackgres sg-ui-secret  --from-literal=k8sUsername=${SGUSER} --from-literal="password=$(echo -n "${SGUSER}${SGPASSWORD}" | openssl dgst -sha256)" ;
## kubectl label secret -n stackgres sg-ui-secret 'api.stackgres.io/auth=user' --overwrite=true
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: sg-ui-secret
  namespace: stackgres

  ## labels should be added manually
  labels:
    api.stackgres.io/auth: user
data:
  k8sUsername: YWRtaW4=
  password: OGU0MGMzZDM0ZDM4NzMxMTEyYzZlOWYxODljODkzYjQwZjQ2NGUyYTNiNDdkODk0NjFkYTBhNzhiOTZkNTQwOQ==
type: Opaque
```
> After creating the secret, be sure to add the label with the command below:
> ```bash
> kubectl label secret -n stackgres sg-ui-secret 'api.stackgres.io/auth=user' --overwrite=true
> ```


With the new secret, is possible to install the operator with ArgoCD:

```yaml
---
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: stackgres-operator
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  # ...
  source:
    chart: stackgres-operator
    helm:
      parameters:
        # ...
        - name: authentication.secretRef.name
          value: sg-ui-secret
    # ...
```

Issue:
Use SGObjectStorage CRD for Postgres base backup and WAL storage
The proposed CRD is basically a small evolution over the currently existing [`SGBackupConfig.storage` subobject](https://stackgres.io/doc/latest/reference/crd/sgbackupconfig/#storage-configuration). The main goal of extracting it into a separate CRD is for being able to re-use and reference it from different contexts.

This would enable to support clusters initialized from a Postgres backup and WAL archive. Having a CRD that references this archive, there could be two use cases perfectly supported by this CRD:
* A user wants to have a cluster replicating from the archive, and there's an existing CRD representing that archive within the same K8s cluster (and namespace). In this case, a reference to the existing CRD should be enough.
* A user wants to have a cluster replicating from the archive, on a different K8s cluster (i.e. a DR scenario). In this case, a local (to the destination K8s cluster) CRD needs to be created, but could have the same or similar contents from the source CRD, which could be easily copied, and then referenced.

The proposed name for this new CRD is `SGObjectStorage`.

More precisely, this change would imply the following changes:
1. ~~Extract the `storage` subobject from the `SGBackupConfig` CRD and "upgrade" it to a full CRD called `SGObjectStorage`.~~ (See #1564)
1. ~~Change the `SGBackupConfig` to include a new property, `.spec.sgObjectStorage`, that will become a reference to the new CRD.~~
1. <del>Add a new property to the new CRD, called `SGObjectStorage.mode`, which will be an enum with possible values `RW, RO`. This would be useful for standby clusters, which might be provided with more restricted user access credentials</del>.
1. Create the section `.spec.configurations.backups` with an array (only allowed to have just 1 element) that will replace the field `.spec.configurations.sgBackupConfig` including a reference to an `SGObjectStorage` and the other properties of `SGBackupConfig`.
1. Deprecate the field `.spec.configurations.sgBackupConfig` in `SGCluster` CRD and forbid create new `SGCluster` using such field.
1. Deprecate `SGBackupConfig` CRD and forbid creation of `SGBackupConfig` CRs. 

Note that this scheme also allows for creating standby clusters processing WALs from an object storage that might not be the original source one, but possibly one replicated in other region (eg. an S3 bucket replicated to another S3 bucket on another region), in which case source and destination CRDs will only differ on the bucket name and region (and potentially, user credentials).

Also note that this issue doesn't deal with how to modify a `SGCluster` to support standby cluster creation. That will be addressed on a separate issue (see #866).

<del>Ideally, some strong validation support should be built into the operator to validate access credentials when creating the CRD (i.e., validate that we can read or read and write to the object storage). This will improve the current user experience of creating an invalid `SGBackupConfig`</del>.

Proposed change to `SGCluster`:

```yaml
spec:
  configurations:
    backupPath: <string>
    sgBackupConfig: <string> # this does not change but will be deprecated and mutually exclusive with `backups` field.
    backups: # The backups is an array that can contain at most 1 element to allow in the future specify multiple backup configuration so that backup may be stored on multiple storages.
    - path: <string>
      compression: <string>
      cronSchedule: <string>
      performance:
        maxDiskBandwitdh: <integer>
        maxNetworkBandwitdh: <integer>
        uploadDiskConcurrency: <integer>
      retention: <integer>
      sgObjectStorage: <string> # name of an SGObjectStorage in the same namespace
```

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [x] Implement a mutating webhook in order to migrate from `SGBackupConfig` + backupPath to `SGObjectStorage` + new backups section in `SGCluster`
- [x] Implement a validating webhook in order to disallow usage of `SGBackupConfig` in `SGCluster`

[ahachete]: Revisiting the issue, I realized that:

> Add a new property to the new CRD, called `SGPostgresArchive.mode`, which will be an enum with possible values `RW, RO`. This would be useful for standby clusters, which might be provided with more restricted user access credentials.

This is not needed nor a good idea. First of all, the RW/RO behavior is already determined by the kind of operation you are doing (if you are a cluster containing a master node, it will be RW as you will be pushing backups and WAL files; if you are replicating, you will be RO only). Yet both behaviors can reuse the same credentials (or not, in which case you'd just create another `SGPostgresArchive`, pointing to the same bucket, but with different credentials. We could create a CRD just for the bucket, and then have the `SGPostgresArchive` reference it and add the credentials, but I think that's just going too too far in "normalization". I'd keep it as-is, without adding the `mode` field.

> Ideally, some strong validation support should be built into the operator to validate access credentials when creating the CRD (i.e., validate that we can read or read and write to the object storage). This will improve the current user experience of creating an invalid `SGBackupConfig`.

This we won't probably do, at least short-term. This implies importing the SDKs (or at least cloud storage related libraries) of all major cloud providers as dependencies, and generate a lot of cloud-dependent code just for simple permission testing. Not a major priority now. Maybe this could better be offloaded to WAL-g.

As an additional comment, if a `SGPostgresArchive` is referenced from a cluster that will be replicating from this archive, an additional parameter `sgClusterName` or equivalent would be required to be specified, as StackGres appends the cluster name as a subpath on the storage (to support potentially many clusters under the same storage bucket and path).

[ahachete]: There are other potential contexts where we may want to use Object Storage, not only for archiving. According to this, we may consider renaming it to something more generic, like `SGObjectStorage`.

[teoincontatto]: Update description to change `SGPostgresArchive` to `SGObjectStorage`

[teoincontatto]: We could relax a little bit the requirements to simplify implementation and adoption by allowing the `SGObjectStorage` be inlined inside an `SGBackupConfig` (as it is now) and offering the option to just reference to an `SGObjectStorage` adding the `.spec.sgObjectStorage` field to `SGBackupConfig` and making it exclusive with the `.spec.storage` field.

[ahachete]: I think this makes the UX a bit more cumbersome. A user that wants to create a cluster, realizes that needs to create a backup configuration first before creating the cluster. Proceeds to do that, and then realizes that needs to create an object storage before creating the backup configuration. So three levels of depth. Sounds too much, I'd try to always cap it to two levels.

What we can do to keep the current behavior unchanged is to create the `SGObjectStorage` as described and move the remaining fields into the `SGCluster`, also as described. But then, we could generate a "legacy" `SGBackupConfig` via mutation, and keep for now the backup mechanism to work only with `SGBackupConfig`. Then at a later version we can call this deprecated and switch exclusively to `SGCluster` and `SGObjectStorage`.

Removing `sgBackupConfig` completely from the `SGCluster` is a breaking change so we have to maintain it for backward compatibility. What we can do is deprecate such field and do not allow to create a cluster with it or to modify it for cluster using latest version of StackGres. In the latter case just removing it would be an option. 

OTOH, I do not think that a mutating webhook should reconcile a `SGBackupConfig`. The proper way to do so is with a reconciliation cycle. But reconciling the `SGBackupConfig` in the cluster reconciliation cycle does not make much sense because it is needed by the cluster reconciliation cycle itself. So I'm proposing to turn this into an array of objects. It would be acceptable not to implement this internally right now (i.e. limiting it to only one), if it would require extra effort; but to already prepare this refactor to support this.

[teoincontatto]: Probably is not the same since here the problem is related to mixing WAL files from different Postgres major versions.

The idea proposed by @sebawebber to solve this ~Bug is to add the postgres major version to the path (maybe architecture too in order to make it work when #1346 is implemented). We have to fix some incompatibilities of this new approach in order to make it working retro compatible with backups and backup configs created in previous StackGres versions:

* Old created backups have been stored under the old path (`[<optional storage path>/]<cluster namespace>/<cluster name>`).
* Old created backup configs have stored all WAL files under the old path (`[<optional storage path>/]<cluster namespace>/<cluster name>`).

The first point could be fixed by adding a new field `.status.sgBackupConfig.storage.*.finalPath` to `SGBackup` so that will be used as the final path (without appending `/<cluster namespace>/<cluster name>`). The old path value (`[<optional storage path>/]<cluster namespace>/<cluster name>`) will then be set in field `.status.sgBackupConfig.storage.*.finalPath` by the conversion webhook for all sgbackups.

The second point could be fixed by adding the field `.spec.storage.*.finalPath` to `SGBackupConfig` so that will be used as the final path (without appending `/<cluster namespace>/<cluster name>`). The old path value (`[<optional storage path>/]<cluster namespace>/<cluster name>`) will then be set in field `.spec.storage.*.finalPath` by the conversion webhook for all sgbackupconfigs. Finally the major version upgrade `SGDbOps` will have a new field `.spec.majorVersionUpgrade.setFinalPath` that:

* if empty will remove the `.spec.storage.*.finalPath` field of the `SGBackupConfig` associated with the `SGCluster`.
* if set not empty will change the `.spec.storage.*.finalPath` field of the `SGBackupConfig` associated with the `SGCluster`.
* if not set and the `SGCluster` have an `SGBackupConfig` with a field `.spec.storage.*.finalPath` set will return a validation error.

The rationale for it is that we frequently need to execute actions local to the pod, like reloading/restarting a service (say pgbouncer configuration is updated and requires a reload) or calling a binary local to the pod (e.g. wal-g, for backups). From this perspective, I believe the best could be done is to turn the actual shell script into a spec of what the backup script should do, and how it could be tested, and then write the implementation as part of the (to be developed) local-pod controller.

Issue:
Implement "ManagedSQL" as a new SGScripts CRD referenced by SGCluster
We want more and more to offer a fully-featured GitOps approach to managing Postgres databases.

One such areas that are not fully covered is managing a database DDL, or even more generic, managing a database with SQL. While you'd normally interact with a database with a CLI or GUI client, having the ability to programmatically maintain database DDL with a CRD is a well justified use-case. The current ability to execute operations by a component of the operator make this system very powerful for programmatic creation and update of DDL.

This issue aims to capture this and define a new CRD, called `SGScripts`, to be added to StackGres' set of CRDs. This would allow to "define in YAML" commands to execute on a cluster.

Note that it won't be a goal to support DDL migrations, deltas and others --that would be relied on the user or other external tools. If any edit is performed to the `SGScripts`, it will be blindly re-executed. If it is deleted, no action will be executed.

The internal spec of the CRD would be very similar to the actual [`initialData.scripts`](https://stackgres.io/doc/latest/reference/crd/sgcluster/#scripts-configuration) spec:

```yaml
  - name: $scriptName
    database: $dbname #optional, default to 'postgres'
    scriptFrom | script: read the script from either a ConfigMap, Secret or inline.
  - name: ...
    ...
```

There is some overlap with the `spec.initialData.scripts` section of the `SGCluster` and for this reason the intermediary CRD called `SGScripts` will be created in order to be used as a reference by both `SGCluster` (and in the future `SGDbOps`). Section `spec.initialData.scripts` of the `SGCluster` will be deprecated and the new array field `spec.managedSQL.sgScripts` will be added in order to reference an array of `SGScripts` instances. `SGScripts` CRD will have the following model:

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1beta1
kind: SGScripts
spec:
  managedVersions: <boolean> # If `true` the versions will be managed by the operator automatically. The user will still be able to update them. `true` by default.
  continueOnError: <boolean> # if true, when any entry fail will not prevent subsequent entries from being executed. `false` by default.
  scripts:
  - name: <string> # Optional. Does not determine order of execution but creates a label to identify this script externally (like in events and logs).
    id: <integer> # The id is immutable and must be unique across all the script entries. It is replaced by the operator and  and is used to identify the script for the whole life of the `SGScript` object.
    version: <integer> # The version of the script. Set to `1` by default.
    database: <string> # Database where the script is executed. Defaults to the `postgres` database
    user: <string> # User that will execute the script. Defaults to the `postgres` user
    wrapInTransaction: <string> # Wrap the script in a transaction using the specified transaction mode (`NONE` (The default, means that the script will not be wrapped in a transaction), `READ COMMITTED`, `REPEATABLE READ` and `SERIALIZABLE`).
    storeStatusInDatabase: <boolean> # When specified `inTransaction` field must not to be set to `null` or `NONE` and the script execution will include storing the status of the execution of this script in the table `managed_sql.status` that will be created in the specified `database`. This will avoid an operation that fails partially to be unrecoverable requiring the intervention from the user. This is `false` by default.
    retryOnError: <boolean> # if true it retries to execute the script entry with an exponential back-off algorithm limited to 5 minutes with a variation of 1 minute. Default is false.
    script: <string> # Raw SQL script to execute. This field is mutually exclusive with
     `scriptFrom` field.
    scriptFrom:
      configMapKeyRef:
        name: <string> # The name of the ConfigMap that contains the SQL script to execute.
        key: <string> # The key name within the ConfigMap that contains the SQL script to execute.
      secretKeyRef:
        name: <string> # The name of the Secret that contains the SQL script to execute.
        key: <string> # The key name within the Secret that contains the SQL script to execute.
status:
  scripts:
    - id: <integer> # Identify the associated script entry with the same value in the `id` field. 
      hash: <string> # Hash of the value of the ConfigMap or Secret referenced by `scriptFrom.configMapKeyRef` and `scriptFrom.secretKeyRef` respectively.
```

However, old `spec.initialData.scripts` section of the `SGCluster` was intended to be run only once, and only if a backup is not restored. We instead allow all referenced `SGScripts` from field `.spec.managedSQL.sgScripts` to be modified and to be applied "live" to the `SGCluster`. The new `version` field will allow to detect if script have to be executed and will be managed by the operator (default) or manually if the `.spec.managedVersions` is set to `false`. When `.spec.managedVersions` is set to `true` in the `SGScripts` following rules will apply:

* Initially set version to 1.
* Secret or ConfigMap values hash is stored in the `SGScripts` `.status.scripts[].hash` section
* When an inline value is changed the version will be automatically incremented by 1.
* When a Secret or a ConfigMap is changed, the operator reconciliation cycle will update the hash and the version will be automatically incremented by 1.
* User will still be able to increment the value manually if needed.

Here is the proposed change to `SGCluster` in order to reference an array of `SGScripts` and maintain the status of applied `SGScripts`:

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGCluster
spec:
  managedSQL:
    continueOnSGScriptsError: <boolean> # if true, when any entry of any `SGScripts` fail will not prevent subsequent `SGScripts` from being executed. `false` by default.
    sgScripts:
    - id: <integer> # The id is immutable and must be unique across all the `SGScript` entries. It is replaced by the operator and is used to identify the `SGScript` entry. 
      name: <string> # a reference to an `SGScript`
status:
  managedSQL:
    sgScripts:
    - id: <integer> # Identify the associated `SGScript` entry with the same value in the `id` field. 
      startedAt: <string> # ISO-8601 datetime of when the script execution has been started. Will be reset each time the referenced `SGScripts` will be re-applied.
      failedAt: <string> # ISO-8601 datetime of when the script execution had failed (mutually exclusive with `completedAt`). Will be reset each time the referenced `SGScripts` will be re-applied.
      completedAt: <string> # ISO-8601 datetime of when the script execution had completed (mutually exclusive with `failedAt`). Will be reset each time the referenced `SGScripts` will be re-applied.
      scripts:
      - id: <integer> # Identify the associated script entry with the same value in the `id` field. 
        version: <integer> # The latest version applied
        intents: <integer> # Indicates the number of intents or failures occurred
        failureCode: <string> # If failed, the error code of the failure. See also https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/errcodes-appendix.html
        failure: <string> # If failed, a message of the failure
```

The user will be able to add or replace any entry of the `.spec.managedSQL.sgScripts` array in the `SGCluster`. When replacing a value the associated status entry will also be emptied as it was never executed. 

The order of execution and rules of the execution flow will be as follow:

* Each `SGScripts` will run in sequence one after another following the order of the `.spec.managedSQL.
* If any entry of any `SGScripts` fails next `SGScripts` will not be executed unless `.spec.managedSQL.continueOnSGScriptsError` is set to `true` in `SGCluster`.
* An entry of an `SGScripts` that has not been executed will be executed only if there are no other previous entry (following the array order) of the same `SGScripts` that has not been executed.
* If execution of an `SGScripts`'s entry fail no subsequent entries will be executed. Execution of subsequent entries is performed when previous entry execution failed only if field `.spec.continueOnError` is set to `true` in `SGScripts`.
* If any entry of an `SGScripts` has been already executed it will not be re-executed even if it failed.
* An entry is detected as "not being executed" if the entry version is missing from the status or different than the entry version in the status. 

This is inspired by the original ideas by @stoetti1 and subsequent discussion on #956.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Implement the feature, TODO raise to epic and create sub epics. Epic measured in 10 days to accomplish.
Sub tasks:
   - [ ] #1545 The UI part. to be evaluated.
   - [x] Creating a CRD to implement sgcripts.
   - [x] Adapting webhooks and rest API.
   - [x] Tests CRD
   - [x] Documentation CRD
   - [x] Implement applying the SQL
   - [x] Implement migrating from `.spec.initialData.scripts`
   - [x] Implement the test and documentation.

[DISCUSSION]
[teoincontatto]: > There is some overlap with the `initialData.scripts` section. However, this section is intended to be run only once, and only if a backup is not restored. It doesn't support updates. A `ManagedSQL` will support updates. However, this may present an opportunity to replace this existing `initialData.scripts` functionality by a reference to an existing `ManagedSQL` operation, that would be executed at initialization time or at any later time if there's an update to it. This is subject to ~Discussion, along with the rest of this proposal.

IMO referencing an `sgdbops` in the `sgcluster` could confuse the user since the `sgdbops` is something to be executed after the cluster is ready following a specific parameterization while scripts will be executed during cluster initialization ignoring such `sgdbops` parameterization.

[ahachete]: > the `sgdbops` is something to be executed after the cluster is ready following a specific parameterization while scripts will be executed during cluster initialization ignoring such `sgdbops` parameterization.

Can you elaborate on what is the "parametrization"?

To me, it makes sense to have the possibility to reference a SGDbOps to be executed after cluster creation. I may be missing some point, though.

[teoincontatto]: > Can you elaborate on what is the "parametrization"?
> 
> To me, it makes sense to have the possibility to reference a SGDbOps to be executed after cluster creation. I may be missing some point, though.

I am referring to following structure of `sgdbops`:

```
spec:
  runAt: <string>
  timeout: <string>
  maxRetries: <string>
  sgCluster: <string>
```

Here some points that need to be addressed:

* To create an `sgdbops` the `sgcluster` pointed by `.spec.sgCluster` have to exists.
* There is no point in having a `.spec.runAt` field when referencing the `sgdbops`, the operation should run right after cluster creation. But currently the operation will be started before the cluster is ready. Right now we miss a check to wait for cluster to be ready but would be OK to add it for this (and potentially other) operation.
* There will be a circular dependency where the `sgdbops` will reference `sgcluster` and vice versa. This is probably what will bring most confusion to users.
* Current behavior is to execute scripts before the cluster is ready, during patroni initialization. Not sure if this could break things or not thought.

[ahachete]: Let go back to the use case that triggered this issue, and see it from a 30,000 feet perspective.

An user may want to manage the DDL (and/or some data) of the database via a "SQL script". This script may be run at creation time, or at any later stage. But later, it may also be edited and re-run against the database.

The current `initialData.scripts` does not cover this functionality, only part of it. In particular, it doesn't support the notion of "editing" those scripts and re-running them.

The idea of having a `SGDbOps` to manage scripts would fulfill those goals: to run and edit+re-run scripts at any time. Except that to do this also at cluster init, it would require the cluster to reference the `SGDbOp`.

To overcome the difficulties you mentioned, I'd propose:
* Reconsider `SGDbOps.spec.sgCluster`. Think about possible (future) operations that may not need to reference a cluster, so this field could be optional (this case would also apply to ops where they are referenced, as they induced externally, exactly like the use case in this example). But it would also be possible that some operation may refer to more than one cluster. So this field may need to be reconsidered. Options I initially see:
    * Make it optional, depending on the operation (that would be compatible with what we have now, but may be skipped in some cases, like the operation of this issue).
    * Move it to the operation, only for those where it would make sense. This is a bit better, as other fields (like `runAt`) may also not make sense for referenced operations.
* I agree with adding a check for the cluster to be ready.
* We should definitely not allow circular dependencies.
* I don't see an issue (or a difference) running scripts before or after patroni initialization. Worst case, we can keep both (the init scripts in the SGCluster --and tell the user those are run by Patroni-- and the ManagedSQL proposed here, that can be edited and re-run in the future).

[teoincontatto]: Thinking better on this whole thread, we way achieve a simpler solution by abstracting what it is contained in initialData.scripts into a new CRD. We could call this new CRD `SGScripts` with the following proposed structure (that is identical to the structure under `.spec.initialData.scripts` section of `SGCluster` CRD but with some validation reductions and with the addition of the missing `user` field):

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGScripts
spec:
  scripts:
  - name: <string> # Optional name of the script
    database: <string> # Database where the script is executed. Defaults to the `postgres` database
    user: <string> # User that will execute the script. Defaults to the `postgres` user
    script: <string> # Raw SQL script to execute. This field is mutually exclusive with
     `scriptFrom` field.
    scriptFrom:
      configMapKeyRef:
        name: <string> # The name of the ConfigMap that contains the SQL script to execute.
        key: <string> # The key name within the ConfigMap that contains the SQL script to execute.
      secretKeyRef:
        name: <string> # The name of the Secret that contains the SQL script to execute.
        key: <string> # The key name within the Secret that contains the SQL script to execute.
```

Having an `SGScripts` we may then use it in `SGCluster` under `.spec.initialData.scripts` section and in `SGDbOps` under `.spec.managedSQL` section. This eliminates the problem of having the script executed asynchronously from the patroni bootstrap phase and allows to only expose the cluster if it has executed all the initialization scripts first. Maintaining backward compatibility.

OTOH I would also like to propose a renaming of the `SGDbOps` type proposed in this issue from `managedSQL` to `managedScript` and allow to make the operation agnostic of the script language. Today we may allow users to only execute SQL script but at some point we may want to enable them to execute other type of script, like shell script or python script. This could be achieved by just extending the `SGScripts` CRD.

[ahachete]: While I want to be careful about not creating too many CRDs (they are great; but they also add cognitive burden) I believe this one is quite justified.

But it makes sense iif it comes with properties related to a reconciliation cycle. That is: if the contents of the script(s) can be edited, the controller detects drifts, and re-applies (as mentioned in the original description it is not expected to generate deltas; but rather to apply "blindly" what the user supplied). As such, the events may contain a history of all the successful (or not) applies of the code. When the modified script is inline, this is trivial; another method to detect drift in referenced script will be needed (maybe keep a hash of the last version of the content of that code).

* Initially set always version to 1.
* Secret or ConfigMap values hash is stored in the `SGScripts` `.status.scripts[].hash` section
* When a inline value is changed the version will be automatically incremented by 1.
* When a Secret or a ConfigMap is changed, the operator reconciliation cycle will update the hash and the version will be automatically incremented by 1.
* User will still be able to increment the value manually if needed.

We may also add a `boolean` field `managedVersions` (`true` by default) to allow the user to disable this automatic updating of the versions in those cases where the user want to fire and forget. Then the user may just update a in-line Script or a referenced ConfigMap or Secret in order to be able to perform the operations.

> It's certainly a problem where to store then the status. One option is still the CR itself, just referencing all the clusters that use it and have had something applied (which can obviously vary over time). Another, possibly better, is what you say, to store them in the `SGCluster.status`.

I advocate to maintain the status in the `SGCluster` (and in the hypothetical `SGDbOps`) and make it as compact as possible, that is, if we store an array of managedSQL where each one contains an array of scripts each with a version and an optional failed message and fail code to indicate that the script failed and why (limited in size to 1024 characters):

```yaml
status:
  managedSQL:
  - [ { version: 1 }, { version: 1 }, { version: 1 } ]
  - [ { version: 1, failure: 'syntax error at or near "return"', failureCode: '42601' } ]
  - [ { version: 1 }, { version: 2 }, { version: 1 } ]
```

---

OTOH it seems to me that ordering of such scripts is something very important and should follow some strict rules. Those rules should be part of each `SGScripts` so that user may tweak rules in its own spec.

We may opt for a main strategy:

* Each `SGScripts` will run in sequence one after another. The execution will be parallelized if `.spec.managedSQL.runInParallel` is set to `true` in `SGCluster`.
* If any entry of any `SGScripts` fails next `SGScripts` will not be executed unless `.spec.managedSQL.continueOnError` is set to `true` in `SGCluster`.
* An entry of an `SGScripts` that has not been executed will be executed only if there are no other previous entry (following the array order) of the same `SGScripts` that has not been executed. The execution will be parallelized if `.spec.runInParallel` is set to `true` in `SGScripts`.
* If execution of an `SGScripts`'s entry fail no subsequent entries will be executed. Execution of subsequent entries is performed if previous entry execution failed by setting to `true` the boolean field `.spec.continueOnFailure` in `SGScripts`.
* If any entry of an `SGScripts` has been already executed it will not be re-executed even if it failed.
* An entry is detected as "not being executed" if the entry version is missing from the status or different than the entry version in the status.

This will change `SGCluster` to:

```yaml
spec:
  initialData:
    sgScripts:
    - <string> # a reference to an `SGScripts`
  managedSQL:
    continueOnError: <boolean> # if true, when any entry of any `SGScripts` fail will not prevent subsequent `SGScripts` from being executed. `false` by default.
    runInParallel: <boolean> # if true, all `SGScripts` will be executed in parallel and `continueOnError` will be required to be set to `true`. `false` by default.
    sgScripts:
    - <string> # a reference to an `SGScripts`
```

  continueOnError: <boolean> # if true, when any entry fail will not prevent subsequent entries from being executed. `false` by default.
  runInParallel: <boolean> # if true, all entries will be executed in parallel and `continueOnError` will be required to be set to `true`. `false` by default.
  scripts:

[teoincontatto]: Status of executed scripts identify the script entry by using the position in the array. Here there is a problematic use case when a user want to add a script entry in the middle of some script entries. In such case the status of subsequent entries is lost and the operator will not known which entries it may or may not re-execute. This will depend on the version of each entry that has been shifted in the array.

I propose to introduce an alternative identifier that the is automatically filled by the operator and allows to add entries in the array without modifying the identifier of other entries in any case.

The idea is to add an immutable integer field called `id` that is initially set incrementally in each script entry section under `.spec.scripts` entries of the `SGScript`. The latest value is also stored in the `.status.lastId` field. Whenever an user add an entry to the `.spec.scripts` section the next value for the `id` field under `.spec.scripts` section is calculated by adding 1 to the value stored in the `.status.lastId` field. Value of the `.status.lastId` field is also incremented by 1.

The same mechanism will be used to the `.spec.managedSQL` section in order to identify a referenced script.

This proposition has been added to the description.

[teoincontatto]: Hi @zer0x, thanks for sharing your case of service disruption. To me, the culprit of the problem you had experienced was this error:

```
[1177595]: db=,user=,app=,client= FATAL:  data directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data" has invalid permissions
[1177659]: db=,user=,app=,client= DETAIL:  Permissions should be u=rwx (0700) or u=rwx,g=rx (0750).
```

And seems we are not alone with this problem:

* https://github.com/zalando/patroni/issues/2307
* https://github.com/CrunchyData/postgres-operator/issues/3023

The thing is that we set the fsGroup to the postgres user id. The storage class provider (if it supports fsGroup correctly) set permissions to something postgres does not like for all the files in the persistent volume where the `/var/lib/postgresql/data` folder is created. To mitigate this we have an [init container script](https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/blob/main/stackgres-k8s/src/operator/src/main/resources/templates/setup-data-paths.sh) that sets the permissions to `700` for the data directory again so there should not be any problem since [the permission change should be performed only when volume is mounted](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/security-context/#configure-volume-permission-and-ownership-change-policy-for-pods):

> By default, Kubernetes recursively changes ownership and permissions for the contents of each volume to match the fsGroup specified in a Pod's securityContext when that volume is mounted.

Now, the assumption made here that is probably wrong, is that the volume is mounted only on Pod creation. When a Kubernetes API disruption occurs a Storage Class Provider may have to re-mount the volume and apply the permission change again while the Pod is still running. I could not find documentation about this behavior since it may depend on the Storage Class Provider solution used. Which was the Storage Class Provider in this case?

Probably a solution to this bug would to set the permissions of the Postgres data directory to `700` before patroni starts using a [Patroni callback on_start and on_restart](https://patroni.readthedocs.io/en/latest/SETTINGS.html#postgresql). Currently the workaround is to connect to the patroni container and set such permission manually:

```shell
kubectl get pod -n $CLUSTER_NAMESPACE -o name -l "stackgres.io/cluster-name=$CLUSTER_NAME" \
  | xargs -I %POD_NAME kubectl exec -n $CLUSTER_NAMESPACE %POD_NAME -c patroni -- chmod 700 /var/lib/postgresql/data
```

Since this seems a quite critical bug I will add it to the upcoming release ~"target_version::1.3.2". I'll try to create a e2e test case for this but I am not sure if I'll be able to reproduce easily. In any case, the solution should not harm if it does not solve the issue as expected but, if my assumption are instead correct, it will have great benefits since it will solve the permission problem on volume re-mounts.

Issue:
Support user-supplied sidecars for SGCluster pods
Some applications might want to access Postgres, or its filesystem, or part of other components, directly (i.e. not through the Postgres wire protocol). For this cases, highly user dependent, we might want to add the possibility to "inject" a user sidecar into the SGCluster pods.

This could potentially imply many options like:
*  Container image.
*  Annotations.
*  Environment variables, config maps?
*  Inject some additional env vars to the container, like the postgres superuser and password.
*  Potentially access the Postgres filesystem (PGDATA) and/or the logs, etc.
*  Resource limits for the user-added sidecar, to control its potential impact.

# Proposal

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGCluster
spec:
  postgresServices:
    primary:
      customPorts: # The list of extra ports that will be exposed by the primary service
      - <ServicePort> # See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#serviceport-v1-core
    replicas:
      customPorts: # The list of extra ports that will be exposed by the replicas service
      - <ServicePort> # See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#serviceport-v1-core
  pods:
    customVolumes:
    - <Volume> # See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#volume-v1-core
    customInitContainers:
    - <Container> # See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#container-v1-core
    customContainers:
    - <Container> # See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#container-v1-core
```

Sections `.spec.postgresServices.primary.customPorts` and `.spec.postgresServices.replicas.customPorts` will allow to expose any custom service defined by a custom sidecars. We may think about renaming section `.spec.postgresServices` to `.spec.services` in a future version of `SGCluster` CRD since we will expose ports from custom containers and user may not want to expose Postgres ports at all but just those of their custom services.

The `.spec.pods.customContainers[]` and `.spec.pods.customInitContainers[]` are the same as the `Container` object present in the Pod resource under section `.spec.containers[]` and `.spec.initContainers[]`.

The `.name` field in `Container` object will forbid using any container name that is used by StackGres.

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGCluster
spec:

      - <ServicePort> # See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#serviceport-v1-core
    replicas:

      - <ServicePort> # See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#serviceport-v1-core
  pods:
    extraInitContainers:
    - <Container> # See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#container-v1-core
    extraContainers:
    - <Container> # See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#container-v1-core
```

Sections `.spec.postgresServices.primary.extraPorts` and `.spec.postgresServices.replicas.extraPorts` will allow to expose any custom service defined by a custom sidecars. We may think about renaming section `.spec.postgresServices` to `.spec.services` in a future version of `SGCluster` CRD since we will expose ports from extra containers and user may not want to expose Postgres ports at all but just those of their custom services.

The `.spec.pods.extraContainers[]` and `.spec.pods.extraInitContainers[]` are the same as the [`Container`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#container-v1-core) object present in the Pod resource under section `.spec.containers[]` and `.spec.initContainers[]`.

The `.name` field in [`Container`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#container-v1-core) object will forbid using any container name that is used by StackGres.

We will forbid following fields:

* `.securityContext`: The users of the container will use the main security context and will be replaced by mounting `/etc/passwd`, `/etc/shadow`, `/etc/groups` and `/etc/gshadow`. This will allow to use postgres UNIX socket and the data volume with the same user as postgres. Also it will allow to use the same container in OpenShift with arbitrary user ids.
* `.stdin`: This will be left unset
* `.stdinOnce`: This will be left unset
* `.terminationMessagePath`: This will be left unset
* `.terminationMessagePolicy`: This will be left unset
* `.tty`: This will be left unset
* `.volumeDevices`: This will be left unset since I do not think StatefulSet can work well with it. 
* `.resources`: This should be handled by `SGInstanceProfile` (see also #144) and first implementation should be the same as for other containers and init containers other than `patroni`. We will open an issue to implement resources for extra containers.

We may also forbid following fields in order to reduce a bit functionality and make a first implementation easier, in particular for the Web UI:

* `.lifecycle`
* `.startupProbe`
* `.readinessProbe`
* `.livenessProbe`
* `.envFrom`

User will be able to use any volume that is defined in the StatefulSet including the data PV by setting the section `.volumeMounts[]` in [`Container`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.22/#container-v1-core) object.

[teoincontatto]: After doing a PoC for custom containers I had to add a new section `.spec.pods.customVolumes` in order to support custom volumes (limited to configMap, downwardAPI, emptyDir, gitRepo, glusterfs, hostPath, nfs, projected and secret) inside of custom containers and init containers:

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGCluster
spec:
  pods:
    customVolumes:
    - name: <string>
      configMap: <object>
      downwardAPI: <object>
      emptyDir: <object>
      gitRepo: <object>
      glusterfs: <object>
      hostPath: <object>
      nfs: <object>
      projected: <object>
      secret: <object>
```

Also, to avoid collisions with StackGres volumes we prefix the `custom-` string to the created custom volumes. So, to reference such custom volumes the user will have to prepend the name of the volume mounts with the same prefix.

The same is done for the ports defined in the custom containers but in this case it is transparent to the user since it does not require to prepend the `custom-` prefix when defining the custom ports (`.spec.postgresServices.customPorts[].targetPort`).

Here is an example to better understand how this works:

```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGCluster
spec:
  postgresServices:
    primary:
      customPorts:
      - name: pgadmin
        port: 9000
        targetPort: pgadmin
    replicas:
      customPorts:
      - name: pgadmin
        port: 9000
        targetPort: pgadmin
  pods:
    customVolumes:
    - name: pgadmin
      emptyDir: {}
    - name: pgadmin-config
      configMap:
        name: pgadmin
    customContainers:
    - name: pgadmin
      image: dpage/pgadmin4:6.14
      env:
      - name: PGADMIN_DEFAULT_EMAIL
        value: admin@stackgres.io
      - name: PGADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD
        value: st4ckgr3s
      - name: PGADMIN_LISTEN_PORT
        value: "9000"
      - name: PGADMIN_DISABLE_POSTFIX
        value: "true"
      ports:
      - containerPort: 9000
        name: pgadmin
        protocol: TCP
      volumeMounts:
      - mountPath: /pgadmin4/config_distro.py
        subPath: config_distro.py
        name: custom-pgadmin-config
      - mountPath: /var/log/pgadmin
        subPath: var/log/pgadmin
        name: custom-pgadmin
      - mountPath: /var/lib/pgadmin
        subPath: var/lib/pgadmin
        name: custom-pgadmin
      - mountPath: /etc/passwd
        name: user
        readOnly: true
        subPath: etc/passwd
      - mountPath: /etc/group
        name: user
        readOnly: true
        subPath: etc/group
      - mountPath: /etc/shadow
        name: user
        readOnly: true
        subPath: etc/shadow
      - mountPath: /etc/gshadow
        name: user
        readOnly: true
        subPath: etc/gshadow
```

To try the example with the PoC the following ConfigMap is required:

```shell
kubectl create configmap pgadmin --from-literal=config_distro.py="$(cat << EOF
CA_FILE = '/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt'
LOG_FILE = '/dev/null'
HELP_PATH = '../../docs'
DEFAULT_BINARY_PATHS = {
        'pg': '/usr/local/pgsql-14',
        'pg-14': '/usr/local/pgsql-14',
        'pg-13': '/usr/local/pgsql-13',
        'pg-12': '/usr/local/pgsql-12',
        'pg-11': '/usr/local/pgsql-11',
        'pg-10': '/usr/local/pgsql-10'
}
EOF
  )"
```

The example also show the usage of StackGres volumes. In this particular case we have to mount the user volume in 4 different location in order to inject the default postgres user id. This is a bit hackish since the container used have probably a different set of user ids. So we can end having problem when accessing files that does not belong to an user defined in the injected users. A proper solution to this would be to create a custom init container that mimics the behavior of the StackGres init container that creates the injected users files but for the target container. This is something that I will try to include in the final e2e test.

Issue:
Add support for cascading, remote and WAL-based SGCluster replication
After #864 is implemented, `SGCluster` would have support for replication (sub)groups within the `SGCluster` itself, allowing for different combinations of replication mechanism (async, sync, etc) and HA/read-only replicas. But these subgroups at the end belong to the same cluster, with a single primary, and all replicas replicate from it. With cascading replication, we create another whole cluster that will replicate from the first cluster, creating a two-level (or obviously multi-level) replication topology (a tree). For this case, replication groups do not provide enough coverage for this, and it is proposed that we use more than one `SGCluster` (basically, one `SGCluster` for every node of the replication topology tree).

The goal of this issue is to add support for the `SGCluster` for the following use cases:

* Support cascading replication within the same K8s cluster. A secondary (or more) `SGCluster` could be created that will replicate from the primary `SGCluster`. The primary would be pointed just by providing as a reference its name.

* Support cascading replication from a different namespace and/or K8s cluster. This is mostly considered for DR (Disaster Recovery) scenarios. A secondary `SGCluster` will be created, and will replicate from the primary cluster that would be identified by its `(host,port,user,password)` credentials.

* Support replication from a WAL archive. A secondary `SGCluster` will be created, and a reference to a `SGObjectStorage` will be added, so that Postgres may replicate from it. Note that this option may be complementary of the above two or even on a primary `SGCluster`: in other words, any replica of any cluster, may be able to combine both streaming replication and replication from a `SGObjectStorage`, which would be used as a backup mechanism.

To support this, it is proposed to add `.spec.replicateFrom` section to the `SGCluster` with the following properties:
* `.sgCluster`: Another document. If present, it signals that this cluster will not have a primary (at least at creation time) and would also imply that `.initialData` cannot be present, they are exclusive. Fields:
    * `.name`: name of a local `SGCluster` (must exist, have a primary and be on the same namespace)
    * `.external`: section with external configuration parameters. Conflicts with `.name`. Properties: `.host`, `.port` and `.secretKeyReference` section (with `.name` and `.key` that point to a `Secret` on the same namespace) for the replication user/password.
* `.sgObjectStorage`: this option may be present on any cluster (primary or otherwise), and may also be present in the presence of the above `.sgCluster` field. It should be a valid reference to a `SGObjectStorage` in the same namespace.


```yaml
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
kind: SGCluster
spec:
  replicateFrom:
    instance:
      sgCluster: <string> # name of an existing SGCluster in the same namespace.
      external:
        host: <string> # the external instance hostname
        port: <integer> # the external instance port
    storage:
      sgObjectStorage: <string> # The name of a SGObjectStorage in the same namespace.
      path: <string> # The path to read the WAL files from inside the referenced SGObjectStorage
    users:
      superuser:
        user:
          name: <string> # The secret containing the username value
          key: <string> # The key of the secret containing the username value
        password:
          name: <string> # The secret containing the password value
          key: <string> # The key of the secret containing the password value
      replication:
        user:
          name: <string> # The secret containing the username value
          key: <string> # The key of the secret containing the username value
        password:
          name: <string> # The secret containing the password value
          key: <string> # The key of the secret containing the password value
      authenticator:
        user:
          name: <string> # The secret containing the username value
          key: <string> # The key of the secret containing the username value
        password:
          name: <string> # The secret containing the password value
          key: <string> # The key of the secret containing the password value
```

If `.spec.replicateFrom` section is specified, it signals that this cluster will not have a primary (at least at creation time) and would also imply that `.initialData` cannot be present, they are exclusive.

The section `.spec.replicateFrom` can be removed later in order to signal that this cluster will have a primary in the `SGCluster` ASAP (or after a restart if required).

Note that each `SGCluster` may have its own internal replication groups. By default, we may assume that a cascading `SGCluster` using replication would replicate always asynchronously and from the primary node that is contained within the primary `SGCluster`. This might be the "candidate primary" instead of the primary if cascading from a `SGCluster` that is in turn cascading. In the future, we may add the ability to pin one or more replicas and drive the cascading replication from them, instead of from the primary.

This issue is inspired by #838.

Issue:
Rollback to previous version (if possible) when major version upgrade fails
### Problem to solve

Whenever a major version upgrade operation fails the user is not able to rollback the operation. Currently the only workaround is to follow the procedure to ["Reconvery PGDATA from existing volume"](https://stackgres.io/doc/latest/runbooks/recover-pgdata-from-existing-volume/) documented in a StackGres runbook.

### Further details

When a major version upgrade operation fails, if the user did not used the link or clone options the old data is not lost but is still present in the Persistent Volume. The problem is that the cluster can not be used due to the following reasons:

* The `.status.dbOps.majorVersionUpgrade` section is used by the operator to know that the major-version-upgrade init container has to be created. The container blocks the cluster from starting
* The `.spec.postgres.version` can not be changed directly by the user but have to be modified by the SGDbOps generated serviceaccount.

### Proposal

Make the SGDbOps major version upgrade operation to automatically rollback the operation in case of failure is the clone or link options are not used or only the check has been executed.

## Testing

Improve major version upgrade test in order to check the rollback is performed if the operation fails

## Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] Implementation
* [ ] Test
* [ ] Documentation

### Links / references

https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/pgupgrade.html

[teoincontatto]: Reopening (again) to improve cleanup in order to restore previous number of instances and do minor fixes to the code

[teoincontatto]: Finally decided to not improve cleanup since rollback is a last resort operation and would require user intervention anyway and minor fixes are not critical ones

[teoincontatto]: The current services that StackGres provides are:

* `<cluster name>` for read and writes
* `<cluster name>-replicas` for read only.

The deprecated `<cluster name>-primary` Service was abandoned in favor of the `<cluster name>` Service that is managed by Patroni to provide a more stable mechanism of promoting the primary node. Patroni set automatically the Endpoints for such service that also are used to perform the election of the primary. This guarantee that only one Pod will be targeted by the Service at any given time. Unfortunately Patroni does not provide any mechanism to change the name of the service without breaking other things since, for Patroni, the name of the service match the name of the cluster. Before that the Service used the labels set by Patroni to target the primary and we could use any name for that read write Service. The problem of using the labels is that there are chances of having a split brain situation since the Service may point to more than one Pod at any given time.

### Problem to solve

We want to integrate [Babelfish Compass](https://github.com/babelfish-for-postgresql/babelfish_compass) into the StackGres REST API in order to be able to asses compatibility of SQL Server schema with [Babelfish for PostgreSQL](https://github.com/babelfish-for-postgresql). 

### Further details

Babelfish Compass generates from an SQL source file a series HTLMs files with logs of the performed operations, the report and the SQL source file provided.

### Proposal

The `/stackgres/application` REST API (see #1536) will have to return `{name: "babelfish-compass", publisher: "com.ongres"}` when env var `APPLICATION_BABELFISH_COMPASS` is not set to `true`.

A new REST API endpoint `/stackgres/application/com.ongres/babelfish-compass` will be created.

The endpoint will be disabled when env var `APPLICATION_BABELFISH_COMPASS` is not set to `true`.

The endpoint will accept the POST method with a payload consisting of an SQL file. A ConfigMap with the SQL file will be created together with a Job that will generate the report using the SQL file from the ConfigMap. The same ConfigMap will be updated by the Job with the resulting HTML report, the HTML with the source SQL and the HTML with the logs of the operation. The REST API will return the following JSON object with a 200 HTTP code:

```yaml
report: <string> # HTML with the report
logs: <string> # HTML with the logs
source: <string> # HTML with the source SQL
```

On error operation the REST API will return the following JSON object with a 500 HTTP code:

```yaml
type: <string>
title: <string>
detail: <string> # the logs
status: <integer>
fields:
- <string>
```

The `APPLICATION_BABELFISH_COMPASS` will be configurable using the StackGres helm chart parameter `application[0].babelfish-compass`

### Links / references

https://github.com/babelfish-for-postgresql/babelfish_compass

> A ConfigMap is not designed to hold large chunks of data. The data stored in a ConfigMap cannot exceed 1 MiB.

It is not infrequent that a provided DDL file will be over this size.

[teoincontatto]: You right!

Then, another approach, is to create a Job that expose an HTTP REST API and, when ready, the REST API will forward the same request to the Job REST API. Sending the SQL file and forwarding back the response to the original client.

WDYT?

[ahachete]: Sounds good to me.

[teoincontatto]: Added publisher `com.ongres` for application REST API endpoint and in the Babelfish Compass REST API endpoint path

[teoincontatto]: The Job created by this endpoint may remain running forever in some cases. To avoid having a Job running forever we may want to set a timeout to the Job (e.g. 1hour) so that it is stopped after such amount of time.

When showing logs for a cluster on the web console, the following issues should be improved:

- The "automatic load" in a `tail -f` manner should be the default loading behavior only when no date filter has been set. 
- If any date filter is applied, the logs should always log starting from the `startDate` to the  `finishDate`

[DISCUSSION]
[ldgarcia]: We have been discussing the best way to handle the loading of records on the different methods we use right now: `live` (`tail -f` like) or `infinite scroll`.

Right now we have a "Scroll to bottom" button which, when no date filters are applied and the `live` method is being used, works fine and the user is able to identify easily how the records are loaded and what that button does (scrolling down to the last record loaded). 

But when a date filter is applied, the `live` method is disabled and the user can only load records in an `infinite scroll` manner. When on this method, users might think that the "Scroll to bottom" button will automatically scroll down to the last record on the selected date range, not the last record on the current slot shown on the viewport.

Our suggestion would be to remove the "Scroll to bottom" option and let users navigate the records just as they would do on any other app, either terminal, native or web based, in which users would simply use the scroll bar or do `END`/`CTRL+END` or `COMMAND+DOWN` to scroll all the way down.

### Problem to solve

Secrets currently are being written to disk using the Helm chart if the templates and values are rendered to disk

e.g:
```
VERSION=1.1.0
helm template \
    -n stackgres stackgres-operator \
    "https://stackgres.io/downloads/stackgres-k8s/stackgres/${VERSION}/helm/stackgres-operator.tgz" \
      > ./stackgres-operator.yaml
grep password ./stackgres-operator.yaml
```

### Further details

If a manifest is templated/rendered out, secrets are written to disk.
By providing a way to use an external secret it will safer.

### Proposal

Add the following fields to set a different secret to use.
```yaml
authentication:
  secretRef:
    name: ""
```

### Testing

Prepare namespace and auth secret
```
mkdir -p stackgres
kubectl create namespace stackgres --dry-run=client -o yaml \
  | kubectl apply -f -
PASSWORD=$(tr -cd '[:alnum:]' < /dev/urandom | fold -w40 | head -n1)
kubectl -n stackgres create secret generic stackgres-custom-auth \
    --from-literal=k8sUsername=admin \
    --from-literal=password="$(echo "${PASSWORD}" | sha256sum)" \
    --from-literal=clearPassword="${PASSWORD}" \
    --dry-run=client \
    -o yaml \
    | kubectl apply -f -
```

Render Helm chart
```
VERSION=1.1.0
helm template \
    -n stackgres stackgres-operator \
    --set authentication.secretRef.name=stackgres-custom-auth \
    "${PWD}" \
      > ./stackgres/stackgres-operator.yaml
```

Install StackGres
```
kubectl -n stackgres apply -f ./stackgres/stackgres-operator.yaml
```

Get the secret
```
kubectl -n stackgres get secret stackgres-custom-auth -o=jsonpath='{.data.clearPassword}' | base64 -d ; echo

Connect and login to StackGres
```
kubectl -n stackgres port-forward svc/stackgres-restapi 8443:443

Issue:
Set restore_command when backup is enabled
### Problem to solve

Whan an `SGCluster` is configured with backups a replica is not able to use the backup storage in order to pull required WAL files in case the primary has removed them. 

### Proposal

To allow a replica catch-up when it requires WAL files that have been removed on the primary the parameter [restore_command](https://postgresqlco.nf/doc/en/param/restore_command/) can be set to use `wal-g` to retrieve the files from the remote storage. The value to be used should be:

```
restore_command: 'exec-with-env "${BACKUP_ENV}" -- wal-g wal-fetch %f %p'
```

Since `BACKUP_ENV` env var is not available in the `restore_command` context (postgres remove all env var in such context for security reasons) its value should be replaced in code with the value hold by Java enum `io.stackgres.common.ClusterStatefulSetEnvVars.BACKUP_ENV`.

### Testing

Create an E2E test to test (or modify an existing one in order to also test) the following scenario:

1. Create a cluster with 2 instances and backup configured
2. Reduce the instances to 1
3. Create a table with some data
4. Rotate the WALs until a new created one is removed
5. Set instances to 2
6. Check that the replica is able to catch-up and the table has all the added data.

## Acceptance Criteria

The replica is able to catch-up after the primary lost the required WAL files.

### Links / references

* https://postgresqlco.nf/doc/en/param/shared_preload_libraries/
* https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html

```shell
check_previous_versions_conversion_webhooks() {
  kubectl proxy --port=9090 &
  KUBECTL_PROXY_PID=$!
  trap_kill "$KUBECTL_PROXY_PID"
  ANY_CONVERSION_FAILED=false
  for CRD_NAME in sgclusters sginstanceprofiles \
    sgpgconfigs sgpoolconfigs sgbackupconfigs \
    sgbackups sgdbops sgdistributedlogs
  do
    for PREVIOUS_API_VERSION in $(kubectl get crd "$CRD_NAME.stackgres.io" \
      -o=jsonpath='{ .spec.versions[?(@.storage != true)].name }')
    do
      if curl -f -s -k -X GET  -H "Accept: application/json" \
        "http://localhost:9090/apis/stackgres.io/$PREVIOUS_API_VERSION/$CRD_NAME" > /dev/null
      then
        echo "SUCCESS. $CRD_NAME.stackgres.io can be converted from $PREVIOUS_API_VERSION"

        echo "FAIL. $CRD_NAME.stackgres.io can not be converted from $PREVIOUS_API_VERSION"
        ANY_CONVERSION_FAILED=true
      fi
    done
  done
  kill "$KUBECTL_PROXY_PID"
  if "$ANY_CONVERSION_FAILED"

We could do that. However, note that the other four possible configurations may be overridden at the replication groups, while the backup configuration can't. Thus, for avoiding doubts as if the backup configuration may be overridden, we may just keep it as a separate parameter. Also note that in your example you included the `.pods` section belonging to the cluster, but it should belong to the replication group. You should be able to change disk size or storage class per replication group. But even more importantly the annotations, to help with different placing of replication groups which may want to have different failure domains. They are DCS/global fields, like sync_node_count, not replication group ones. This needs should be filled by the global patroni config file, not .replication field, IMHO. The issue I see with BOTH .role and a local Patroni config file, is a potential inconsistency, ambiguity and redundancy. What about a group having role: HA and tags: nofailover=true ? What does is 'really' mean role: HA? Can't I have different HA groups? What I would like is to remove .role BUT address simplicty too. How? By providing **off the shelf** some Patroni config files with pre-defined use cases. This library of config files could then be referenced by users in their group. They could create new Patroni config and provide them to the community too. In the same way, the complexity for PG configuration is already _masked_ by the pred-defined config file, not by some masquerading fields. In the end, choose what's your confortable with...
