In this case, if we expose the `.role` on the `SGCluster` CRD as I keep proposing, we won't expose the tags in the `SGPatroniConfig`. So this config would never occur. > By providing **off the shelf** some Patroni config files with pre-defined use cases. This library of config files could then be referenced by users in their group. They could create new Patroni config and provide them to the community too. In the same way, the complexity for PG configuration is already *masked* by the pred-defined config file, not by some masquerading fields. As I mentioned, the main problem here is that 1:1 mappings CRD<->Patroni config file (or Postgres configuration, for that matter) lead to: a) tight coupling, which makes evolution/replacement harder; b) harder for non-Postgres experts. IOW: I believe it's best for most of our intended audience, which is non-necessarily Postgres and Patroni experts, to set `.role=HA` instead of having to create a Patroni configuration, be scared by most of the parameters there, and having to understand that they need to set a `tag` with `nofailover=false` for the same purpose. It's just abstracting this particular configuration detail to a higher-level interface. I strongly believe de-coupling them and offering higher level interfaces for non-experts is a good thing. That's why we provide very carefully crafted default configurations for both `SGPostgresConfig` and `SGPoolingConfig` (surely you have checked, but if you haven't, we use a mutating webhook to inject default values with carefully tuned parameters for those parameters that you haven't tuned; you can check those default values injected either via the web console or the `.status` field of the CRD). The same we will do with the Patroni configuration: block some parameters (e.g. `tags`, in this case since it is exposed elsewhere) and set some good defaults that may be overridden, but that are good for non-Patroni experts. This doesn't prevent the Community from creating and publishing their own set of different configurations that could be shared. We might also at some point include some by default. [wvh]: @teoincontatto We're running StackGres v1.0.0 release using the latest 12.x version included (I believe that's Postgresql 12.8).

I don't think there has been any fail-over near the time of the error, nor any update or Kubernetes cluster issue. Moreover, we have seen the same issue the last two weeks in different clusters. It shows up as backups failing, and after some debugging, the logs show it's related to these `*.history` files. According to its code, `Wal-G` refuses to overwrite them, so there's no clear course of action once the problem manifests itself.

Backups started sometime during the StackGres `-beta` cycle though, so they are strictly speaking older than the installation of StackGres v1.0.0; not sure if that matters because they should have been rotated (configuration only keeps 5 or 7 last versions).

I guess it could happen that things sometimes don't line up after switch-over or upgrades and associated rewrites, but ideally there would be a way forward so we don't end up without backups and/or potentially master and replicas drifting apart.

[teoincontatto]: We know that wal-g prevent the timeline history file (those like `00000002.history`) from being changed [for security reasons](https://github.com/wal-g/wal-g/issues/420). This is because if we overwrite a timeline history file with a different one for the same timeline we are actually altering the timeline (so adding inconsistencies). Such wal-g check is happening after a controlled switchover performed by Patroni preventing backups from working. The weird thing about this issue is that after a switchover the new elected primary increments the timeline by 1 and when archiving the respective timeline history file find out that a different timeline history file for the same timeline already exists. How that could be possible is still mistery! I was not able to reproduce it and I suspect there is some race conditions that happens in order to trigger the problem. If I found any insight I'll share it in the issue but basically we need the logs of Patroni and Postgres for all the Pods before and after the problem appear.

[teoincontatto]: After some digging in the [patroni project issues](https://github.com/zalando/patroni/issues) I found a very interesting discussion about the [possibility of a split brain in Patroni using asynchronous replication](https://github.com/zalando/patroni/issues/890) (and currently StackGres only use asynchronous replication, but we plan to add #864) that might cause a duplicated timeline to be pick by a postgres instance. Not sure if a controlled switchover should not be enough to trigger that scenario since, well, it is controlled. BTW the restart operation may trigger an automatic failover when postgres is restarted and failures may happen in between that trigger the automatic failover too.

Seems that Patroni added a new configuration parameter, disabled by default, that would check the timeline of replicas:

> By default, when running leader elections, Patroni does not take into account the current timeline of replicas, what in some cases could be undesirable behavior. You can prevent the node not having the same timeline as a former master become the new leader by changing the value of `check_timeline` parameter to `true`.

We may set that parameter to true in StackGres by default but I am not sure if the user should be able to configure it to favor availability over data loss. And in such case we should find a way to allow to overwrite timeline history files that mismatch in content in a way that does not break continuous archiving and the latest history. We may do this under the hood by detecting that a new .history file want to overwite an existing one and, in such case, rename it in the remote storage to something like `<timeline>.history.<incremental number>.<timestamp>`. This resolution opens the way to restore previous lost timelines. But to support such case we should open an issue on the wal-g project since the tool should be in control of this particular behavior and give to the user the option to list and restore previous lost timelines (if this is even possible of course).

Looking into some code can reveal places ([example](https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/blob/main/stackgres-k8s/src/jobs/src/main/java/io/stackgres/jobs/dbops/clusterrestart/PatroniApiMetadataFinderImpl.java#L21)) where the domain  is hardcoded (which in my situation caused the restart DbOps job to be in the infinite loop because of not able to resolve the pods).

Issue:
Change internal DNS for services
## Summary

Some specific k8s providers configure the internal DNS for services using a search path different from `.svc.cluster.local`, since such search path is not a requirement in Kubernetes configuration ([see here](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/dns-debugging-resolution/#check-the-local-dns-configuration-first)).

## Implementation Plan

We need to remove the search path `.svc.cluster.local` and use only `<service name>.<service namespace>` as the internal DNS for services.

Reference: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/dns-pod-service/#namespaces-of-services

Related to #1396.

Issue:
Allow to copy backups across namespaces
Backups (either manual or managed) are tied to a given namespace. It doesn't matter which cluster they belonged to, as long as those clusters were part of the same namespace. And then restoring a backup, it can only be present in the same namespace.

However, if permissions allow for this, a user may want to restore a backup into another namespace. Since we don't allow for this, this issue tackles copying a backup to another namespace to enable a backup to be effectively restored in another namespace.

The feature will work by just copying the CR backup and with minimal modifications, not the actual backup files (i.e., it will point to the same resources). Considerations for this feature:

*  The copied backup CR will have to point to the cluster using `<cluster namespace>.<cluster name>` syntax in order to allow the backup to point correctly to the stored backup.
*  ~~The copied backup CR will be marked as permanent (i.e. not `subjectToRetentionPolicy`), even if the source CR was a managed one.~~
*  The algorithm to delete the backup resources when a CR needs to be changed. Now, many CRs may point to the same underlying resources, the backup itself, and those can only be deleted when the last CR is deleted.
*  ~~To implement the above, we'd need to implement reference counting (could be a status field in the backup CR with the number of times the physical backup is referenced) or maybe a global `ConfigMap` with the reference counting of every existing backup, managed by StackGres controller.~~
*  ~~We may need to verify that the user has permissions to create a CR on the destination namespace.~~

-----------

There was another issue duplicating this functionality (#489). Closing in favor of this one, but quoting here initial description in that issue for quick reference and completeness:

> The goal is to support "Backup CR cloning". This feature enables a single ("call it physical") backup to be referenced from potentially more than one CR. If either of the CRs or the backup itself are deleted, everything else is also expected to be deleted. A backup may be restored by referencing either of the existing CR UIDs pointing to it.
> We need to be able to augment the current CRD of backup to include an optional field "cloneFromBackup: $UID". Then the user can specify the resulting name and optionally the namespace of the cloned backup. The `cloneFromBackup` field would be exclusive to the current `sgCluster`.

[DISCUSSION]
[teoincontatto]: > And then restoring a backup, it can only be present in the same namespace.

Currently a backup can be used from another namespace without any issue. Please see this e2e test: https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/blob/development/stackgres-k8s/e2e/spec/restore

If this is enough we can think of closing this issue. Feel free to re-open if this is not the case.

> However, if permissions allow for this, a user may want to restore a backup into another namespace. Since we don't allow for this, this issue tackles copying a backup to another namespace to enable a backup to be effectively restored in another namespace.

There is no permission restriction in order to use backups from another namespace. This seems to me a security flaw and should be fixed. To address this and similar flaws I've opened #832 to discuss this separately since it is not a trivial aspect.

Issue:
stackgres-operator Helm chart: allow to configure resources for operator, restapi and amdinui containers
When installing stackgres-operator chart, there is no `resources` definition for the containers in `operator` and `webapi` deployments.

This puts the pods in [`BestEffort` Quality of service class](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/quality-service-pod/).

A user should be able to set resources for each container, to improve the quality of service for the pods.

The solution could be as following:
- For each one of `operator`, `jobs`, `restapi` and `adminui` entries: Add a `resources` object, empty by default, in `values.yaml`
- In the respective containers definitions, add something like the following:
```
{{- with .Values.operator.resources }}
  resources:
{{- toYaml . | nindent 12 }}
{{- end }}
```

Issue:
Support ARM64 when installing extensions
Currently when extensions are installed the architecture used is always x86_64 (aka amd64). This makes impossible the installation of extensions on arm64.

## Implementation plan

The selection of the extension in the mutating webhook must be independent of architecture on first creation of the cluster since, until the first primary Pod is elected, the architecture is unknown to the operator. In such case extensions will be chosen only based on name, version, postgres version and flavor.

When the extension is then installed in the Pod the architecture will be resolved by the cluster controller.

When the primary pod is elected and ready the cluster controller of such Pod will set the architecture in the `SGCluster` under `.status.primaryArch`.

When the mutating webhook check extensions, will be able to filter by architecture when the `.status.primaryArch` is set in `SGCluster` using such value. Since [postgres does not support streaming replication between different architectures](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/59264875/replicating-a-postgresql-database-when-master-is-running-on-arm-and-replication) all the extensions that will be installed on the cluster will always have the same architecture.

## Acceptance Criteria

When creating an `SGCluster` the first time the architecture will not be used to filter extensions. When adding extensions they will be filtered by architecture when the `.status.primaryArch` is set in `SGCluster` using such value.
The cluster controller will detect the architeture where it is running, will use the detected architecture to generate the URL to download extensions and, if it is running in the same Pod that is elected as primary, will set the `.status.primaryArch` in `SGCluster` if not already set.

    greatest(age(pg_class.relfrozenxid), age(toast.relfrozenxid)) as freeze_age,

Now, let me clarify my position. Let me first explain why I believe the latest design is not ideal from a UX perspective. The main culprit is the prominent position of the toggle "Babelfish Experimental Feature". It has to be prominent (otherwise Babelfish button won't even show) but this kills the main purpose of the cluster creation form. Let me explain why with an analogy.

Imagine you want to buy a Porsche 911, and you go to a car dealer. The seller takes you to the car, and goes to explain you the main controls. You are sitting behind the wheel.

* Use case 1. The first thing the seller says is "hey, look at this red button here. It says 'for expert drivers only, use at your own risk'". And then it goes on to explain that with that you can use a 'competition mode', but the insurance won't cover you. That you can drive up to % faster, that the wheel will become stronger, and the distance to the ground smaller. At this point, you are already lost, you lost interest in the car, your mind is only asking "where's the f***ing start button, and how do I turn on the radio?".

* Use case 2. The seller instead shows you first the basic stuff: here's the start button, the radio, volume control, A/C, shift gear... and then, when you have a good overview, or even when you notice yourself that red button, then he goes on to explain what it does and the caveats.

So I'd like here something like this analogy: I don't want to see this "experimental" thing too early or too prominently. I need to focus first on the very main things: postgres version, Postgres configuration. But then I want to see the "flavors". If I don't see the flavors right away, I won't even know what options are available! So I like to have the two buttons and see always from the beginning the "Community" and the "Babelfish (experimental)" (with the `(experimental)` part as part of the name) buttons there. And then iif I select Babelfish, to get a second-level check asking me to reconfirm that I really want to select that one. This check is one that may be hidden and only shown when `Babelfish (experimental)` is selected.

This way I achieve the following, in summary:
* I focus first on the more general use case (nothing experimental) and the main inputs (version, configuration, storage, etc).
* I still see all options available, and one is labeled explicitly as experimental.
* If I select the experimental flavor, a new text+toggle appears to warn me. I then need to take an explicit confirmation that I'm willing to take the risk *specifically for this very thing*, not for a general concept of "experimental stuff".

How this is later encoded internally, it doesn't really matter, we could always map it. However, I believe it matches very clearly: we have encoded it as "feature flags", and them being enabled or not is decided on a feature by feature basis. Here we would be doing exactly that: to enable or not the Babelfish feature flag. Also, BTW, we're preventing a use case that wouldn't make any sense: to enable the Babelfish feature flag but select the Community flavor. While it won't harm anyone, it doesn't make any sense.

Issue:
Log4j2 Vulnerability "Log4Shell" analysis in relation to StackGres
# Background
An exploit for a critical zero-day vulnerability affecting Apache Log4j2 (CVE-2021-44228) known as Log4Shell was disclosed on December 10, 2021. All versions of Log4j2 versions >= 2.0-beta9 and <= 2.14.1 are affected by this vulnerability. This vulnerability is actively being exploited in the wild and allows an attacker to execute code on a remote server; a so-called Remote Code Execution (RCE).

There are many blogs posts and articles that explain the Log4Shell vulnerability, so it's not worth explaining it one more time, please read the following if you wish to know more:
* https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-44228
* https://logging.apache.org/log4j/2.x/security.html
* https://blog.cloudflare.com/inside-the-log4j2-vulnerability-cve-2021-44228/
* https://snyk.io/blog/log4j-rce-log4shell-vulnerability-cve-2021-4428/
* https://blog.checkpoint.com/2021/12/11/protecting-against-cve-2021-44228-apache-log4j2-versions-2-14-1/

# Is StackGres affected by this vulnerability?
The short answer is: NO.

The StackGres platform uses Quarkus as the framework for developing the core components of the operator, and internally, Quarkus uses JBoss Log Manager and the JBoss Logging facade.

* https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/discussions/22108

Currently, StackGres makes use of `SLF4J` API that routes the log messages through `org.jboss.slf4j:slf4j-jboss-logmanager` to the JBoss logging library used by Quarkus, and that library is not affected by the Log4Shell vulnerability.

We do have declared the log4j2 dependency, but only with `test` scope, it's not included in the final, distributed images, and also the test configuration is using `nolookups` that disables this vulnerability and logs the message string untouched. And even then, the log4j dependency was actually not being used directly in any part of StackGres, so the next step is to simply drop the dependency declaration from StackGres since it's not used at all.

# Summary
* StackGres is **NOT** affected by this vulnerability since it uses the Quarkus Logging library instead of Log4j.
* If **your** application does use log4j, please follow the mitigation steps like the upgrade to Log4j v2.16.0+
* This issue is used to track the drop of log4j in the `test` scope since it's not used at all and will be closed once all the references to log4j are deleted from the main repo.

When updating from 1.0.0 to 1.1.0 the images are upgraded
### Summary

When upgrading from 1.0.0 to 1.1.0 all the images of an SGCluster (or SGDistributedLogs) before running any security upgrade SGDbOps.

### Current Behavior 

After StackGres is upgraded the SGCluster (or SGDistributedLogs) should not be in `PendingRestart`.

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Install StackGres 1.0.0
2. Create a cluster
3. Upgrade StackGres to 1.1.0-beta1

### Expected Behavior

After StackGres is upgraded the SGCluster (or SGDistributedLogs) is not in `PendingRestart`.

### Possible Solution

Create a list of previous image versions for all previous StackGres versions and apply accordingly to the operator version annotation present on the SGCluster or SGDistributedLogs

### Environment

- StackGres version: 1.1.0-beta1
- Kubernetes version: ?
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: ?

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

Run e2e test dbops-secutiry-upgrade by setting `STACKGRES_PREVIOUS_VERSION` env var to `1.0.0`.

[DISCUSSION]
[teoincontatto]: Components versions have been refactored into multiple properties files each one with the components versions for current and previous StackGres minor versions:

* `stackgres-k8s/src/common/src/main/resources/versions.properties`: Component versions for current StackGres version
* `stackgres-k8s/src/common/src/main/resources/versions-1.0.properties`: Component versions for StackGres version 1.0
* `stackgres-k8s/src/common/src/main/resources/versions-0.9.properties`: Component versions for StackGres version 0.9

There is known bug that we may want to address in a separate issue (present in previous StackGres versions). Basically the Web UI uses a couple of REST API to retrieve versions of postgresql component that will not return the correct list if the SGCluster is using a previous minor version of StackGres. We may create a new REST API in order to return available postgresql versions for an existing cluster (so we can match the StackGres minor version with the version used for the SGCluster) and use the current REST API that return postgresql component versions for the current StackGres version only for new SGClusters.

Another suspected issue is related to extensions, and this should be fixed in this issue. Basically extensions will use the same metadata version than 1.1 for every previous version and this should change based on version of the cluster. Not sure if this is currently causing any bug but should be addressed since it could easily convert into an issue in the future.

[teoincontatto]: Finally using always the latest version of extensions metadata is not an issue as long as old extensions are not deprecated.

Deprecation of extensions is something that could happen at some point and will affect any version of StackGres that use extensions repository, but how this affect StackGres and how we should handle such cases goes beyond the scope of this issue.

[teoincontatto]: Another bug that has been fixed in this issue is related to deletion of extensions on Pod initialization and changing the Pod status in order to unset the pending restart flag. Since the update of the status could lead to a conflict when using kubernetes API (HTTP 409) and this is ignored during reconciliation in the local controller, the whole cluster could being set as pending restart after a security upgrade. To fix this behavior the conflict error is not ignored during initialization.

Re-implement SGDbOps for minor version upgrade operations
The operator already handle smoothly postgresql minor version upgrade. The operation will also perform the change of value in associated `SGCluster` CR to change the `.spec.postgresVersion` to the new value. 

> **NOTE** major pg version updates must be avoided since not supported. The operator have to print an error message requiring the intervention of the user to perform such update.

This action will be triggered by `SGDbOps` CRD (see #535) when `minorVersionUpgrade` operation is issued. Information about the process will be posted to the `status` field of the CR.

```yaml
spec:
  sgCluster: <string> # The name of sgcluster on which the operation will be performed

When creating a new cluster and describing the CR, we see in the `Status` and `Events` output similar to:

```

    Last Transition Time:  2020-03-18T17:44:05.810Z
    Status:                False

        ClusterUpdated  3s    stackgres-operator  StackGres Cluster default.simple updated
```

What is that `PendingRestart` means? And what is "updated"?

These messages need to provide more detailed information.

# Proposition

Cluster created and updated message should show what created/changed using the following format:

* For each resource created the message will be composed like so: `Cluster <namespace>.<name> [created|updated]: +<resource>[, +<resource>, ...]`
* For each resource deleted the message will be composed like so: `Cluster <namespace>.<name> [created|updated]: -<resource>[, -<resource>, ...]`
* For each resource updated the message will be composed like so: `Cluster <namespace>.<name> [created|updated]: <resource> (<field> -> <new value>[, <field> -> <new value>, ...])[, <resource> (<field> -> <new value>[, <field> -> <new value>, ...]), ...]`
* A `<resource>` is expressed as `<resource kind>:<resource name>`
* A `<field>` is expressed as the `<field path>` (e.g. `/spec/replicas`) prefixed by a `+` or `-` character if it is a new field or a removed field or without prefix if it is a changed field.
* Values for Secret will be obfuscated
* Resources will be ordered by created, deleted and updated and in each grup they will be order by kind, first SGCluster (see below), StatefulSet, CronJob, Job, Pod, Service, Endpoints, ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding, PersistentVolumeClaim, ConfigMap, Secret, then others in alphabetical order
* If too many resources are updated, the log will be stripped to a maximum length of 256 characters becoming like: "`Cluster <namespace>.<name> updated: X (a -> b), Y (c -> d), Z (e -> f) and 7 other resources`"
* In case the change is about number of instances the message will be transformed to: "StatefulSet:<name> (instances have been updated to 2 (cluster instances are now 2))"

> Cross-namespace owner references are disallowed by design.
> 
> Namespaced dependents can specify cluster-scoped or namespaced owners. A namespaced owner must exist in the same namespace as the dependent. If it does not, the owner reference is treated as absent, and the dependent is subject to deletion once all owners are verified absent.
> 
> Cluster-scoped dependents can only specify cluster-scoped owners. In v1.20+, if a cluster-scoped dependent specifies a namespaced kind as an owner, it is treated as having an unresolvable owner reference, and is not able to be garbage collected.
> 
> In v1.20+, if the garbage collector detects an invalid cross-namespace ownerReference, or a cluster-scoped dependent with an ownerReference referencing a namespaced kind, a warning Event with a reason of OwnerRefInvalidNamespace and an involvedObject of the invalid dependent is reported. You can check for that kind of Event by running kubectl get events -A --field-selector=reason=OwnerRefInvalidNamespace.

This means that from Kubernetes 1.20+ resources with cross-namespace owner references will be deleted. This can be seen for `ServiceMonitor` created in `prometheus-integration-default` E2E test when testing #950 with Kubenrnetes 1.20:

[teoincontatto]: Following YAML represent the structure of the node affinity inside of a sgcluster CR. A `<nodeSelectorTerm>` represents a node selector term described below.

```yaml
spec:
  pods:
    scheduling:
      nodeAffinity:
        preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          - preference:
              <nodeSelectorTerm>
            weight: <integer>
        requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          nodeSelectorTerms:
            - <nodeSelectorTerm>
```

# Node selector term

A `<nodeSelectorRequirement>` represents a node selector requirement described below.

```yaml
matchExpressions:
  - <nodeSelectorRequirement>
matchFields:
  - <nodeSelectorRequirement>
```

# Node selector requirement

```yaml
key: <string> # a label or a field
operator: <string> # enum (In|NotIn|Exists|DoesNotExist|Gt|Lt)
values: # array of stirngs interpreted depending on the `operator` value
  - <string>
```

## Operators constraints

* `In`: `values` must not be empty
* `NotIn`: `values` must not be empty
* `Exists`: `values` must be empty
* `DoesNotExists`: `values` must be empty
* `Gt`: `values` must have a single element that must be parsed to integer
* `Lt`: `values` must have a single element that must be parsed to integer

While we strive for maximum compatibility with the Kubernetes versions that we support, we also need to be able to leverage new features present in newer versions, and there must be a clearly minimum supported versions. Also, we need to be aware of the release and support versions of Kubernetes, and what major players in the market are doing.

Note that K8s releases happen, approximately, every three months. And that up to 1.18 they were supported for 9 months, and one year starting with 1.19. This means that currently only three versions are supported (currently 1.17 to 1.19).

This issue proposes to open a ~Discussion on what is the minimum K8s version that we support. As of today, it is 1.11. This issue proposes to bump the minimum version supported to 1.16 (which is even EOL as of today from K8s perspective). Main reasons:

* CRDs are moved to GA in this release. We rely in CRDs extensively, by design, and as such we should rely on GA versions of them. Also, significant changes were introduced in this release for CRDs.
* Also webhooks are GA in 1.16.
* Notable enhancements to volume extension, even if in beta, but important for us as a database operator.
* It introduces, even in alpha, ephemeral containers. This would allow us to change the `postgres-util` into an ephemeral container, which is what it should be.
* Similarly in alpha, but [Pod Topology Spread Constraints](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-topology-spread-constraints/) are introduced. I believe they are a very important part to ensure realistic production scenarios of any complexity.
* Possibly other improvements present in earlier versions of K8s which we might now specifically leverage.
* Last but not least, the ongoing work to support CRD upgrades has to support different cases for versions earlier than 1.16. By raising the bar to 1.16 we would clean up code and implement a single version of the CRD upgrade process.

A quick check on major K8s platforms shows that 1.16 (or higher) is always an option:

| Environment | Versions supported   | Notes                               |
|-------------|----------------------|-------------------------------------|
| EKS         | 1.14-1.17            |                                     |
| GKE         | 1.15-1.18            | (1.15 by default)                   |
| AKS         | 1.16-1.18            | By Nov 2020 it will be 1.17-1.19    |
| OpenShift   | 4.3: 1.16, 4.4: 1.17 | 4.2 is 1.14, but is EOL as of today |


While significant effort was recently done to support 1.11 and OpenShift 3.11, most of that effort improved in general the state of SG, and is thus well amortized.

Basic support to skip reconciliation cycle is provided by #658. There are more advanced scenario where a user would like to skip reconciliation cycle for configuration CRDs.

The proposal is to have the annotation `stackgres.io/reconciliation-pause` with value `true` on the object such that, if present, the controller will not perform the reconciliation cycle on this object and change behaviour. This annotation may be present on:

* `sginstanceprofile` CR resources: the operator will not modify the value of statefulset fields `.spec.template.spec.containers.<index>.resources` in the reconciliation cycle for those `sgcluster` that uses such `sginstanceprofile`.

* `sgpoolingconfig` CR resources: the operator will not modify the pooling configmap in the reconciliation cycle for those `sgcluster` that uses such `sgpoolingconfig`.
* `sgbackupconfig` CR resources: the operator will not modify the backup cronjob and any environment variable in the cluster statefulset for patroni container in the reconciliation cycle for those `sgcluster` that uses such `sgbackupconfig`.
* `sgbackup` CR resources: the operator will not modify the backup job created in the reconciliation cycle for those `sgcluster` to which such `sgbackup` points to.

Issue:

[Babelfish for Postgres](https://babelfish-for-postgresql.github.io/babelfish-for-postgresql/) is an enhanced Postgres with SQL Server compatibility, at both the SQL, T-SQL and wire compatibility levels.

As it is open source (under Apache 2 license) we would like to offer Babelfish as an option for StackGres users. It is not published yet. Assuming it would be a drop-in replacement, it should work as-is, for the most part.

Among possibly others, the following changes would be required:
1. Add `SGCluster.postgresFamily` optional field, which would be an enum `[postgresql|babelfish]`. If unset, it would default to `postgresql`.
1. Depending on the versioning scheme, the `postgresVersion` field may need to be adjusted, including validations.
1. Related to the two items above, a new higher level object `postgres` may be created, with two child properties: `family` and `version`. The current `postgresVersion` could remain to be backwards compatible.
1. TDS-required ports may need to be opened. We will need to evaluate whether they may be proxied through Envoy or not, including performance evaluation.
1. New Service(s) may need to be exposed.

Other considerations will be evaluated more precisely when Babelfish is published.

When operator helm chart creates the certificate singing request it should not just check it is approved but also should wait for the certificate field to be filled. This is because the two operations are asynchronous:

> For certificates that have been approved, the next step is signing. The relevant signing controller first validates that the signing conditions are met and then creates a certificate. > 
> Once the status.certificate field has been populated, the request has been completed and clients can now fetch the signed certificate PEM data from the CertificateSigningRequest resource. The signers can instead deny certificate signing if the approval conditions are not met.

Issue:
Not using Patroni service to publish read/write DNS
Currently StackGres is publishing the primary service through a service backed by Kubernetes readiness probe. We should instead use the service backed by Patroni to avoid split brain. This is because Patroni controls the service Endpoints and update the primary lock and the address in the same place that guarantee the information of primary address is correct even in a split brain situation.

See also https://patroni.readthedocs.io/en/latest/kubernetes.html#use-endpoints

> # Use Endpoints
> 
> Despite the fact that this is the recommended mode, it is turned off by default for compatibility reasons. When it is on, Patroni stores the cluster configuration and the leader key in the metadata: annotations fields of the respective Endpoints it creates. Changing the leader is safer than when using ConfigMaps, since both the annotations, containing the leader information, and the actual addresses pointing to the running leader pod are updated simultaneously in one go.

[DISCUSSION]
[ahachete]: Yes, this is really important.

[teoincontatto]: # Approach 1

Seems that the Endpoints that Patroni uses for leader lock and set with the addresses of elected leader has a name set to the cluster name. The idea is that we can change the Patroni scope (the cluster name used by Patroni) to be our primary service name (cluster name + "-primary"). That would also mean:

1. We need to set a specific label for Patroni cluster name. Currently Patroni is using "cluster_name" that is used by the operator so we need another label for Patroni like "patroni_cluster_name".
2. All commands with `patronictl` will require to use the cluster name + "-primary" to refer to the name of the cluster instead of just the cluster name (that is a bit weird). Changes in code and doc.

This change is quite disruptive for running clusters and may require an hard to implement upgrade procedure.

# Approach 2

Change the current primary service type to be ExternalName and point to the service with just cluster name. The problem of this approach is that the current primary service type will have a fixed type and the type configured in sgcluster will apply to the service backed by Endpoints created by Patroni.

This change can bring problems to the upgrade of already running cluster, in particular if they have the primary service configured with "LoadBalancer" since the DNS will change making required a change in the clients.

# Approach 3

Remove the label selector from the current primary service and make the operator create the relative Endpoints to point to the IP assigned to the service backed by Endpoints created by Patroni.

# Proposed solution

The proposed solution is to use the approach 3 since is quite simple and has no drawbacks.

Issue:
Implement the UI for sgdbops
SGDbOps are automatic database operations.

There is a set of options that are common to all operations:

* sgCluster: The name of SGCluster on which the operation will be performed
* runAt: An ISO 8601 date, that holds UTC scheduled date of the operation execution. If not specified or date it’s in the past it will be interpreted as ASAP.
* timeout: An ISO 8601 duration format `PnDTnHnMn.nS`, that specify a timeout after which the operation execution will not be performed. If the operation can not be performed due to timeout expiration the condition `Failed` will have a status of `True` and and the reason will be `TimedOut`. If not specified the operation will never fail for timeout expiration.
* maxRetries: The maximum number of retries the operation is allowed to do after a failure. If not specified this default to `1`. Can not be greater than `10`.

The CRD currently define the following operations but new operation could be added in the future:

* op: The kind of operation that will be performed on the SGCluster. Available operations are:
  * `benchmark`: run a benchmark on the specified SGCluster and report the results in the status.
  * `vacuum`: perform a [vacuum](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-vacuum.html) operation on the specified SGCluster.
  * `repack`: run [`pg_repack`](https://github.com/reorg/pg_repack) command on the specified SGCluster.
  * `majorVersionUpgrade`: perform a major version upgrade of PostgreSQL using [`pg_upgrade`](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/pgupgrade.html) command.
  * `restart`: perform a restart of the cluster.
  * `minorVersionUpgrade`: perform a minor version upgrade of PostgreSQL.
  * `securityUpgrade`: perform a security upgrade of the cluster.

Please refer to the StackGres REST API documentation to view all the available sections: https://stackgres.io/doc/latest/07-stackgres-web-api/03-api-reference
You can also refer to the `SGDbOps` CRD documentation for more info: https://stackgres.io/doc/latest/reference/crd/sgdbops/

    persistentVolume:
      size: '10Gi'

....
```

Then you get the error: 

```
error: error validating "10b-SGCluster.yaml": error validating data: ValidationError(SGCluster.spec.pods.metadata): unknown field "annotations" in io.stackgres.v1.SGCluster.spec.pods.metadata; if you choose to ignore these errors, turn validation off with --validate=false
```

### Possible Solution

Refactor label and annotation specs for the CRD using following structure:

```
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v2
kind: SGCluster
metadata:
  namespace: ongres-db
  name: ongres-db
spec:

....
```

Issue:
Add task dependencies among SGDbOps
**This is a confidential issue. Please do not share publicly**

`SGDbOps` is a great abstraction to model "Day 2 operations" with StackGres. But more often than not, you may want to "chain" tasks, execute one only after another one has finished.

The goal of this issue is to capture this reality, and introduce the concept of an SGDbOps to optionally depend on another one. The changes to the CRD could be similar to adding the following optional object to the spec:

```yaml
dependsOn:
    sgDbOp: $name
    expectedResult: enum (COMPLETED, FAILED) # optional, COMPLETED by default
    runAfter: iso_8601_duration # optional, default 0
```

It is assumed that the parent and dependant SGDbOp need to be in the same namespace (and hence reference each other).

This architecture allows for arbitrarily complex dependency graphs. This allows for great flexibility in automating database task execution, without having to create a much more complex specific runtime to allow for programmability within SG. This is a quick way of supporting a very broad set of automation problems for the database.

The operator must ensure upon CR validation phase that dependency graphs are strictly tree-like (there are no loops).

Issue:
Support Postgres 13
We need to provide support for Postgres 13 major versions and remove the Postgres 11 major versions.

We have to make sure user will have a means to upgrade to Postgres 12 before upgrading to the new version of operator that does not support Postgres 11. So the dbops (`op == securityUpgrade`) that upgrade the cluster to ~"target_version::1.0.0-beta1" should make sure that the major version of Postgres is 12 using the validating webhook. If not, the user will then be forced to perform a major version upgrade before upgrading the cluster to ~"target_version::1.0.0-beta1". Since for version up to %"StackGres 0.9" there is no automatic database operation mechanism we should include the mechanism in the documentation.

## Major version upgrade for %"StackGres 0.9" 

* Having an old cluster with PG11. Lets call it `pg11`
* Set `pg11` instances to 1.
* Create a new cluster of 1 instance with PG12. Lets call it `pg12` by copying the `pg11` spec and only changing `.spec.instances` and `.spec.postgresVersion`:

```shell
kubectl get sgcluster pg11 -o json | jq '.metadata.name = "pg12" | .spec.instances = 1 | .spec.postgresVersion = "12"' | kubectl create sgcluster -f -
```

* From `patroni` container of `pg12` do a `pg_dump` and store it in the PV:

```shell
kubectl exec -ti pg12-0 -c patroni -- sh -c 'PGPASSWORD=*** pg_dumpall -h pg11-primary | psql'
```

* Then remove the old cluster `pg11`

[DISCUSSION]
[teoincontatto]: Updated description with required checks for SGDbOps that upgrades cluster to the latest operator version.

[jorsol]: To give proper support to PostgreSQL 13, Patroni needs to be upgraded to 2.x: https://github.com/zalando/patroni/blob/master/docs/releases.rst#version-200

[jorsol]: Supporting a new version should not depend on upgrading the cluster, we can support PostgreSQL 13 while still having PostgreSQL 11 around, just like we support PostgreSQL 12 and 11 at the same time.

It's also hard to force users to upgrade to a new major version, and more if that version is still supported, if we force the upgrade many users would not use StackGres since they can't upgrade or test their applications every time we drop support of an older release.

[adescoms]: Our philosophy is that we only support the last 2 Postgres Major versions for `StackGres OS`, that's why if we add support for PostgreSQL 13, we remove the support for Postgres 11. 

Not sure if we could allow the upgrade of StackGres without force the upgrade of the last Major version (PG11 at this moment) so that it could work, for example, SG v1.0.0 with PG11, even if we don't support it. 

OTOH, this is blocked until we can upgrade Patroni to 2.x version, https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/issues/774

[jorsol]: Sure, we can only support only 2 major versions, but I'm not sure if forcing an upgrade would be beneficial, most users would not upgrade StackGres if they are forced to upgrade Postgres.

And yes, this is blocked until we can upgrade Patroni to 2.x, still, the force upgrade should be discussed with great care.

[adescoms]: The `stackgres OS` policy will be: we only support the last 2 Postgres Major versions. If you want to upgrade StackGres you must have one of the two supported versions, otherwise, we don't let you upgrade the StackGres version. 

For example, if you are running StackGres OS `0.9.5` with Postgres 11, you have to upgrade to Postgres 12 before being able to upgrade to StackGres `1.0.0`

This should be a precheck in the StackGres upgrade (@xaviersierra)

[xaviersierra]: We have two kinds of upgrades that we need to consider here. 

We have the operator upgrade, which we can't prevent the user from doing it. And the security upgrade, which is a migration of a SGCluster in an old StackGres version to the latest one. 

If the user has a SGCluster from StackGres version 0.9.5 with Postgres 11, and the user upgrades the operator to 1.0.0, the SGCluster in 0.9.5 would still be working as usual. 

What the user should not be able to do, is a security upgrade without doing a major version upgrade to Postgres 12 or 13. 

Bear in mind, that StackGres 0.9.5 doesn't provide a major version upgrade feature. Therefore, to make easy for users to migrate to Postgres 12 or 13, they should be able to upgrade the operator to version 1.0.0.

[teoincontatto]: We should then also provide a procedure to perform major version upgrade in StackGres 0.9, a section similar to the one that document how to [restart a cluster]() but for major version upgrade.

The problem here is that the procedure to perform a major version upgrade using `pg_upgrade` is very hard to perform in StackGres 0.9 since requires some steps that involve modify the StatefulSet (you have to copy binaries from PG11 container to the PV and mount them in the PG12 container. The best option here is probably to document a major version upgrade backing up data using `pg_dumpall` from cluster with PG11 and restoring it using `psql` on a fresh cluster with PG12. Something like:

* Having an old cluster with PG11. Lets call it `pg11`
* Set `pg11` instances to 1.
* Create a new cluster of 1 instance with PG12. Lets call it `pg12` by copying the `pg11` spec and only changing `.spec.instances` and `.spec.postgresVersion`:

```bash
kubectl get sgcluster pg11 -o json | jq '.metadata.name = "pg12" | .spec.instances = 1 | .spec.postgresVersion = "12"' | kubectl create sgcluster -f -
```

* From `patroni` container of `pg12` do a `pg_dump` and store it in the PV:

```bash
kubectl exec -ti pg12-0 -c patroni -- sh -c 'PGPASSWORD=*** pg_dumpall -h pg11-primary > /var/lib/postgresql/dump-pg11.sql'
```

* From `patroni` container of `pg12` do a `psql` and feed it with the dump in the PV:

```bash
kubectl exec -ti pg12-0 -c patroni -- sh -c 'psql < /var/lib/postgresql/dump-pg11.sql'
```

* Then remove the old cluster `pg11`

[ahachete]: Slightly related, but if we do https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/issues/1127, then this could also be referenced as a potential option for the user to perform an upgrade.

[teoincontatto]: Also, to avoid storing the dump in the PV, do dump/restore in a single step:

```bash
kubectl exec -ti pg12-0 -c patroni -- sh -c 'PGPASSWORD=*** pg_dumpall -h pg11-primary | psql'
```

This happen if some configuration modify the Pod resource, some parameters that requires restart is changed or some extensions requires the cluster to be restarted to complete an install or uninstall operation. I don't think marking the operation as `Failed` is good since the operation does what it was meant for: "Restart those Pods that requires restart" (as long as anything new happens that makes those Pods to requires restart again). I would prefer to mark it as `Completed` and add a counter like `.status.initalInstancesRequiringRestart`.

Also IMO we should document better than only those Pods that requires restart are restarted (unless forced, if finally implemented).

[jorsol]: I agree that a restart operation should do a restart regardless it's needed or not, but to avoid potential downtime it makes sense to use a new boolean field to force the restart, in this case, that would be a new feature.

initialData:

  op: <string> # majorVersionUpgrade
  schedule: <string> # An ISO 8601 date, that holds UTC scheduled date of the operation execution.

  timeout: <string> # An ISO 8601 duration format `PnDTnHnMn.nS`, that specify a timeout after which the operation execution will not be performed.

  maxRetries: <integer> # The maximum number of retries the operation is allowed to do after a failure. If not specified this default to `1`. Can not be greater than `10`.
  majorVersionUpgrade:
    postgresVersion: <string> # (required) the target postgres version to upgrade (or downgrade).
    sgPostgresConfig: <string> # (required) the new postgres configuration to use with the same target postgres major version. 
    link: <boolean>
    clone: <boolean>
    check: <boolean>
status:

  opRetries: <integer> # The number of retries performed by the operation
  majorVersionUpgrade:
    sourcePostgresVersion: <string> # The postgres version currently used by primary instance
    targetPostgresVersion: <string> # The postgres version that the cluster will be upgraded (or downgraded) to
    primaryInstance: <string>

* If specified `.spec.majorVersionUpgrade.postgresVersion` has same major version than the one specified by the associated `SGCluster` `.spec.postgresVersion` the validating webhook will return the error "major version upgrade operation can not be used to upgrade to a PostgreSQL minor version".

Following validations of `SGCluster` will apply:

* If `.spec.postgresVersion` is modified with a version that has a different major version than the previous the validating webhook will return the error "Use SGDbOps with `op = majorVersionUpgrade` to perform minor version upgrade of PostgreSQL".

Issue:
Allow more customization for pgbouncer
### Problem to solve

Currently it is not possible to customize a little bit more pgbouncer deployment, you can only specify the parameters to modify that correspond to `[pgbouncer]` section.

Pooling configuration in SG:

```
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1beta1
kind: SGPoolingConfig
metadata:
  name: poolconfig
spec:
  pgBouncer:
    pgbouncer.ini:
      pool_mode: session
      default_pool_size: '300'
...
```

This generate a configuration file like:

```
$ kubectl exec -it -n gitlab-db gitlab-db-0 -c pgbouncer -- cat /etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini
[databases]
 * = port = 5432

[pgbouncer]
listen_port = 6432
unix_socket_dir = /var/run/postgresql
stats_users = postgres
ignore_startup_parameters = extra_float_digits
auth_type = md5
max_db_connections = 0
pool_mode = session
auth_query = SELECT usename, passwd FROM pg_shadow WHERE usename=$1
application_name_add_host = 1
log_disconnections = 1
max_client_conn = 2000
log_stats = 1
log_connections = 1
default_pool_size = 20
max_user_connections = 0
auth_user = authenticator
listen_addr = 127.0.0.1
admin_users = postgres
```

But pgbouncer has three main sections:

1- `[databases]`: To specify database connections.

2- `[users]`: To add some custom configuration for some users

3- `[pgbouncer]` :  To add pgbouncer configurations parameters 


And right now ong the the 3 section is allowed to be modified.

### Further details

In some environments it is required to add some user restrictions like amount of connectios allowed for a user or using different pool mode like : 

```
[users]
user1 = pool_mode=transaction max_user_connections=20
user2 = pool_mode=session max_user_connections=50
```

### Proposal

Add to SGPoolingConfig CRD the options to configure the 3 differents sections:

```
apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1beta1
kind: SGPoolingConfig
metadata:
  name: poolconfig
spec:
  pgBouncer:
    pgbouncer.ini:
      databases:  # optional and if not added * = port = 5432 should be the default
        gitlab:
          host: gitlab-db
          port: 5433
          dbname: gitlab
          auth_user: pgbouncer
          pool_size: 100
       users_custom_config:   #Optional
          user1:
            pool_mode: transaction
            max_user_connections: 50
          user2:
            pool_mode: session
            max_user_connections: 100
       parameters:
         pool_mode: session
         default_pool_size: '20'
         max_db_connections: 200
```

And this should generate a configuration like: 

```
$cat /etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini
[databases]
gitlab = host=localhost port=5432  auth_user=pgbouncer dbname=gitlab pool_size=100

[users]
user1 = pool_mode=transaction max_user_connections=50
user2 = pool_mode=session max_user_connections=100

[pgbouncer]
default_pool_size = 50
max_db_connections = 200
pool_mode = session
listen_addr = 127.0.0.1
...
```

### Links / references

https://www.pgbouncer.org/config.html

Classify as SMELL or NO_SMELL based on whether it describes architectural problems.

Answer (SMELL or NO_SMELL):

2. Create a StackGres cluster with 2 instances

### Expected Behaviour

Patroni nodes are not failing over

### Possible Solution

Annotations should not be overwritten but merged:

* Required annotations will overwrite exiting annotations with the same key or, if no existing annotation match the same key, will be added.
* Existing annotations will not be removed if no required annotation match its key.

# Server Side Apply Considerations
Server side apply has been enabled by default in kubernetes 1.16 and later, and provides some
advantages that we could take advantage of.
 
Here I try to explain its implications for StackGres when it's enabled, and how we can benefit
from it.
 
## What is it
It's a mechanism of kubernetes to keep track of who modifies what and intent to prevent conflict
by assigning owners to every applied field.
 
For a more in depth explanation of what server side apply is, please check the [kubernetes
documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/server-side-apply/)
 
## What we do at the moment
At the moment of this writing, we don't support SSA. If one of the operator generated resource has
some SSA configuration the operator we just get rid of it.
 
## What we could gain of using SSA
Currently, every time that the operator detects a resource out of sync, in most cases StackGres
will replace the existing resource with the in sync version.
 
This strategy comes with some problems. Specifically there could be changes that comes from k8s,
that the operator could detect as out of sync. The operator handle this scenarios
but still can have some problems.
 
### Skipping resource comparison
Consider the case of the primary service endpoint.
 
Given a SGCluster named `simple`, the primary service endpoint would like this:
 
``` yaml

 annotations:
   acquireTime: "2021-07-14T17:10:36.630841+00:00"

   transitions: "0"
   ttl: "30"
 creationTimestamp: "2021-07-14T17:10:33Z"
 labels:
   app: StackGresCluster
   cluster: "true"
   cluster-name: simple
   cluster-uid: 9e255311-31ac-4cc9-9e27-e96c4e618a30
 name: simple
 namespace: default
 ownerReferences:
 - apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
   controller: true
   kind: SGCluster
   name: simple
   uid: 9e255311-31ac-4cc9-9e27-e96c4e618a30
 resourceVersion: "5988"
 selfLink: /api/v1/namespaces/default/endpoints/simple
 uid: 01ac8f78-4c6d-47cb-8425-2d9e6ecf1f20
subsets:
- addresses:
 - hostname: simple-0
   ip: 10.244.0.17
   nodeName: kind-control-plane
   targetRef:
     kind: Pod
     name: simple-0
     namespace: default
     resourceVersion: "3733"
     uid: 2f006c5a-fab6-4b62-ab70-c0518ca483df
 ports:
 - name: pgport
   port: 7432
   protocol: TCP
 - name: pgreplication
   port: 7433
   protocol: TCP
```
 
In this case, the StackGres operator only manage directly the fields:
* metadata.ownerReferences
* metadata.labels
 
The rest of the fields are managed by Patroni or Kubernetes.
 
In order to maintain the endpoint in sync the operator needs to do the following steps:
* Generate the required endpoint
* Compare it with the one that is already created
* If there is a difference with the fields that are managed by StackGres, patch the resource
 
If SSA is implemented, the operator could skip the second step and just send patches all the time.
 
The patch would be equivalent to this command:
``` sh
cat << EOF | kubectl apply --server-side=true --field-manager="StackGres" -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Endpoints
metadata:
 name: simple
 namespace: default
 labels:
   app: StackGresCluster
   cluster: "true"
   cluster-name: simple
   cluster-uid: 9e255311-31ac-4cc9-9e27-e96c4e618a30
 ownerReferences:
 - apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
   controller: true
   kind: SGCluster
   name: simple
   uid: 9e255311-31ac-4cc9-9e27-e96c4e618a30
EOF
```
 
Since its using SSA the flag --server-side=true, it would interfere with the rest of the fields.
And only if there is an actual difference it would be applied.
 
### Avoid accidental field deletion
Continuing with the previous case, consider a case in which the StackGres operator
needs to add an annotation. Currently, the operator would handle the patch as following command:
 
``` sh
cat << EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Endpoints

   cluster-name: simple
   cluster-uid: 9e255311-31ac-4cc9-9e27-e96c4e618a30

 - apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
   controller: true
   kind: SGCluster
   name: simple
   uid: 9e255311-31ac-4cc9-9e27-e96c4e618a30

```
 
The above command has a side effect that it would delete the rest of the fields that are not
managed directly by the operator like subnets, or the Patroni annotations. In this case,
Patroni and Kubernetes would re-create its data but there is a brief moment in which the
resource doesn't have it.
 
By using SSA, the other fields would not be altered. Hence, the problem its avoided.

This outcome can be confusing, because on one side it says that Patroni is the owner of
the annotations: acquireTime, leader, optime, renewTime, transitions and ttl; and also the
field subsets. On the other side okhttp is the owner of the OwnerReferences field, and the labels:

The actual owner of the okhttp fields is the StackGres operator, but since it's not specified,
kubernetes calculates the field based on the User-Agent of the HTTP Request, okhttp its just

if other applications use the okhttp as a client to interact with Kubernetes API,  Kubernetes

By using the field manager flag, it is possible to specify to kubernetes who is actual owner of those,
which, in this case is StackGres
 
### Tolerate user changes
 
By using SSA the StackGres operator would focus only in the fields it manages, this allow to users
to make changes on the generated resources without the operator to be  aware of.
 
This can be useful in some scenarios like the following:
 
Suppose that in a kubernetes cluster there is a mutation webhook in place that add an annotation
with a key `department` value `security` to every Secret in the cluster, regardless of who have
created those Secrets.
 
Such webhook would make our database credential secret to look like this (Notice the department
annotation):
 
``` yaml

kind: Secret

   cluster-name: simple
   cluster-uid: c4554cdd-c351-4313-80df-ead7bd679dd6

 - apiVersion: stackgres.io/v1
   controller: true
   kind: SGCluster
   name: simple
   uid: c4554cdd-c351-4313-80df-ead7bd679dd6
 resourceVersion: "27682"
 selfLink: /api/v1/namespaces/default/secrets/simple
 uid: 7726f761-e746-4107-a0d3-801f66cfddee
type: Opaque
```
 
In a case like this, the operator would detect the Secret as out of sync, and proceed to delete
the annotation. Then the webhook would add the annotation again making the resource to appear to
be out of sync, resulting in an endless loop.
 
By using SSA, the operator would not care about such differences as long as the fields that are
managed by StackGres remains unaltered.
 
This behavior would also allow users to play with the generated StackGres resources on their own,
which can be useful to solve unexpected issues in some environments.
 
### What happens if the Server Side Apply feature gate its disabled?
Since the SSA support its in beta since 1.16, its enabled by default. Nonetheless, users can still
disable this feature gate.
 
If the SSA feature gate is disabled, it would cause that every request that have the --server-side
flag to fail.
 
At this moment, this would suppose a problem, but if we start to rely on SSA it could.
 
Nonetheless, we have alternatives to achieve a similar behavior that SSA would provide for us.
 
Currently, every time that the operator is going to make a patch of a resource it makes an operation
similar to this:
 
``` java
client.apps()
   .configmaps()
   .inNamespace(namespace)
   .withName(name)
   .patch(configmap);
```
 
This results in an actual replacement of the resource, this is because fabric8 internally, would get
the resource to patch. Can be seen [here](https://github.com/fabric8io/kubernetes-client/blob/0f1e4873ba1d2816eeeba67241aa534ea7d4ad51/kubernetes-client/src/main/java/io/fabric8/kubernetes/client/dsl/base/HasMetadataOperation.java#L160).
 
 
Then it would calculate its difference with the given resource. As can seen [here](https://github.com/fabric8io/kubernetes-client/blob/0f1e4873ba1d2816eeeba67241aa534ea7d4ad51/kubernetes-client/src/main/java/io/fabric8/kubernetes/client/dsl/base/OperationSupport.java#L350)
 
Also, it assumes that the patch type is `json`.  Looking into the fabric8 code a warning can be found
of this behavior [here](https://github.com/fabric8io/kubernetes-client/blob/0f1e4873ba1d2816eeeba67241aa534ea7d4ad51/kubernetes-client/src/main/java/io/fabric8/kubernetes/client/dsl/Patchable.java#L23):
 
 
In order to avoid this, we can change the way of StackGres makes patches to something
like this:
 
``` java
client.apps()
   .configmaps()
   .inNamespace(namespace)
   .withName(name)
   .patch(new PatchContext.Builder()
       .withPatchType(PatchType.JSON_MERGE)
       .build(), resource);
```
 
By specifying the JSON_MERGE as the patch type, we can avoid fabric8 to get the resource to patch and
calculate its differences, instead it would send the given object as the patch and let kubernetes
to perform the merge.
 
More information about this can be found [here] (https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/manage-kubernetes-objects/update-api-object-kubectl-patch/#use-a-strategic-merge-patch-to-update-a-deployment)
 
Using this strategy, could only prevent the accidental field deletion and resource skipping resource comparison.
 
## Is Server Side Apply bullet proof?
No, users can intentionally or unintentionally override the SSA configuration, hence the
operator must be prepared for these scenarios.
 
Suppose that StackGres creates an resource in the following manner:
 
``` sh
 cat << EOF | kubectl apply --server-side=true --field-manager="StackGres" -f -

[xaviersierra]: After doing a proof of concept, I realized that it's not possible to implement 
  Server Side Apply using only what fabric8 provides.
 
In order to support SSA, all kubernetes clients need to be set as content type 
  `application/apply-patch+yaml`. All media types supported by fabric8 are 
  listed in the OperationSupport [here](https://github.com/fabric8io/kubernetes-client/blob/c24152096f1a0438be1cd4978bea23a8dc185334/kubernetes-client/src/main/java/io/fabric8/kubernetes/client/dsl/base/OperationSupport.java#L58). As it can be seen this

Furthermore, all PATCH requests with the content type `application/apply-patch+yaml` 
  need to set the metadata.managedFields fields as `null`. Otherwise, Kubernetes 
  responds with the following message:
``` json
{
  "kind":"Status",
  "apiVersion":"v1",
  "metadata":{
    
  },
  "status":"Failure",
  "message":"metadata.managedFields must be nil",
  "reason":"BadRequest",
  "code":400
}
```

In short, SSA is not supported by fabric8.
 
Nonetheless, it's possible to implement SSA. In which case I can see two alternatives.

- Extending the DefaultKubernetesClient class and adding a serverSideApply method.
  Here is an example of what we can do:

  ``` java
    import java.io.IOException;
    import java.net.URL;
    import java.util.Objects;
    import java.util.Optional;

    import io.fabric8.kubernetes.api.model.HasMetadata;
    import io.fabric8.kubernetes.api.model.Status;
    import io.fabric8.kubernetes.client.DefaultKubernetesClient;
    import io.fabric8.kubernetes.client.KubernetesClientException;
    import io.fabric8.kubernetes.client.utils.Serialization;
    import okhttp3.MediaType;
    import okhttp3.OkHttpClient;
    import okhttp3.Request;
    import okhttp3.RequestBody;
    import okhttp3.Response;

    public class CustomKubernetesClient extends DefaultKubernetesClient {

    public static final MediaType APPLY_PATCH
        = MediaType.get("application/apply-patch+yaml");

    private static final String SERVER_SIDE_APPLY_PATH_FORMAT =
        "/api/v1/namespaces/%s/%s/%s?fieldManager=%s";

    public <T extends HasMetadata> T serverSideApply(String fieldManager, T intent) {

        var plural = HasMetadata.getPlural(intent.getClass());

        var name = intent.getMetadata().getName();

        var namespace = Optional.ofNullable(intent.getMetadata().getNamespace())
            .orElseGet(() -> Optional.ofNullable(getNamespace())
                .orElse("default"));

        var masterURL = getMasterUrl();

        intent.getMetadata().setManagedFields(null);

        try {
        var applyUrl = new URL(masterURL, String.format(SERVER_SIDE_APPLY_PATH_FORMAT,
            namespace, plural, name, fieldManager));

        String content = Serialization.jsonMapper().valueToTree(intent).toString();

        RequestBody body = RequestBody.create(APPLY_PATCH, content);

        Request request = new Request.Builder()
            .url(applyUrl)
            .patch(body)
            .build();

        OkHttpClient client = getHttpClient();

        try (Response response = client.newCall(request).execute()) {
          Objects.requireNonNull(response.body());
          String responseString = response.body().string();

          if (response.isSuccessful()) {
            return (T) Serialization.unmarshal(responseString, intent.getClass());
          } else {
            var status = Serialization.unmarshal(responseString, Status.class);
            throw new KubernetesClientException(status);
          }
        }

        } catch (IOException e) {
        throw new RuntimeException(e);
        }

      }

    }

  ```
  This has the advantage of requiring very few lines of code. Nonetheless, it breaks
   the fluent style of fabric8 API.

You are an expert software architect analyzing GitHub issues.


An architectural smell is a design problem indicating violations of fundamental design principles:
- Big Dependency Cycle (BDC): Circular dependencies between components violating architectural layering
- Link Overload (LO): One component has too many dependencies


Issue:
One reconciliation loop per resource creating/managing CRD
Actually we have two main reconciliation loops, with some "sub loops":

* `SGCluster`, with sub loops:
    * `SGBackups`
    * `SGDbOps`
* `SGDistributedLogs`

According to CNCF's [Operator White Paper](https://github.com/cncf/tag-app-delivery/blob/eece8f7307f2970f46f100f51932db106db46968/operator-wg/whitepaper/Operator-WhitePaper_v1-0.md#one-crd-per-controller) it is a good practice to have one controller per CRD. That doesn't mean that the controllers need to be separate container images --they may belong to the same container image or even executable. But from a code perspective, it should be structured following this best practice --if we agree it is a best practice, and this issue vouches for this.

To refine the statement, this issue proposes that every CRD that creates/manages any resources (and not only represents metadata) should have its own "controller", understanding by controller its own reconciliation cycle. This includes the case of CRDs that do not create "direct" resources but rather create other CRs. They need also a reconciliation cycle.

From this perspective, the following current CRDs should have the code refactor such that they will have their own independent reconciliation cycle:

* `SGCluster`
* `SGDistributedLogs`
* `SGBackup`
* `SGDbOps`

Once #1190 is implemented, `SGDistributedLogs` will have its reconciliation loop modified, but still would be required to control the generation of the appropriate custom `SGCluster` CRs.

I believe we should keep number alignment as it is now:

Method `io.stackgres.operator.app.ReconciliationClockImpl.reconcile` is called from `java.util.concurrent.ScheduledExecutorService.scheduleAtFixedRate` and, as stated by Javadoc:

> The task is explicitly cancelled via the returned future.
> The executor terminates, also resulting in task cancellation.
> An execution of the task throws an exception. In this case calling get on the returned future will throw ExecutionException, holding the exception as its cause.
> Subsequent executions are suppressed. Subsequent calls to isDone() on the returned future will return true.

Probably a try catch in method `io.stackgres.operator.app.ReconciliationClockImpl.reconcile` with proper logging of error will solve the problem.

[xaviersierra]: In order to confirm if there is a continious action of the operator over the 
  SGCluser, I've repeated the experiment annotating the SGCluster with the 
  annotation "stackgres.io/reconciliation-pause=true" just after the test 
  annotation is applied to all resources. 

I haven't found any big difference in the performance impact. Without the 
  "stackgres.io/reconciliation-pause=true" annotation the performance loss 
  was ~50% whereas with the annotation the performance loss was ~52%. 

With this results we can discard that there is no continous action of the 
  operator over SGCluster at least in the 1.0.0-beta2 version. 

After inspected a Patroni's logs from SGClusters, I've a detected a message that 
  only appears in the SGCluster with the configured annotation, the message has 
  the following form:

```
2021-07-27 11:21:35,246 INFO: acquired session lock as a leader
```

Which sugest that Patroni is loosing the lock after the configured annotation 
  has been applied.

[xaviersierra]: Since Patroni stores its lock information in the metadata information of a Endpoint that have the same 
  name as the cluster. It's possible that the cause of the lock loss happen when the operator 
  applies the "test" annotation to the Endpoints resource. 

In order to be sure that the loss of the lock it's the cause of the performance
  degradation, I've reproduced the error without using the operator. To do that, 
  instead of using the operator API to add the annotation, I've reproduced an 
  equivalent patch of what the operator does over the Endpoints resource. 

Such patch would be the following: 

``` sh
kubectl patch endpoints "test" -n "availability" --type='json' \
    -p='[
      {"op": "add", "path": "/metadata/annotations/test", "value": "test"},
      {"op": "remove", "path": "/metadata/annotations/acquireTime"},
      {"op": "remove", "path": "/metadata/annotations/leader"},
      {"op": "remove", "path": "/metadata/annotations/renewTime"},
      {"op": "remove", "path": "/metadata/annotations/transitions"},
      {"op": "remove", "path": "/metadata/annotations/ttl"},
      {"op": "remove", "path": "/subsets"}
      ]'
```

The reasons behind this are detailed [here](https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/issues/1207#what-happens-if-the-server-side-apply-feature-gate-its-disabled).

[gelias]: @teoincontatto the math to calculate the maximum size of the names is:

The Template of the label is: $NAME-$OPERATION_NAME-$UUID_IN_HEX-$OPERATION_SEQUENCE_NUMBER

Generated label example `updatePostgresPrimary-minorVersionUpgrade-c43158866d5646d7-1`

- $OPERATION_NAME: The most largest operation size found was (minorVersionUpgrade): 19 characters 
- $UUID_IN_HEX: The most significant number from UUID in hex generation will always has 16 characters (e.g.: c43158866d5646d7)
- $OPERATION_SEQUENCE_NUMBER: 10 characters ( Max integer size - 2147483647)
- $NAME = Auto generated chars (19 + 16 + 10) + 3 hyphens - 63( limit size of a label) = **15 characters**

**The restriction of the name should be only 15 characters!**

Issue:

# Problem to solve

Reconciliation cycle uses the synchronized method `io.stackgres.operator.conciliation.StackGresReconciliator.reconcile` that is called by watchers and scheduler (each 10 seconds). Issue:
Change SGPoolingConfig to improve pgbouncer.ini section
The `SGPoolingConfig` CRD declares the section `pgbouncer.ini` but we have `databases` and `users` sections that are sibling of the former, this might create confusion since in the `pgbouncer.ini` file sections are defined like following:

```
[pgbouncer]
pool_mode = session
listen_port = 6432
listen_addr = localhost
auth_type = md5

[databases]
template1 = host=localhost dbname=template1 auth_user=someuser

[users]
user1 = pool_mode=transaction max_user_connections=50
```

To better represent the actual `pgbouncer.ini` file structure we propose to change the `SGPoolingConfig` CRD like following:

```yaml
spec:
  pgBouncer:
    pgbouncer.ini:
      pgbouncer:
        max_client_conn: '2000'
        default_pool_size: '50'
      databases:
        foodb:
          pool_size: '20'
          dbname: 'bardb'
      users:
        user1:
          pool_mode: transaction
          max_user_connections: '50'
```

The section in the INI file is called just `[pgbouncer]`, so nesting into section `pgbouncer` the current `pgbouncer.ini` section makes sense.

The change will affect the current conversion webhook from/to `stackgres.io/v1beta1` to/from `stackgres.io/v1`.

[DISCUSSION]
[ahachete]: While there's a possibility of confusion, I believe it is widely understood that YAML files, specially if they are proper CRDs, may have opted to YAML-ize configuration files in other formats, without expecting to have them verbatim included in the CRD.

And we have proper documentation about the format, I'm unsure about this change. The goal is to be able to distinguish among potentially many different configuration files (e.g. in PgBouncer, we may want to also let the user configure via the CRD `userlist.txt`, which is a separate file).

Furthermore, the current naming is consistent with that of using `postgresql.conf` in [`SGPgConfig`](https://stackgres.io/doc/latest/reference/crd/sgpgconfig/) --or else, if we change one, we should change both.

[teoincontatto]: Maybe another approach would be to refactor the current structure as a sub-structure of `pgbouncer.ini` as for `postgresql.conf` in `SGPostgresConfig` but with an additional level since the latter does not define sections. This is an example of my proposal:

```yaml
spec:
  pgBouncer:
    pgbouncer.ini:
      pgbouncer: # <- .spec.pgBouncer.pgbouncer\.ini
        max_client_conn: '2000'
        default_pool_size: '50'
      databases: # <- .spec.pgBouncer.databases
        foodb:
          pool_size: 20
          dbname: 'bardb'
      users: # <- .spec.pgBouncer.users
        user1:
          pool_mode: transaction
          max_user_connections: 50
```

[jorsol]: It makes sense to refactor the structure as a sub-structure of `pgbouncer.ini`, this way we could probably later add `userlist.txt` and/or `pg_hba.conf`.

Issue:
Allow specifying Service Type for SG cluster services and allow to add custom annotations
### Problem to solve

The current StackGres configuration creates services for the database cluster as `ClusterIP` with no option to change it. Also for some Cloud providers, there are some options available through adding some custom `annotations`. i.e from GKE `cloud.google.com/load-balancer-type: "Internal"` to set an internal LoadBalancer.

### Proposal

Allow through the configuration to change:

- Service type for StackGres Cluster
- Add custom `annotations` to services. 

### Links / references

https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/internal-load-balancing

[DISCUSSION]
[ahachete]: I propose to add this to the `SGCluster` CRD, adding a top-level section called `services`:

```yaml
  postgresServices:
    - primary:
      enabled: <boolean> # default true
      type: <enum: values ClusterIP|LoadBalancer> # default ClusterIP
      annotations: <array, optional>
    - replicas:
      enabled: <boolean> # default true
      type: <enum: values ClusterIP|LoadBalancer> # default ClusterIP
      annotations: <array, optional>
```

Open for ~Discussion.

[xaviersierra]: Why allow to disable the postgres services? Whitout them is really hard to connect to the DB

[ahachete]: I don't see a clear use case where you might want to disable the `primary` service. But who knows, maybe someone just wants to `kubectl exec...`. But for the `replicas` you might want to do that if you only want `rw` connections.

In any case, I believe we might want to provide this degree of flexibility. Still, users may expose the services how they want, manually, at any time.

[xaviersierra]: I believe we should treat the primary and replica as objetecs that are part of the postgresServices object, instead of an array of objects. Leaving it as array, introduce a bigger surface of user errors that we will need to validate.

[ahachete]: Yes, agreed.

[ahachete]: I have been reviewing this, and other related issues, like #179. And I have come to the following conclusions:

* We might want to treat `labels` and `annotations` differently ([quick refresher on the differences between them](https://vsupalov.com/kubernetes-labels-annotations-difference/)).
* In particular, there's value in providing additional user-supplied `labels` to the pods (for example, for node placement or to prevent injection of sidecars). However, the use of `annotations` can be more widespread, and could be interesting, for example, and as illustrated by this issue, for the services generated.
* Following-up with the above, we might want to extend support for user-supplied (additional) annotations to, potentially, every object created by StackGres (`SGCluster`).

Based on this, I'd like to propose the following changes:

* Remove the `SGCluster.spec.pods.metadata.annotations` object (or at least mark it for deprecation).
* Add an specific sub-object for supporting annotations with some degree of flexibility. Proposed spec (to add) to `SGCluster`:

```yaml
spec:
  metadata:
    annotations:
      allResources:
        - key1: value1
        - key2: value2
      pods:
        - key3: value3
        - key4: value4
      services:
        - key5: value5
        - key6: value6
```

In the future, we might add more fields to the above, with specific annotations that would only apply to any given kind of resource (e.g. a `StatefulSet`). But I believe, with the above, is good enough for now.

It might be argued, then, that the whole ecosystem of annotations to generate is not completely described by the above section, as there may also be annotations added to the Postgres services, as per [the above spec](https://gitlab.com/ongresinc/stackgres/-/issues/527#note_369947056). This is true, and should be clearly documented, but Postgres service annotations make a lot of sense to be enclosed within the `postgresServices` object, as they might be tightly coupled with the `type` field.

To make it clear, with the spec above, and adding an annotation `key7: value7` to the `postgresServices.primary.annotations` field, the following annotations would be propagated:
* pods: `key1, key2, key3, key4`
* primary service: `key1, key2, key5, key6, key7`
* other services: `key1, key2, key5, key6`
* every other resource created when a `SGCluster` is created: `key1, key2`.

Implement CRDs upgrades
Since Helm doesn't provide any mechanism to upgrade CRD. We've decided that the operator will handle CRD upgrade. 

For this purpose, we need to move CRD inside the operator's classpath. So the operator can install them, but also upgrade them if it needed.

To avoid such situation the `/read-only` endpoint of Patroni REST API could be used to make sure the initialization has completed too and the node is Ready to be exposed:

> GET /replica: replica health check endpoint. It returns HTTP status code 200 only when the Patroni node is in the state running, the role is replica and noloadbalance tag is not set.
